# Pauta 6.1.0: every rule

> 405 rules from https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/, published 2026-11-14. Each page's prose, screenshots and mockups are on
> the page itself (as Markdown at the page's address with `.md` for the trailing `/`); this file holds the rules alone.

## Using Pauta

**Starting a new app:** create it from the GitHub template repository
https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template (`gh repo create <name> --template
adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template`, or **Use this template** on GitHub), then run `scripts/rename.sh <AppName>
<package>`. It is built to the edition its README and AGENTS.md name; audit it against this edition and add what is
missing.

**Building a feature:** read its page first (`<page>.md`, below, has the prose, the rules and the spec tables), then
copy from the code each rule's *Reference* names. Editora is the reference implementation.

**Auditing an app:** the full procedure is the pauta-audit skill, https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/skills/pauta-audit/SKILL.md. It decides how to audit and how
to write the report; an edition supplies only its rules. In short:

1. Find the edition the app implements: `pauta.version` in its `pom.xml`, or failing that its README. Read that
   edition's rules at `https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/rules.json`. If the app names none, ask which edition to audit against and offer
   the newest; with no one to ask, use the newest and say so in the report. Editions before 2.0.0 serve no
   rules.json: audit against 2.0.0 or newer, and report a failed rule that the app's own edition didn't have as
   upgrade work.
2. Take each rule in turn. *Check (code)*: when it has a *Command* (`check.command`), run it with `sh -c` from the
   app's repository root. Exit 0: the check passes; still read the rest of the rule and cite the file:line that meets
   it. Any other exit: the check fails, and what it printed is the evidence. Otherwise read or search the source as the
   check says: a search written inside the check's text lists lines to judge, and its exit code is no verdict; a
   check that names a test as "the surest evidence" passes on the behavior without it. *Check (test)*: the
   statement requires a test; find it, or the app's equivalent, and confirm the build runs it.
   *Check (by hand)*: the source can't confirm it; report it as manual, unless the source plainly shows it unmet,
   which is `fail`. A check that needs the website's repository or a repository setting says so: read it if you
   can reach it, and report `not-checked` if you can't. Some names in a rule's statement are required as
   written: a command id, a catalog key, a chord, a command-line flag, an environment variable, a property in
   pom.xml or pauta.json, and a file the repository must carry (a document at its root, or a resource or tool
   configuration the rule names: emacs.json, jreleaser.yml). A platform API the rule names (javafx.stage.Popup,
   SystemTray, Future.get()) is the requirement itself. Any other name (a class, method or constant of the app's
   own code, a CSS file or style class, a branch or workflow file, a file the app writes as it runs), and every name only a
   Check or Reference gives, is Editora's spelling, and the app's equivalent meets it.
3. A rule applies to every app unless it is limited: its text names the apps it covers ("An app with user
   documents…"), its page or section opens with an **Applies to** line (`appliesTo` in rules.json), or it details a
   rule that is limited. A limited rule the app is outside of is `limited` and needs no exception.
4. Read the app's `src/main/resources/com/<app>/pauta.json`, its recorded exceptions. An unmet rule it lists gets the
   entry's kind as its status (not-applicable, deviation, pending, or in a template app-only); MAYs need no entry.
   An unmet MUST or SHOULD it doesn't list is `fail`; so is an unmet MAY, which has no consequence. An entry for a
   rule that passes or is limited, and a deviation or pending entry with no link, are problems to report. A by-hand
   rule it lists as an exception gets that kind, not `manual`. Its `checked` list, which an app may keep or
   not, records the by-hand rules a person checked and found met (PAUTA-18): a `manual` result carries its entry,
   one with none is reported as not recorded, which is not a failure, and an entry older than the rule's
   `changed` is stale, a problem.
5. Report one result per rule: ID, level, status and evidence as `file:line`. The statuses: `fail`, `manual`, `not-checked`, `pending`, `deviation`, `not-applicable`, `app-only`, `limited`, `pass`. As JSON, the report follows https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/audit.schema.json. A failed MUST blocks a release; a
   `manual` or `not-checked` one does not.

Cite a rule by its ID and edition, for example "KBD-07 (Pauta 6.1.0)". Each rule's address is the page's plus
`#` and the ID in lowercase: `https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-07`.

Levels: **MUST**: A release blocker for a new app. **SHOULD**: Expected unless the app has a stated reason. **MAY**: A pattern worth copying when the app grows into it.

## Same on every OS (OS)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/: The one list of places where Windows, macOS and Linux may differ, and the rules that keep everything else the same.

### Rules

- **OS-01 · MUST.** Every command, setting and window exists on Windows, macOS and Linux, with the same default. Where
  the OS can't do what one asks, it stays where it is, disabled, and says why; it is never hidden. The only
  exceptions are the rows of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins), on the page Same on
  every OS: the places where the app hands work to the OS or sits in the OS's own interface, such as the macOS
  application menu and the macOS form of a keymap's chords.
  - *Why:* a user who moves to another OS looks for a feature where they left it. A missing row looks like a
    different app; a disabled one with a reason explains itself.
  - *Check (code):* no command, menu row or settings row is registered or added inside an OS check, and no default
    in the settings model depends on the OS, unless a row of the table under
    [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins) gives that difference: the rows of the macOS application
    menu, a default chord in its macOS form. An OS check is a test whose answer can differ among Windows, macOS
    and Linux; a gate that holds on all three alike (a command registered only when the app finds its own
    launcher, whatever the OS) is not one. A row the OS can't serve calls `setDisable` and carries its reason
    ([KBD-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-04) for a command).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java) (the extended-window row, disabled on macOS
    "rather than hidden, so its note still explains why"). Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: its
    `file.saveAsAdmin` command ([`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)) is registered with nothing that disables it on
    Windows, where it can do nothing. Termina removes its `hideMenuBar` command on macOS ([`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)).

- **OS-02 · MUST.** In an app's code, one class answers which OS the app runs on (this guide calls it `Os`, with
  `isWindows()`, `isMac()` and `isLinux()`; the names are the app's own), and no other class reads the `os.name`
  property. A class that only shows the OS's name, in About or a problem report, asks that one class for it.
  - *Why:* checks scattered through the code are how apps drift apart on one OS without anyone choosing it. In one
    class, every difference can be found with one search, and a test can run the app as any OS
    ([OS-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#os-03)).
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java` lists one file, the `Os` class, and no other file works out
    the OS for itself. The Command also lists the files that compare `File.separatorChar` or `File.pathSeparatorChar`
    with a character (`File.separatorChar == '\\'` for "is this Windows"), the other way Editora does it. A class that
    only prints the name, in About or a problem report, reads the property too, so it is listed. A grep finds only
    the spellings it is given: when the Command passes, still read for a test that stands in for the OS some other
    way, such as a separator compared as a string or an environment variable only one OS sets.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; n=$(grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java | wc -l); s=$(grep -rlE "eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java | wc -l); u=$(grep -rlE "\"os[.]name\"|eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 1 ] && [ "$u" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$n files read os.name (one Os class should):"; grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java; echo "$s files compare a file or path separator with a character (only that class may):"; grep -rlE "eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java; false; }`
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java), the one class that reads `os.name` (`current`, `isWindows`, `isMac`,
    `isLinux`, and `description` for About and a problem report); the Command passes on it. Each of the six apps
    reads `os.name` in several classes, Editora in about fifty, and eleven of
    Editora's classes tell Windows apart by a separator, eight of them without reading `os.name`
    ([`lsp/JavaRuntimes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/lsp/JavaRuntimes.java),
    [`dap/DapManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/DapManager.java),
    [`dap/InstalledAdapter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/InstalledAdapter.java)). Editora's
    [`process/DesktopActions.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/DesktopActions.java) has the `Os` enum to start from.

- **OS-03 · SHOULD.** An app's tests can run as any OS: the one class that answers which OS the app runs on
  ([OS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#os-02); this guide calls it `Os`) takes an override, and one test asserts that the command ids, the menu
  bar's rows and the settings pages are the same for Windows, macOS and Linux.
  - *Why:* CI runs the FX tests on one or two OSes ([REL-20](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-20)); with the override, the
    comparison runs on every pull request on Linux alone.
  - *Check (test):* a test sets each OS in turn through the override and compares the three lists.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java) (`override`, and the `exampleapp.os` property) and
    [`SameOnEveryOsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SameOnEveryOsFxTest.java) (`theCommandsTheMenusAndSettingsAreTheSameOnEveryOs`), which starts the app as each OS and compares
    the command ids, the menu bar's rows and every Settings page's rows. Editora's [`KeymapsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/command/KeymapsTest.java)
    (`guiKeymapsBindSameCommandSetOnBothPlatforms`) does it for the keymaps.

- **OS-04 · MUST.** No behavior or layout of an app differs by OS: what a command, a key or a click does, where a
  control sits and how a window is drawn are the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. The only exceptions are the rows
  of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins), on the page Same on every OS: the places
  where the app hands work to the OS or sits in the OS's own interface, such as the macOS form of a keymap's chords,
  the system menu bar, the OS's file dialogs, trash, tray and notifications, and the shells a terminal offers.
  Whether a command, setting or window exists, and its default, is [OS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#os-01).
  - *Why:* a feature can be on every OS and still act or sit differently on one: Escape that closes the window on
    Linux only, a title on the left on Windows only. Each is something to relearn on the next machine, which is
    what the family exists to spare its users.
  - *Check (code):* list every place the code tests the OS. They are the callers of the methods of the class
    [OS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#os-02) asks for and, in an app that has no such class yet, every file OS-02's Command prints (the files
    that read `os.name`, and the files that compare `File.separatorChar` or `File.pathSeparatorChar` with a
    character), together with the callers of whatever those files offer other classes to ask the OS by: a method
    (Editora's `KeymapManager.isMac()`, which ten files call and eight of them read no `os.name` themselves) or a
    constant. `grep -rnE 'isMac|isWindows|isLinux' src/main/java` lists the usual names; read the printed files for
    the app's own. Read each place. It passes when what it changes is what a row of the table under
    [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins) gives that OS, or is nothing a user can see or do (the path
    of a binary, a process's arguments, a line ending). It fails when it changes anything else a user can see or
    do: what a command, a key or a click does, where something sits, how it is drawn or what it says. A place
    that gives an OS something other than what its row gives is judged by the rule that row links, where that
    rule covers it: a Windows notification raised as the tray's balloon and not a toast fails
    [TRAY-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tray-and-background/#tray-09), not this rule. It fails this rule when the row links no rule, or
    the rule it links does not cover the difference (a menu bar on one OS and a menu button on the others).
  - *Reference:* the app template, read through: every place it tests the OS calls its [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java), and each is
    on a row or changes nothing a user sees: the macOS form of the keymap's chords (`Keymap`, `KeyDispatcher`,
    `AppServices`, and the pickers' keys that `MainWindow` hands `PickerKeys`), the system menu bar and its
    application menu (`MainWindow`, `Chrome`, `MacAppMenu`), and a program's path, arguments and `PATH`
    (`Executables`, `Browser`, `ShellPath`). No other app has been read through for it yet. The
    differences found so far, each on no row or short of its row: Mirada
    closes its window on Escape on Linux only ([`Command.escapeCloses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Command.java)), follows the OS's accent color on macOS and
    Windows only ([`Theme.followsAccent`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Theme.java)), puts its title on the left on Windows only ([`TitleBar.Layout`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)) and has a
    menu bar on macOS only ([`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)); Editora deletes a file for good on Windows ([`io/Trash.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/io/Trash.java)),
    keeps the user's key bindings apart by OS (`keybindings` and `keybindingsMac` in [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java)) and
    registers its WSL targets on Windows only ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)); Termina believes the folder a shell reports for itself on
    Windows only ([`ProcessCwd.reportedDirectoryWins`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/pty/ProcessCwd.java)), and its Settings Sync keeps the user's key bindings in one
    file for macOS and another for Windows and Linux ([`sync/KeybindingsFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/KeybindingsFile.java)). On a row, and passing: a click that takes `Cmd` on macOS
    and `Ctrl` elsewhere (Editora's [`editor/EditorBuffer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/EditorBuffer.java), Termina's [`link/LinkGesture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/link/LinkGesture.java)), and the
    profiles Termina lists on Windows only, Command Prompt, PowerShell, Git Bash and the WSL distributions
    ([`shell/ShellDiscovery.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/shell/ShellDiscovery.java)).

## Conformance (PAUTA)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/: How an app says which edition of Pauta it implements and how fully it conforms, and how it records the rules it does not meet: not applicable, a deliberate deviation, or work still pending.

### Complete, Core and Partial

- **PAUTA-01 · MUST.** Every app implements Pauta: it names one edition (the `pauta.version` of
  [ABOUT-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-08)) and states its conformance as [Complete, Core or Partial](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#complete-core-and-partial): Complete meets every MUST and
  every SHOULD (met, not applicable or a recorded deviation), Core every MUST with SHOULDs still pending, Partial not
  yet every MUST.
  - *Why:* an app that is in the family answers to these rules; saying which ones, and how far, is the first of them.
  - *Check (code):* `pom.xml` defines `pauta.version` and `src/main/resources/com/<app>/pauta.json` exists.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; { grep -q '<pauta.version>' pom.xml || { echo 'no pauta.version in pom.xml'; false; }; } && { find src/main/resources -path '*/com/*' -name pauta.json | grep . || { echo 'no pauta.json'; false; }; }`
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) (`pauta.version`) and [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json).

- **PAUTA-02 · MUST.** An app's conformance is computed, never stored: one pure helper reads the exceptions and returns Partial
  when any MUST is pending, Core when any SHOULD is pending, and Complete otherwise. Nothing else enters it: the
  `checked` list ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)) is a record, and a by-hand rule with no entry there leaves the result as
  it is. About, the Pauta window and the docs page take it from there; the README's badge and line
  ([PAUTA-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-15)), which can't call the helper, are held to it by a test.
  - *Why:* [*One source of truth for each fact*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-building-them). A conformance typed
    in by hand stays "Complete" after a pending exception is added.
  - *Check (code):* one helper returns the conformance (the template's `PautaConformance.of`): it is handed the
    exceptions and nothing of the `checked` list, returns Partial for a pending MUST, Core for a pending SHOULD
    and Complete otherwise, and deviation, not-applicable and app-only entries leave its result alone. About and
    the Pauta window call it, and nothing in the app's code stores a conformance. A test fails when the README's badge
    or line names another conformance than the helper returns: the statement requires that one. A unit test of
    the helper that covers all three results is the surest evidence for the rest. That the docs page shows the
    same conformance is read with the page itself, in the website's repository ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-13)).
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/PautaConformance.java) (`of`, which takes the exceptions alone, and `conformance`), tested by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java),
    whose `theReadmeNamesTheEditionAndTheConformanceAndLinksTheDocsPage` holds the README and whose
    `deviationsAppOnlyAndNotApplicableEntriesAndMaysLeaveTheConformanceAlone` covers the entries that leave it alone.

- **PAUTA-03 · MUST.** A new app, one that has made no release yet, makes its first release at Core or Complete:
  the [New app checklist](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/checklist/)'s MUSTs are release blockers, and recording one as pending does not lift
  that. An app with a release behind it is not covered: it may be at Partial, and says so
  ([Complete, Core and Partial](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#complete-core-and-partial)). A template repository is never released as an app,
  so this rule is for the app made from it and the template records no entry for it.
  - *Check (by hand):* in an app with no release yet (no numbered section in its `CHANGELOG.md`, no version tag),
    the About window of the build to be released says Core or Complete. An app that has released, and a template,
    are outside the rule.
  - *Reference:* no app yet.

### Exceptions

- **PAUTA-04 · MUST.** Every MUST and SHOULD of the edition that the app does not meet has an exception, and every
  exception names a rule the app does not meet. An unmet rule with no entry is a failed audit, not an exception; an
  entry for a rule the app now meets is removed in the same change that meets it. A rule checked by hand counts like
  any other once a person has checked it in the running app: found unmet, it gets an exception; found met, a
  `checked` entry ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)). Until then it has neither, and that is not a failed audit: the audit
  reports it as `manual`, not recorded.
  - *Why:* [*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps). The list is the app's
    claim; it has to be whole and current.
  - *Check (code):* the audit of the app against its edition ([Coding agents and LLMs](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/coding-agents/#audit-an-app))
    is this check, so the audit judges this rule last, from its other results: no MUST or SHOULD is `fail`, and no
    result reports an entry for a rule that passes. The evidence names the rules that fail. A
    `manual` result with no `checked` entry is reported as not recorded (PAUTA-18), and a `not-checked` one as
    out of the audit's reach: neither is a failure of the app, and neither fails this check. An audit of part of
    the edition judges it from the rules in its scope and says so.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json), the only list of exceptions so far, beside the audit report that shows it whole:
    [`docs/pauta-audit.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.json) and [`docs/pauta-audit.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.md), where
    no MUST or SHOULD fails and its nine `app-only` entries are the only exceptions.

- **PAUTA-05 · MUST.** A rule limited to apps with a feature needs no entry in an app without that feature. A rule is
  limited when its own text says so ("An app that stores a secret…"), when its page or
  section opens with an **Applies to** line (the [Tray and background](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tray-and-background/) page; `appliesTo` in
  `rules.json`), or when it details a rule that is limited (WELC-03 onward detail the Welcome page of [WELC-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/#welc-01)).
  Nothing else limits a rule: a scope is read from one of the three, never inferred from what the app lacks.
  `not-applicable` is for a rule that reads as applying to every app.
  - *Check (code):* no `not-applicable` entry names a rule whose text, page, section or parent rule already limits
    it.
  - *Reference:* the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has no `not-applicable` entry, so it meets the
    rule with nothing to hold; the six apps have no `pauta.json`.

- **PAUTA-06 · MUST.** A `deviation` is a choice, not a gap, and only a SHOULD can have one: a SHOULD is expected
  unless the app has a stated reason, and the deviation is that reason. It links a decision record in
  `docs/decisions/` ([DOCS-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-13)) that gives the context, what the app does instead, and what
  it costs. A MUST the app does not meet is `pending`, as is any work it has not done yet.
  - *Why:* a deviation keeps the conformance; a deviation from a MUST, or missing work called a deviation, would let
    the app say it is built to an edition it does not meet.
  - *Check (code):* every `deviation` entry names a SHOULD, and its `link` opens a file under `docs/decisions/` that
    names the rule's ID.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`).

- **PAUTA-07 · MUST.** A `pending` exception links an open issue in the app's own repository that names the rule's
  ID and edition, "MENU-15 (Pauta x.y.z)". One issue may hold several rules, one per page for example, if it names
  each one that way. Closing the issue removes its entries.
  - *Check (code):* every `pending` entry's `link` is an issue URL in the app's own repository; the source settles
    that much, and a link that is not one fails the rule. That the issue is open and names the entry's rule ID and
    edition is read from the issue itself (`gh issue view <number>`), which is on GitHub and not in the checkout.
    An audit that cannot read the issues reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it. With no
    `pending` entry there is nothing to read, and the rule is met.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`), which fails a pending link that is not an issue in the app's repository or the template's.
    The template has no `pending` entry left, so it meets the rule with nothing to read.

- **PAUTA-08 · MUST.** Each exception's `reason` is one plain sentence for the person using the app, in English like
  the changelog: what is different and, for a deviation, what they get instead. No rule text, no class names.
  - *Check (by hand):* read each reason in the Pauta window as a user would. The source settles two cases: a
    reason that runs to more than one sentence, or carries rule text or a class name, fails the rule, and with no
    exception there is no reason to read and the rule is met.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`: a reason ends with a period and names no rule ID).

- **PAUTA-16 · MUST.** A template repository, one that new apps are made from, sets `"template": true` in its
  `pauta.json` and records as `app-only` the rules that only an app made from it can meet. `app-only` leaves the
  conformance as it is, like `not-applicable`, and nothing but a template may use it. Making an app from the
  template sets `template` to `false`. From then on the app's everyday build passes but lists what it inherited:
  each `app-only` entry and each `pending` link to another repository. Its release build fails until each one is
  met, or recorded as `pending` with an issue in the app's own repository. An app that was not made from a
  template inherits nothing, and the rule asks nothing of it.
  - *Why:* a template can't have the website or screenshots of an app that doesn't exist yet, and an app must not
    inherit its template's issues as its own. A build that failed the moment the app was made would fail its first
    step; the release is where it has to be settled ([PAUTA-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-03)).
  - *Check (code):* in a template, `pauta.json` has `"template": true` and the script that makes an app from it
    sets it to `false`. Outside a template, an `app-only` entry or a `pending` link to another repository is what
    a template left behind: the test of [PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-10) lists each one in the everyday build, and the
    release build runs it with them treated as failures, so no released app keeps an `app-only` entry. An app
    whose `pauta.json` has no `template` field, no `app-only` entry and no `pending` link to another repository,
    or that has no `pauta.json`, shows nothing inherited from a template: it is outside the rule, and an audit
    reports it as `limited`.
  - *Reference:* the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template): its [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has `"template": true` and nine `app-only`
    entries, its [`scripts/rename.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/scripts/rename.sh) sets `"template": false`, and its
    [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) holds both (`onlyATemplateRecordsWhatOnlyAnAppCanMeet`) and, outside a template, lists the
    `app-only` entries and the `pending` links to another repository in every build and fails on them when the
    `dist` profile sets `pauta.release` (`theAppListsWhatItInherited`; [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml)). No app has been made
    from it yet.

- **PAUTA-18 · MUST.** `pauta.json`'s `checked` list is the record of the rules checked by hand, and this rule
  governs only the entries an app chooses to record: each one is well formed and not stale. An app that records
  none, with no `checked` list or an empty one, meets it. An entry is there
  only because a person checked the rule in the running app and found it met, and it holds the `rule`, the `edition`
  it was checked against and the `date`, and may hold the app's `version`, for a rule that is checked again with
  each release (the screen-reader pass of [ACC-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/accessibility/#acc-07)): the audit reports it, and nothing
  expires by it. It says the rule was met when it was checked, not that the app still meets
  it. A rule found unmet gets an exception instead ([PAUTA-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-04)), never both. A by-hand rule with no entry
  has not been recorded as checked: it needs no exception and no issue, it does not change the computed conformance
  ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-02)), and it does not fail this rule. The audit reports it as not recorded, so its report
  still says which by-hand rules nobody has recorded. An entry is stale when its `edition` is older
  than the rule's `changed` in the edition's `rules.json`, the edition in which the rule's level, scope or statement
  last changed, and only then: the app's test fails it ([PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-10)) until it is removed and the rule
  checked again.
  - *Why:* an audit can only answer `manual` for these rules, and its report is written again each time. Without a
    record, a rule someone checked last week and a rule nobody ever looked at read the same. The record stays out
    of the conformance because nothing in the code tells an unchecked rule from a met one: counting it would make
    an app record as pending what it may well meet.
  - *Check (code):* every `checked` entry has a `rule`, an `edition` and a `date`; the rule is one of the edition's
    whose check is by hand (`check.kind` in `rules.json`); the edition is no older than the rule's `changed`
    (one newer than `pauta.version`, and a rule listed twice, are for the test of [PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-10) to fail);
    and no rule has an exception as well. With no `checked` list, or an empty one, there is no entry to fail and the
    rule is met: the audit's `manual` results say which by-hand rules are not recorded, and that is no failure of
    this rule. That a person looked is the entry's own claim, which the code can't show.
  - *Reference:* no app records a by-hand check yet, so each meets the rule with nothing to hold: the
    [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has no `checked` list, though its [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) would hold one
    (`eachCheckedEntryIsWellFormedAndCurrent`), and the six apps have no `pauta.json`.

### The file

- **PAUTA-09 · MUST.** An app's exceptions and its record of by-hand checks have one source: `pauta.json`, bundled
  with the app's resources (`src/main/resources/com/<app>/pauta.json`) and laid out as [The file](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#the-file) shows.
  Its `exceptions` list has `rule`, `level`, `url`, `kind` and `reason` on every entry, `link` on every deviation and
  pending entry, and one entry per rule. Its `checked` list is the app's to keep or not: an app that records no
  by-hand check leaves it out or empty, and what an entry of it holds is [PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)'s. `"template": true`
  stands beside the two lists only in a template repository (PAUTA-16).
  - *Check (code):* `pauta.json` is among the app's bundled resources, under `src/main/resources/`; each exception has
    the fields its kind needs and no rule has two. The entries of the `checked` list are [PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)'s to
    judge, and a file with no `checked` list passes.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json), read by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`parsesEveryField`, `everyEntryNamesARuleOfTheEditionWithItsLevelAndAddress`).
    The file has no `checked` list, which the rule allows.

- **PAUTA-10 · MUST.** A test reads `pauta.json` against a copy of the edition's `rules.json` in
  `src/test/resources/pauta-rules.json` and fails when the copy's `edition` is not `pauta.version`, when an entry
  names a rule the edition does not have, when its `level` or `url` differs from the edition's, when a rule appears
  twice, when a deviation names a MUST, when a deviation or pending entry has no `link`, or when a `checked` entry
  ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)) names a rule that is not checked by hand, a rule listed twice, a rule with an exception,
  an edition newer than `pauta.version`, or an edition older than the rule's `changed`, which makes the entry
  stale. Outside a template, it reports each `app-only` entry and each `pending` link that is not
  an issue in the app's own repository (the one the app's own code names; `AppInfo.GITHUB_REPO` in the template),
  and fails on them in the release build ([PAUTA-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-16)).
  - *Why:* moving to a newer edition changes levels, retires IDs and changes rules a person checked by hand; the
    test turns each stale entry into a failure.
  - *Check (test):* `PautaConformanceTest`, or the app's equivalent, runs in the build and has a case for each
    failure the rule lists.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) and its copy of the edition's rules, [`pauta-rules.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/resources/pauta-rules.json). It has a case
    for each failure: `theRulesCopyIsTheEditionThePomNames`, `everyEntryNamesARuleOfTheEditionWithItsLevelAndAddress`
    (an unknown rule, a level or `url` that differs, a rule twice), `eachKindHasWhatItNeeds` (a deviation on a MUST,
    a missing `link`), `eachCheckedEntryIsWellFormedAndCurrent` (the `checked` list) and `theAppListsWhatItInherited`
    (what a template left, failed when `pauta.release` is set).

- **PAUTA-11 · SHOULD.** Moving to a newer edition is one change: replace `pauta-rules.json` with the new edition's,
  and the app's copy of the audit skill where it keeps one (the app template's is
  `.claude/skills/pauta-audit/SKILL.md`); remove the `checked` entries the new `rules.json` makes stale
  ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)) and check those rules again; run the audit again and update `pauta.json`; then change
  `pauta.version`, the README and `AGENTS.md` together.
  - *Why:* each of these names or follows the edition. The test fails a `pauta-rules.json` or a `checked` entry left
    behind (PAUTA-10); nothing fails a skill copy left behind, which then audits the new rules by the old procedure.
  - *Check (by hand):* the change that raises `pauta.version` also replaces `pauta-rules.json` and the skill copy,
    where the app keeps one, leaves no `checked` entry older than its rule's `changed`, and touches `pauta.json`
    where the audit found something new.
  - *Reference:* [Move an app to a newer edition](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/coding-agents/#move-an-app-to-a-newer-edition).

### Where it shows

- **PAUTA-13 · MUST.** In the user docs: the app's website has a *Pauta conformance* page under `/docs/`
  ([DOCS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-02)) with the edition, the conformance and every exception, grouped by kind, each with
  its rule ID linked to the edition's rule, its reason and its link. The Pauta window's link to it is
  [PWIN-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/pauta-window/#pwin-07).
  - *Check (code):* the app names a website for its user docs ([DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-01)): an app
    whose repository and About name none has nowhere to carry the page, and fails the rule from the app's
    checkout. The rest is in the website's repository (`<app>-website`, [DOCS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-02)):
    its docs (the files of `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) have the page, and the page gives the edition
    `pauta.version` names, the conformance the app's exceptions give, and every exception of the app's
    `pauta.json` under its kind, each with its rule ID linked to the edition's rule, its reason and its link. A
    page that lists other rules than the file fails. With no `pauta.json`, which is
    [PAUTA-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-01)'s and [PAUTA-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-09)'s failure, there is no list to compare, and the page is
    judged on being there with the edition. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as
    `not-checked` and says what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* no app yet.

- **PAUTA-14 · SHOULD.** The website's *Pauta conformance* page ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-13)) is generated from the
  app's `pauta.json`, like the Commands page ([DOCS-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-04)), so it cannot list a different
  set from the app.
  - *Check (code):* the app's website repository has a generator that reads the app's `pauta.json` (beside the
    others in `scripts/`, in editora-website's layout), and its output is committed. An app that names no website
    has no page to generate: the rule fails with [PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-13). An audit run from the app's checkout
    alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* no app yet; editora-website's [`scripts/GenCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenCommands.java) is the pattern.

- **PAUTA-15 · MUST.** An app's README shows its conformance: the README's Pauta badge
  ([README badges](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#readme-badges-in-this-order)) and its "Built to" line (at Partial, "Working
  toward") name the edition and the conformance, and both link to the website's *Pauta conformance* page
  ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-13)). The edition is the one `pauta.version` names ([ABOUT-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-08)),
  and the conformance the one the app computes ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-02)).
  - *Check (code):* `README.md` has the badge and the line; each names the edition `pauta.version` names and the
    conformance the app's exceptions give (Partial with a pending MUST, Core with a pending SHOULD, else
    Complete), the line opens "Working toward" at Partial and "Built to" otherwise, and both link the app's
    conformance page under its website's `/docs/`. A test that asserts it (the template's
    `theReadmeNamesTheEditionAndTheConformanceAndLinksTheDocsPage`) is the surest evidence, and PAUTA-02 requires
    one for the conformance.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/README.md) (the badge and the *Working toward* line), held by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`theReadmeNamesTheEditionAndTheConformanceAndLinksTheDocsPage`).
    Termina's and Mirada's READMEs have a badge that names the edition alone and links the edition; Mirada's has
    a "Built to" line, which names no conformance. The other four READMEs name no edition.

- **PAUTA-17 · MUST.** For the app's coding agent: `AGENTS.md` has a section on Pauta (the app template heads
  it "Pauta") that names the edition `pauta.version` names and links that edition's `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`
  at its numbered address, never `latest/`
  ([Coding agents and LLMs](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/coding-agents/#point-the-apps-agent-at-its-edition)).
  - *Why:* an agent that reads no rules builds without them, and one that reads `latest/` "fixes" MUSTs of a newer
    edition the app hasn't moved to.
  - *Check (code):* `AGENTS.md` has a section on Pauta, under whatever heading, that names the edition
    `pauta.version` names and links `https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/llms.txt` and
    `https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/llms-full.txt` with that number; the file links neither at `latest/` nor at
    another edition. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/AGENTS.md), Termina's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/AGENTS.md) and Mirada's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/AGENTS.md) have the
    section, each under the heading "Pauta".
    Termina's [`AppInfoTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/AppInfoTest.java) (`agentsAndReadmeNameTheSameEdition`) asserts the edition and the `llms.txt` link; the
    template's [`EditionTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/EditionTest.java) asserts the edition (`theReadmeAndAgentsNameTheSameEdition`) and both links at
    that edition's address, with no `latest/` and no other edition (`agentsLinksTheEditionsRulesForCodingAgents`).
    Mirada's [`EditionTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/EditionTest.java) (`theReadmeAndAgentsNameTheSameEdition`) asserts the edition the file names and not its
    links. Editora's and nux's `AGENTS.md` have no such section, and Torrenta
    and Modula have no `AGENTS.md`.

## Platform baseline (PLAT)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/: JDK, JavaFX, AtlantaFX, NullAway, Maven Wrapper, tests and coverage: the stack every app shares.

- **PLAT-01 · MUST.** The app builds on **JDK 25 or newer**. `maven.compiler.release` 25 is the floor, not the
  ceiling: a newer JDK builds the app too, so no enforcer rule refuses one, in the main build or in any profile
  that turns itself on (an `<activation>` by JDK version, OS, property or file, or one that is `activeByDefault`;
  a profile turned on only by name, with `-P`, is not counted). CI builds every app on JDK 25, the current LTS:
  every workflow step that sets up a JDK sets up release 25, and the runtime an installer carries
  ([PLAT-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-02)) is that JDK's. A leg that builds a native image carries no JDK: it sets up a GraalVM 25
  release instead, 25.0 or any later 25.x. The family moves to the next LTS together, in an edition of Pauta.
  - *Check (code):* `pom.xml` sets `maven.compiler.release` to 25 or later. Every enforcer `requireJavaVersion`
    rule that counts refuses no JDK from 25 up: its range has no upper bound and starts at 25 or below, as the
    open-ended `[25,)` does, or a bare `25`, which the enforcer reads as 25 or newer. The rules that count
    are those of the main build and those inside a profile that turns itself on, one whose `<activation>` holds a
    `<jdk>`, an `<os>`, a `<property>` or a `<file>`, or an `<activeByDefault>` that is `true`: such a profile is
    on without being asked for, so its rule is the build's rule wherever it activates. A rule in a profile turned
    on only by name with `-P` is not counted, and an app with no rule that counts passes. In the workflows, every
    step that uses a `setup-java` or `setup-graalvm` action (`actions/setup-java`, `graalvm/setup-graalvm`) names
    25 or a 25.x release in its `java-version`, and in the `version` a GraalVM step may give beside it or instead.
    The Command reads the pom as text, with its XML comments left out, and a workflow line by line, not as YAML: a
    step ends at the next line that opens a list item. A version it cannot read as a number (an expression such as
    `${{ matrix.java }}`, a `java-version-file`) it prints as not judged and does not fail: read the matrix or the
    file it names. An enforcer range held in a property (`${…}`) it cannot follow: it prints the property and
    fails, so read the property's value.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; r=$(sed -n 's:.*<maven.compiler.release>\([0-9]*\)<.*:\1:p' pom.xml | head -n 1); p=$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < pom.xml | tr '<' '\n' | sed -n '/^!--.*-->/!p' | sed -n '/^!--/,/-->/!p'); j=$({ printf '%s\n' "$p" | sed -n '/^profiles>/,/^\/profiles>/!p'; printf '%s\n' "$p" | sed -n '/^profile>/,/^\/profile>/{/^profile>/h;/^profile>/!H;/^\/profile>/{x;/\nactivation>.*\njdk>.*\n\/activation>/{p;d;};/\nactivation>.*\nos>.*\n\/activation>/{p;d;};/\nactivation>.*\nproperty>.*\n\/activation>/{p;d;};/\nactivation>.*\nfile>.*\n\/activation>/{p;d;};/\nactivation>.*\nactiveByDefault>true\n.*\/activation>/{p;d;};};}'; } | sed -n '/^requireJavaVersion>/,/^\/requireJavaVersion>/s/^version>//p'); w=$(for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; for n in $(grep -nE '^[^#]*uses:[^#]*/setup-(java|graalvm)@' "$f" | cut -d: -f1); do c=0; for v in $(tail -n +"$n" "$f" | sed -n '1d;/^ *- /q;p' | grep -E '^ *(java-)?version:' | cut -d: -f2- | cut -d'#' -f1 | tr -d " '\"\r"); do c=1; if printf '%s\n' "$v" | grep -qE '^25([.+-].*)?$'; then :; elif printf '%s\n' "$v" | grep -q '^[0-9]'; then echo "$f:$n sets up release $v"; else echo "not judged: $f:$n version $v" >&2; fi; done; [ "$c" -eq 1 ] || echo "not judged: $f:$n version not given" >&2; done; done); [ "${r:-0}" -ge 25 ] && ! echo "$j" | grep -vxE '\[(1?[0-9]|2[0-5])([.][0-9]+)*,\)|(1?[0-9]|2[0-5])([.][0-9]+)*' | grep -q . && [ -z "$w" ] || { echo "maven.compiler.release ${r:-none}; requireJavaVersion in the main build and in profiles that turn themselves on:" ${j:-none}; [ -z "$w" ] || echo "$w"; false; }`
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) (one enforcer rule, `[25,)`) and [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
    (`java-version: '25'`); Termina's and Mirada's rules have the same range, and Modula and nux have no enforcer
    rule. Editora doesn't yet: beside the `[25,)` rule of its main build, its [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) has a profile,
    `formatter-needs-jdk25`, that activates on JDK `[26,)` and holds an enforcer rule with the range `[25,26)`, so
    a plain build on JDK 26 or newer stops unless it is told to skip the format check. Torrenta doesn't either: the
    rule in its main build has the range `[25,26)`. Mirada's profile of the same name skips the format check on
    those JDKs, says so, and refuses nothing ([`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/pom.xml)). No app's profile that activates by OS, property or
    file holds an enforcer rule (Termina's `os-windows` and `git-commit` and Modula's `app-image` among them), and
    no app has a profile that is `activeByDefault`.
    Every app's workflows set up 25. Mirada's native legs
    set up Oracle GraalVM with `version: '25.4'`, a GraalVM 25 release
    ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/release.yml)); its jlink leg sets up JDK 25.

- **PLAT-02 · SHOULD.** The installers carry a jlinked runtime; users never install Java.
  - *Check (code):* the `dist` profile's jpackage step builds a jlinked app image (`jLinkOptions`) and wraps the
    installer around it, and that image is what the release ships.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) (`dist` profile). Mirada ships a GraalVM native image instead on every target
    GraalVM builds one for, all but Intel macOS, which gets the jlinked image: [`scripts/native-app-image.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/native-app-image.sh) takes the
    Java runtime out of the app image, and users still install nothing.

- **PLAT-03 · MUST.** The app builds on **JavaFX 27 or newer**.
  - *Check (code):* `pom.xml` sets `javafx.version` to 27 or later.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; v=$(sed -n 's:.*<javafx.version>\([0-9]*\).*:\1:p' pom.xml | head -n 1); echo "javafx.version ${v:-none}"; [ "${v:-0}" -ge 27 ]`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml).

- **PLAT-04 · MUST.** The app is one named JPMS module, whose `module-info.java` opens only what reflection, FXML
  and Jackson need.
  - *Check (code):* `src/main/java/module-info.java` declares one named module, not an `open module`, which opens
    every package; each `opens` line serves FXML, Jackson or another reflective reader.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`src/main/java/module-info.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/module-info.java) (its module is `com.editora`). The name is the
    app's to choose: the template's is `com.example.app`, and its [`scripts/rename.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/scripts/rename.sh) gives the module the
    name of the app's Java package.

- **PLAT-05 · MUST.** Controls use **AtlantaFX 3.x** (`atlantafx-base`). The light and dark themes it carries are
  [ICON-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-15).
  - *Check (code):* `pom.xml` depends on `atlantafx-base` 3.x.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml), [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java).

- **PLAT-08 · MUST.** The build is **Maven** with the **Maven Wrapper** committed (`mvnw`, `mvnw.cmd`,
  `.mvn/wrapper/`), so `./mvnw` works on a clean machine.
  - *Check (code):* `mvnw`, `mvnw.cmd` and `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` are in the repository.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; ! for f in mvnw mvnw.cmd .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties; do test -f "$f" || echo "missing $f"; done | grep .`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`mvnw`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/mvnw), [`.mvn/wrapper/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.mvn/wrapper).

- **PLAT-09 · MUST.** Nullness is declared with **JSpecify** and checked by **NullAway** on **Error Prone** at
  compile time. Every package is `@NullMarked` in its own `package-info.java`.
  - *Check (code):* the compiler arguments include `-Xep:NullAway:ERROR`; every source package has a
    `package-info.java` with `@NullMarked`.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d src/main/java ] || { echo 'no src/main/java'; exit 1; }; { grep -q 'NullAway:ERROR' pom.xml || { echo 'no -Xep:NullAway:ERROR in pom.xml'; false; }; } && ! find src/main/java -name '*.java' ! -name package-info.java ! -name module-info.java -exec dirname {} \; | sort -u | while read -r d; do grep -qs '@NullMarked' "$d/package-info.java" || echo "not @NullMarked: $d"; done | grep .`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml), [`docs/conventions.md#null-annotations-jspecify-checked-by-nullaway`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/conventions.md#null-annotations-jspecify-checked-by-nullaway).

- **PLAT-10 · MUST.** Code is formatted by **Spotless** with Palantir Java Format, and CI fails an unformatted
  change in a Format job of its own: a job that runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests. When CI runs
  and which of its jobs the default branch requires are [REL-19](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-19).
  - *Why:* a check bound to a build phase fails in the same job as the tests, so the failed job does not say which
    of the two is wrong.
  - *Check (code):* the spotless plugin configures `palantirJavaFormat`, and in a workflow that runs on pull
    requests, which is where [REL-19](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-19) has CI run and so where an unformatted change is
    failed, a job runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests: no Maven `compile`, `test-compile`, `test`,
    `package`, `verify`, `integration-test`, `install` or `deploy` in the same job. The plugin's `check` goal bound
    to a phase (`./mvnw verify`) does not meet it alone.
    The Command reads a workflow line by line, not as YAML: a job is what lies between two keys at the indentation
    of the first key under `jobs:`, and a Maven run counts when its goal is on the line that names `mvn` or `mvnw`
    (a `name:` line is not a run). A Format job in a workflow of its own that a pull-request workflow calls
    (`workflow_call`, `uses: ./.github/workflows/<file>`) meets the rule, and the Command follows that call. What
    it does not see, so read the workflow where one applies: a goal on a continuation line; a build started from a
    script; a job's `if:`.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; grep -q palantirJavaFormat pom.xml || { echo 'pom.xml configures no palantirJavaFormat'; exit 1; }; for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do grep -qE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])pull_request(_target)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' "$f" 2>/dev/null || { grep -qE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])workflow_call([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' "$f" 2>/dev/null && grep -lE "^[^#]*uses:[^#]*\./$f" .github/workflows/* 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -lE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])pull_request(_target)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; } || continue; i=$(sed -n '/^jobs:/,$p' < "$f" | grep -E '^ +[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:' | head -n 1 | sed -n 's/^\( *\).*/\1/p'); for s in $(grep -nE '^[^#]*mvnw?(\.cmd)?[[:space:]]([^#]*[[:space:]])?spotless:check' "$f" | grep -vE '^[0-9]+: *-? *name:' | cut -d: -f1); do a=0; b=999999; for h in $(grep -nE "^$i[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:" "$f" | cut -d: -f1); do if [ "$h" -le "$s" ]; then a=$h; elif [ "$b" -eq 999999 ]; then b=$h; fi; done; m=; for t in $(grep -nE '^[^#]*mvnw?(\.cmd)?[[:space:]]([^#]*[[:space:]])?(compile|test-compile|test|package|verify|integration-test|install|deploy)([^A-Za-z0-9:_.=/-]|$)' "$f" | grep -vE '^[0-9]+: *-? *name:' | cut -d: -f1); do [ "$t" -ge "$a" ] && [ "$t" -lt "$b" ] && m="$m $f:$t"; done; [ -z "$m" ] && exit 0; echo "spotless:check at $f:$s shares its job with a build or test run:$m"; done; done; w=$(grep -lE '^[^#]*spotless:check' .github/workflows/* 2>/dev/null); echo "no job of its own runs spotless:check in a workflow that runs on pull requests (named in: ${w:-no workflow})"; exit 1`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) (spotless plugin), [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml) (the `format` job, *Format*); the
    template, Termina and Mirada have the same job in their `ci.yml`. Torrenta and Modula do not yet: their `test`
    job runs `./mvnw verify`, the phase the check is bound to, and no job runs `spotless:check`. nux has no Spotless.

- **PLAT-11 · MUST.** Tests run on **JUnit** (Jupiter, 5 or newer) over JavaFX's built-in **Headless** glass platform
  (`-Dglass.platform=Headless`), so FX tests need no display, no xvfb and no Monocle. **TestFX** MAY drive them; an
  app that doesn't use it starts the toolkit with `Platform.startup` and runs its steps on the FX thread.
  - *Check (code):* surefire's `systemPropertyVariables` set `glass.platform` to `Headless`; no Monocle dependency,
    and no xvfb in a step that runs tests (a release leg may use it to train the AOT cache, [REL-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-10)).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) (surefire), [`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md), [`FxTestSupport`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FxTestSupport.java), with TestFX;
    Termina [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/pom.xml) (surefire) and [`DialogAnswers`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/DialogAnswers.java), without it; the app template's
    [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) (surefire, and TestFX only to boot the toolkit) and [`FxTestSupport`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FxTestSupport.java).

- **PLAT-12 · MUST.** A **JaCoCo** `check` runs at `mvn verify` with build-wide floors of **≥ 0.90 lines and
  ≥ 0.90 methods**, and no profile that activates by OS or by JDK version lowers a floor or skips the check. The
  rule is about the pom's profiles, not about where CI runs the gate: a workflow that runs the tests on some of
  its runners with JaCoCo skipped is the workflow's choice and passes. The branch floor and each package's own
  floor are [QUAL-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-03).
  - *Check (code):* an execution of the JaCoCo plugin's `check` goal, whatever its id (Editora's is
    `jacoco-check`), is bound to `verify` with `BUNDLE` limits of 0.90 `LINE` and 0.90 `METHOD`. Where a limit is
    a property (`${coverage.bundle.line}` in Termina), its value is 0.90 or more in the main `<properties>` and
    in every profile that sets it and activates by OS or by JDK version (an `<activation>` with an `<os>` or a
    `<jdk>`), and no such profile sets `jacoco.skip` or the check's `<skip>`.
    A `-Djacoco.skip` on a workflow's command line is not judged.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) `jacoco-check`, with no profile that touches it; the template's and Mirada's are the
    same. Editora's [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) runs its tests on the other OSes with `-Djacoco.skip=true`, which the rule
    leaves to the workflow. Termina doesn't yet: its `os-windows` profile lowers the two floors to 0.45 and 0.47 on Windows
    ([`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/pom.xml)). Torrenta's check has a line floor and no method floor, and Modula and nux have no JaCoCo
    check.

- **PLAT-13 · SHOULD.** The app logs through `java.util.logging` and no other logging API. The Debug Log captures
  it: [DIAG-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-02).
  - *Check (code):* the app's own code imports no logging API other than `java.util.logging`.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d src/main/java ] || { echo 'no src/main/java'; exit 1; }; ! grep -rnE '^import (static )?(org\.slf4j|org\.apache\.logging|org\.apache\.commons\.logging|ch\.qos\.logback|org\.jboss\.logging|org\.tinylog)\.' src/main/java`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java).

- **PLAT-14 · SHOULD.** Config files are JSON, read and written by Jackson as plain classes (POJOs). Their schema
  versions and migrations are [SET-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-09).
  - *Check (code):* every class written to the config folder is read and written through Jackson's
    `ObjectMapper`; no store builds or parses its JSON by hand.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/Settings`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java), [`config/migration/ConfigSchema.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigSchema.java).

## Repository documents (REPO)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/: README, CHANGELOG, LICENSE, NOTICE, AGENTS.md and the rest of the files every repository carries.

- **REPO-01 · MUST.** `README.md` is a landing page with these parts: logo, badges, a one-paragraph pitch, the
  hero screenshot, highlights, install, build, command line, config folder, license. Detail lives on the website,
  which the README links, so the README stays short: at most 250 lines.
  - *Check (code):* `README.md` has each of those parts, links to the website for the rest, and runs to at most 250
    lines (`wc -l README.md`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/README.md) (221 lines) and the template's [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/README.md) (155); Termina's has 152
    and Mirada's 172. Three are over the 250: Torrenta's runs to 433 lines, Modula's to 364 and nux's to 313.

- **REPO-02 · MUST.** `CHANGELOG.md` follows [Keep a Changelog 1.1](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and
  SemVer: an `## [Unreleased]` section with Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed, and each entry opens with a bold
  one-line summary written for users.
  - *Check (code):* the file's first section is `## [Unreleased]` and the others are headed by a SemVer number
    and a date (`## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD`); the entries of a section sit under `### Added`, `### Changed`,
    `### Fixed` or `### Removed`, whichever it has entries for (Keep a Changelog's other two, `### Deprecated` and
    `### Security`, are as good); and every entry starts with `- **`.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/CHANGELOG.md) and Mirada's, where every entry opens in bold. In Editora's
    [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/CHANGELOG.md) 1,804 of 2,173 entries do: the older ones don't, and some sections have
    headings of its own (`### Performance`, `### Internal`, `### Packaging`), as some of Modula's and nux's do.
    Torrenta's sections are headed `## Unreleased` and `## 0.4.1 — 2026-10-28`, without the brackets.

- **REPO-03 · MUST.** `LICENSE` is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Adrián Arturo De León Saldivar", with the year the app
  started in: 2026 for the six apps, later for a newer one.
  - *Check (code):* `LICENSE` opens with `MIT License` and has that copyright line, with a year from 2026 on.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; tr -d '\r' < LICENSE | head -n 1 | grep -qx 'MIT License' && tr -d '\r' < LICENSE | grep -qxE 'Copyright \(c\) 20(2[6-9]|[3-9][0-9]) Adrián Arturo De León Saldivar' || { head -n 3 LICENSE; false; }`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/LICENSE).

- **REPO-04 · MUST.** `NOTICE` gives the app name, the copyright, "licensed under the MIT License", then every
  bundled third-party component with its license (Inter is OFL, AtlantaFX is MIT, OpenJFX is GPLv2+CPE…). The
  installers carry `NOTICE` too.
  - *Check (code):* `NOTICE` opens with the app's name, the copyright and the MIT sentence, and names every
    runtime dependency in `pom.xml` and every bundled font with its license; and the build puts `NOTICE` into what
    every installer carries (a `<resource>` that packages it into the application jar in Editora; an argument to
    `jpackage` or a packaging script does it as well). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`NOTICE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/NOTICE) and [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) (the `<resource>` that packages `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` into the
    application jar); two tests hold it: [`NoticeCoverageTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/packaging/NoticeCoverageTest.java) fails when a runtime dependency in `pom.xml` has no
    `NOTICE` entry, and [`BuildHygieneTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/packaging/BuildHygieneTest.java) when the pom no longer packages the two files.

- **REPO-05 · MUST.** `AGENTS.md` holds the operational rules for coding agents: essential commands,
  worktree-per-task, the change checklist. It is not a changelog. A short `CLAUDE.md` points to it.
  - *Check (code):* `AGENTS.md` has sections for commands, worktrees and the change checklist; `CLAUDE.md` is a few
    lines that send the reader to `AGENTS.md`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md), [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/CLAUDE.md).

- **REPO-06 · MUST.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` says how to build, test, format, and open a PR.
  - *Check (code):* `CONTRIBUTING.md` names the build, test and format commands and the PR step.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/CONTRIBUTING.md).

- **REPO-07 · MUST.** `docs/` holds `architecture.md`, `conventions.md`, `testing.md`, `gotchas.md`, `release.md`,
  `building-and-packaging.md` and `decisions/` (ADRs). The folder's index, `docs/README.md`, is
  [DOCS-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-12).
  - *Check (code):* each of those paths exists under `docs/`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs).

- **REPO-08 · MAY.** `TODO.md` holds the open list, kept in the same PR as the change.
  - *Check (code):* `TODO.md` exists at the root.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/TODO.md).

- **REPO-09 · MUST.** `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` is an issue form, and the in-app Report a Problem
  fills it: the link it opens names the form and carries the environment and the report as query parameters named
  by the ids of the form's two fields for them (Editora's ids are `environment` and `report`).
  - *Check (code):* the form is at that path and has a field for the environment and a field for the report, each
    with an `id`; and the link Report a Problem builds names the form's file and carries one query parameter per
    field, named by the field's id (`template=bug_report.yml&environment=…&report=…` in Editora). The ids are the
    app's to choose, as long as the form and the link agree.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) and [`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReport.java), which builds
    the link. The template, Termina, Torrenta and Mirada have the same form, ids and link; Modula and nux have no
    issue form.

- **REPO-10 · MUST.** `branding/` holds the source SVG of the icon. The PNG, ICNS and ICO generated from it sit
  beside it or in `packaging/`.
  - *Check (code):* `branding/` has an `.svg`; the `jpackage` icon paths in `pom.xml` point at the generated files.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`branding/editora-icon.svg`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/branding/editora-icon.svg), with [`editora.png`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/branding/editora.png), `.icns` and `.ico` beside it; the
    template keeps them in [`packaging/icons/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/tree/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/packaging/icons).

- **REPO-11 · SHOULD.** Every script in `scripts/` is a Java source file the JDK runs as it is (`java
  scripts/Name.java`, a compact source file or an ordinary class) or an `sh` or bash script.
  - *Why:* every app already needs the JDK, and a Java script runs the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Python or
    Node script makes every contributor and CI runner install a second toolchain for one step. A script that runs on
    Windows is easier to keep in Java than in bash.
  - *Check (code):* no file under `scripts/` is Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Perl, Groovy, Lua, PHP,
    PowerShell or a batch file, and every shebang there names `sh`, `bash` or `java`. Data files beside the scripts
    (fixtures, lists, templates) are not scripts.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d scripts ] || exit 0; bad=$(find scripts -type f | while IFS= read -r f; do if printf '%s\n' "$f" | grep -qE '\.(py|js|mjs|cjs|ts|rb|pl|ps1|bat|cmd|groovy|kts|lua|php)$'; then echo "$f"; continue; fi; l=$(head -n 1 "$f" | tr -d '\r'); if printf '%s\n' "$l" | grep -q '^#!'; then printf '%s\n' "$l" | grep -qE '^#! *(/usr)?/bin/(env +(-S +)?)?((ba|da)?sh|java)( |$)' || echo "$f: $l"; fi; done); [ -z "$bad" ] || { printf '%s\n' "$bad"; false; }`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`scripts/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts), whose Java
    scripts have their own tests, run by [`scripts/lib/RunTests.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/lib/RunTests.java)
    ([`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md)).

## Documentation (DOCS)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/: User docs on the app's website, developer docs in docs/, and the Help menu that opens them. Every app documents itself, and the docs change with the code.

### User documentation

- **DOCS-01 · MUST.** Every app has user documentation: a *Getting started* page (install, first launch, the first
  thing to do), one page per feature area, the keyboard reference, the Settings, and an FAQ. It is written for the
  person using the app, in their words, with screenshots from the real window. The README, a landing page of at
  most 250 lines ([REPO-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-01)), is not it.
  - *Check (code):* the app names a website for its user docs: its README or its About links one, or the address
    `help.documentation` opens ([DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-06)) is on one. The repository's own address on GitHub is not
    one. An app whose repository and About name no website has no user documentation to point at, and fails the
    rule from the app's checkout. The rest is in the website's repository: its docs (the files of
    `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) have a getting-started page, a keyboard reference (a keymaps page
    there), a settings or configuration page, an FAQ and a page per feature area, and the pages carry screenshots
    of the app's real window. The website is a repository of its own ([DOCS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-02)), which the app's
    checkout does not hold. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says
    what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* editora-website [`src/content/docs/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/tree/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/src/content/docs) (43 pages in nine categories, from *Getting started* to
    *Help*); torrenta-website (19), termina-website (16), mirada-website (11).

- **DOCS-02 · MUST.** The user docs live on the app's website, under `/docs/`, in the app's `<app>-website`
  repository, beside the feature pages, the screenshots, the news posts and the blog. Each docs page is a Markdown
  file whose frontmatter gives the page's category and its place in it (editora-website's keys are `category` and
