  `order`); the sidebar, the sitemap and the RSS feed follow. The app's repository carries none of them: a page
  kept in the app's `docs/` fails the rule when any section of it tells the app's user how to install or use
  something, even if the rest of the page is for contributors, and whether or not the website has it too.
  - *Check (code):* no page in the app's `docs/` has a section that tells the person using the app how to install
    or use something: one found there fails the rule from the app's checkout, whoever the rest of the page is
    written for. So does an app whose repository and About name no website for its user docs
    ([DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-01)): its user docs live on none. The rest is in the website's repository: every docs page
    there (the files of `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) gives its category and its order in its
    frontmatter. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would
    settle it.
  - *Reference:* editora-website [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/README.md) (*Content*). Editora doesn't yet, though its [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md) says "User-facing feature
    documentation goes to the separate website repository": [`docs/plugins.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/plugins.md), a page for plugin authors, has a
    section that tells the user the three ways to install a plugin and one on troubleshooting plugins. Termina
    doesn't either: [`docs/reference/installing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/docs/reference/installing.md) tells the person installing it which download to take, how to
    install each and how to check its signature, and its README sends the reader there. Nor does Torrenta:
    [`docs/headless.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/headless.md), [`docs/webapi.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/webapi.md) and [`docs/search-providers.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/search-providers.md) are guides for the person using it.

- **DOCS-03 · SHOULD.** Every link from the app into its user docs opens the running version's docs, the address
  `help.documentation` opens ([DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-06)) as much as a link to one page. Pages live under
  `/docs/v-<version>/…`; bare `/docs` and every unversioned slug redirect to the current version, so a link in a
  page never carries a version and a bump just regenerates one file (editora-website's `src/lib/version.ts`). The
  app builds the base from its own version with `-SNAPSHOT` dropped, so a development build points at the release
  it is working toward instead of a path that would always 404.
  - *Why:* a release that pointed at another release's docs would claim what is not true
    ([*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps)).
  - *Check (code):* the address the app opens for its docs is its website's `/docs/v-` plus the app's version
    without `-SNAPSHOT`: another address, the unversioned `/docs/` among them, fails the rule from the app's
    checkout. An app that opens no docs address has no link to judge and nothing to fail here: the missing address
    is [DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-06)'s. The rest is in the website's repository: it serves `/docs/v-<version>/` and redirects
    the unversioned paths (in its `astro.config.mjs`, in editora-website). An audit run from the app's checkout
    alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`AppInfo.docsUrl()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java), `releaseVersion()`; editora-website [`astro.config.mjs`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/astro.config.mjs), [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/README.md)
    (*Versioned docs*). The app template builds the same address (`docsUrl()` in its [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java)). Termina and
    Mirada don't yet: each opens its site's unversioned `/docs/` (`DOCUMENTATION` in Termina's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java),
    `DOCS_URL` in Mirada's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java)). Torrenta, Modula and nux open no docs address. The other three
    sites carry a comment to port these routes when their app first deep-links.

- **DOCS-04 · SHOULD.** The website's docs are generated where the app is the source. The Commands and Keybindings
  pages are generated from the app's command registrations, `messages.properties` and keymaps; What's new from
  `CHANGELOG.md`, and the Roadmap from `TODO.md` where the app keeps one ([REPO-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-08)); the
  version from `pom.xml`. The output is committed, so the site builds without the app checked out. A check fails
  the site when a docs page quotes a command id that does not exist or a chord that is bound to a different
  command.
  - *Why:* one fact, one source ([*One source of truth for each fact*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-building-them)).
  - *Check (code):* the website's repository holds the generators and their committed output (`scripts/` and
    `src/lib/` in editora-website) and a check of the ids and chords its docs quote (`npm run check:docs` there),
    and the site's build or its deploy workflow runs that check. An app that names no website has no docs to
    generate: the rule fails with [DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-01). All the rest is in the website's repository. An audit run
    from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* editora-website [`scripts/GenCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenCommands.java) (every `Command.of` in Editora's `com.editora.ui`,
    [`WindowCommandRegistrar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java) holding most), [`GenRoadmap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenRoadmap.java), [`GenFeatures.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenFeatures.java); [`scripts/check-doc-commands.mjs`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/check-doc-commands.mjs)
    (`npm run check:docs`), which exits non-zero on a missing id or a chord bound to another command. Nothing runs it
    yet: neither the `build` script in [`package.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/package.json) nor [`pages.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/.github/workflows/pages.yml) calls it, so it fails the site only when
    someone runs it by hand.

- **DOCS-05 · MUST.** The notes of a GitHub release, the text under its title, are written for the person using the
  app: they say what changed for them, and are not a list of commits or pull requests. In an app with a Welcome
  page, the page's *What's New* link opens this build's release, so those notes are what it shows. The bold
  one-line summary that opens each `CHANGELOG.md` entry is [REPO-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-02); the website's What's
  new is [DOCS-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-04); taking the notes from the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section is
  [REL-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-04).
  - *Check (code):* the release's notes are not generated from the history: the JReleaser configuration's
    `changelog` is not a `format` of commit hashes and titles, and no release step sets `generate_release_notes`.
    They come from text someone wrote, the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section or a notes file. And in an app with a
    Welcome page, the page's *What's New* link opens the build's own release page (`AppInfo.releaseNotesUrl()` in
    Editora).
  - *Reference:* Termina's [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/jreleaser.yml) takes the notes from a file (`changelog.external`) that
    [`scripts/release-notes.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/scripts/release-notes.sh) writes from the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section; the app template, Torrenta and Mirada
    do the same. Editora doesn't yet: its [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/jreleaser.yml) builds the notes from the commits
    (`format: '- {{commitShortHash}} {{commitTitle}}'`), and that list is what its *What's New* opens
    ([`AppInfo.releaseNotesUrl()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java), [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java), `welcome.whatsNew`). Modula's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) and nux's
    [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml) have GitHub generate them (`generate_release_notes: true`).

### Reachable from the app

- **DOCS-06 · MUST.** The `help.documentation` command opens the user docs in the browser. It is a command like any
  other, so it is in the palette and bindable, and where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a
  Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines) a **Documentation** row of
  that menu runs it through the registry like every other row. An app with a Welcome page repeats the command in the
  page's Help row. The row's place in the Help menu is [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-07).
  - *Check (code):* the command `help.documentation` is registered and opens the user docs' address in the
    browser; where the app has a Help menu, a row of that menu runs the command (the Help `MenuSpec` of Editora's
    `MenuBarModel` lists it), and a row beside a Help submenu is not in it; and in an app with a Welcome page, the
    page's Help row runs the same command through the registry (`welcome.documentation` in Editora's
    `WelcomePane`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowCommandRegistrar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java) (`help.documentation` → [`MainController.openDocumentation()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java)),
    [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`menubar.help`), [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java) (`welcome.documentation`). Mirada's macOS Help menu has
    the row ([`MacMenus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)); its main menu doesn't yet: there the Documentation row sits beside the Help submenu,
    not in it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)).

- **DOCS-07 · SHOULD.** Where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's
  main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines), its rows run in this order: Command Palette ·
  Documentation · the keyboard reference ([DOCS-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-08)) · Welcome Page · Check for Updates · Message Log ·
  Debug Log · Report a Problem · Pauta Conformance · About. In an app with a Simple mode, that mode's Help menu keeps
  Command Palette, Documentation, Welcome Page and About. An app without a feature drops its row; nothing moves.
  - *Check (code):* the rows of the Help menu the app has are in that order, in the full menu and in Simple mode's
    where the app has one (both `menubar.help` menu specs in Editora). An app with a Help menu in a menu bar on one
    OS and a Help submenu in its main menu is judged on both.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java), both `MenuSpec("menubar.help", …)`, for the rows its Help menu has. It has
    no Welcome Page row, since `view.welcome` is still in the View menu ([WELC-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/#welc-03)),
    and no keyboard-reference row. Termina's [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`documentation`, `whatsNew`, `keyboardShortcuts`,
    then `checkForUpdates`) and Mirada's macOS menu bar, [`MacMenus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java) (`PALETTE`, `DOCUMENTATION`, `SHORTCUTS`, then
    `CHECK_FOR_UPDATES`) put the keyboard reference there; Termina's What's New row, between the two, is its own.
    The Help submenu of Mirada's main menu doesn't follow the order yet: it holds Message Log, Debug Log, Report a
    Problem, then Check for Updates, and Documentation, the keyboard reference and About are rows of the main menu
    beside it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)).

- **DOCS-08 · SHOULD.** Where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's
  main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines), a row of it opens a keyboard reference: a searchable
  window of every key, grouped as the menus are, or the keybinding editor.
  - *Check (by hand):* open it from Help, search for a command, and find its key.
  - *Reference:* Termina's [`ShortcutsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ShortcutsWindow.java), a row of its Help menu, and Mirada's [`ShortcutsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ShortcutsWindow.java), a row of its
    macOS Help menu; in Mirada's main menu the row sits beside the Help submenu. Editora doesn't yet: its
    keybinding editor is a page of Settings ([Keyboard first](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/)), and no row of its Help menu opens it
    ([`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)).

- **DOCS-10 · MAY.** An app with a Search Everywhere picker opens per-command help from it as the Command Palette
  does: with a command highlighted, the palette's help chord ([PAL-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/#pal-08)) opens
  the command's page, `/docs/v-<version>/commands/<id>`. The two pickers share the chord and the URL builder, so
  they can never disagree.
  - *Check (code):* Search Everywhere takes its help chord the way the palette does and builds the page's address
    with the palette's own method (Editora's `CommandPalette.docsUrl`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`SearchEverywhereHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywhereHost.java) (`CommandPalette.docsUrl`) and [`SearchEverywherePopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java) (`docsChord`, from
    [`PickerKeys.freeChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) as the palette's); [`CommandPalette.docsUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java).

- **DOCS-11 · MAY.** Each page of the Settings window has a link to its docs page, *Help for* and the page's name,
  from one map of page to slug.
  - *Check (code):* one map from Settings page to docs slug feeds every page's help link.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`SettingsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java), [`SettingsFrameBits.helpUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsFrameBits.java), `settings.help`.

### Developer documentation

- **DOCS-12 · MUST.** `docs/` has an index. `docs/README.md` says who the folder is for (contributors; user docs
  live on the website) and lists every guide with one line; that the code wins is [DOCS-17](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-17). Which
  guides the folder holds is [REPO-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-07).
  - *Check (code):* `docs/README.md` exists, says who it is for, and links each guide in `docs/`.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`docs/README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/README.md); the template's [`docs/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/tree/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs).

- **DOCS-13 · SHOULD.** Every choice a newcomer would question has a decision record: a fork, a rejected
  dependency, a storage format, an escape hatch. It is one numbered Markdown file, `docs/decisions/NNNN-slug.md`,
  with the context, the decision and what it costs.
  - *Check (code):* `docs/decisions/` holds `NNNN-slug.md` files, each with context, decision and consequences.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`docs/decisions/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/decisions) (18 records, from [`0001-richtextfx-fork.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/decisions/0001-richtextfx-fork.md)).

- **DOCS-14 · MUST.** Three files have three jobs. `AGENTS.md` is the operational guide (what it holds is
  [REPO-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-05)). `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the short version for a person, pointing into
  `docs/`. `docs/` holds the durable explanations. Exhaustive history goes to `docs/reference/`, not into any of
  the three.
  - *Check (code):* `CONTRIBUTING.md` links into `docs/`. Neither `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` nor a guide in
    `docs/` ([REPO-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-07)) holds exhaustive history: a record of past work, or a catalog
    that sets out to list every part of a subsystem or every command (Editora's `architecture-catalog.md` and
    `commands.md` are two). Where the app keeps such material, it is in files under `docs/reference/`; an app
    that keeps none needs no `docs/reference/` and passes on the link. An audit report (`docs/pauta-audit.md`) is
    not such material.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md) (*Documentation map*), [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/CONTRIBUTING.md), [`docs/reference/README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/reference/README.md).

- **DOCS-15 · SHOULD.** Javadoc sits on its member: a doc comment above another doc comment documents nothing.
  Comments say why, not what.
  - *Check (code):* no Javadoc comment in the main or the test sources is followed by another with only blank
    lines or `//` comments between them. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`StackedJavadocTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/StackedJavadocTest.java), which fails the build on one.

### Kept in step

- **DOCS-16 · MUST.** The docs change with the code. A change that affects behavior updates `CHANGELOG.md` and the
  contributor guides it touches in the same pull request, the website's user docs in a pull request on the
  website's repository opened with it, and `TODO.md` where the app keeps one ([REPO-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-08));
  never as a follow-up. A reviewer treats a feature PR with no docs change as incomplete.
  - *Check (by hand):* read the app's most recently merged feature pull requests on GitHub, as many as it takes
    to see the habit: each one's diff touches `CHANGELOG.md`, the guides it concerns and, where the app keeps
    one, `TODO.md`, and one that changes what a user sees names the website's pull request. A recent one that
    changed behavior and touched none of them fails the rule. That `docs/conventions.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and
    `AGENTS.md` state the rule shows it is asked, not that it is kept. The person reads GitHub, not the running
    app, and the rule is still checked by hand: an audit reports it as `manual`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/conventions.md#docs-in-the-same-pr`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/conventions.md#docs-in-the-same-pr), [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/CONTRIBUTING.md) (step 4, which names the
    website repository), [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md); the template's [`docs/conventions.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/conventions.md). Editora, the template, Mirada and nux
    keep a `TODO.md`; Termina, Torrenta and Modula keep none.

- **DOCS-17 · MUST.** When documentation and code disagree, the code wins, and the documentation is fixed in the
  same change. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/README.md` say so, where a coding agent and a contributor start reading.
  Pauta applies the same rule to itself.
  - *Check (code):* `AGENTS.md` and `docs/README.md` say so.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md), [`docs/README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/README.md).

- **DOCS-18 · SHOULD.** An app's screenshots are retaken, not described: its capture hook or headless fixture
  ([QUAL-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-09)) renders the real window at 2× after any UI change, for the README (its hero in
  light and dark), the website and bug reports.
  - *Why:* a stale screenshot claims what is not true.
  - *Check (by hand):* the README's hero, in its light and its dark form, and the website's screenshots show the
    current UI at 2×; they are rendered from the real window by the capture hook or headless fixture
    [QUAL-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-09) asks for, not drawn or described.
  - *Reference:* Termina's [`DevCapture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/DevCapture.java) and Torrenta's [`DevCapture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/DevCapture.java), and nux's
    [`ui/Screenshot.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Screenshot.java) ([Shared features](https://pauta-project.dev/family/shared-features/)). None of the three renders at 2× yet: each writes what
    `scene.snapshot(null)` returns, the scene at its own size. Editora doesn't yet: it has no capture hook, and its
    headless fixture writes a screenshot from three FX tests only, when `-Deditora.test.shots=<dir>` is set, and
    at the scene's own size too ([`SplitViewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SplitViewFxTest.java)).

## Code quality gates (QUAL)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/: NullAway, coverage floors and the guard tests that pay for themselves across the family.

- **QUAL-02 · SHOULD.** A NullAway report is fixed, not suppressed: put `@Nullable` on what may be null.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rn '@SuppressWarnings("NullAway")' src/main` finds nothing.
  - *Reference:* Editora; one suppression is left, in [`recovery/RecoveryCodec.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/recovery/RecoveryCodec.java).

- **QUAL-03 · SHOULD.** Coverage floors are a regression net, not a target. Beyond the build-wide floor of 0.90
  lines and methods ([PLAT-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-12)), the build holds a branch floor (Editora's is 0.79), and
  each package of 300+ lines gets its own floor about three points below its measured level; when a package's
  coverage rises, its floor is ratcheted up.
  - *Check (code):* the `jacoco-check` rules in `pom.xml` carry a `BUNDLE` `BRANCH` limit and a `PACKAGE` line floor
    for each large package.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) `jacoco-check`.

- **QUAL-04 · SHOULD.** When a guide quotes the coverage floors, a test fails when the quoted table and the pom
  disagree.
  - *Check (test):* a build test reads the `jacoco-check` rules from `pom.xml` and compares them with the guide's
    table.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`BuildHygieneTest.theCoverageFloorsQuotedInTheTestingGuideAreTheOnesTheBuildEnforces`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/packaging/BuildHygieneTest.java),
    [`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md).

- **QUAL-05 · SHOULD.** Extract the decision, then test it ([principle 12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-building-them)):
  what decides whether a control is enabled or shown, or where a key or a click leads, sits in a pure helper
  with unit tests. The headless FX harness is for a test whose point is controller or toolkit behavior.
  - *Check (code):* enablement, visibility and navigation rules sit in classes that import no `javafx` type, each
    with a unit test that does not carry the FX tests' tag ([QUAL-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-06)).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md) (*Prefer pure logic*): [`ui/Chrome`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java), [`editops/TextNav`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editops/TextNav.java),
    [`config/PathKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/PathKeys.java), each with a plain unit test.

- **QUAL-06 · MUST.** Every test class that boots the JavaFX toolkit carries one JUnit tag, the same for all of
  them (Editora's is `fx`), so the pure suite runs alone by excluding that tag (`-DexcludedGroups=fx` in Editora).
  - *Check (code):* every test class that boots the toolkit (`Platform.startup`, `FxToolkit`, or a helper that
    calls one, such as Editora's `FxTestSupport`) carries the app's FX tag in a JUnit `@Tag`, whatever the tag is
    called (`@Tag("fx")` in Editora).
  - *Reference:* Termina holds it by test: [`FxTestTagsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/FxTestTagsTest.java) fails when a test source that names
    `Platform.startup(` or `FxToolkit.` has no `@Tag("fx")`. Editora states it in [`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md) and does not
    hold it fully yet: 38 of its `*FxTest` classes, 18 of them `ProjectMap*FxTest`, carry no tag. Torrenta doesn't
    yet: 26 of its test classes start the toolkit through its [`FxToolkit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/ui/FxToolkit.java) extension, and no test in the
    repository carries a tag.

- **QUAL-07 · SHOULD.** Tests do not sleep. A scope owns the workers and FX callbacks (Editora's
  `AsyncTestScope`), and tests wait on latches.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rn 'Thread.sleep' src/test` finds nothing.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`AsyncTestScope`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/AsyncTestScope.java), [`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md). Many older Editora tests still poll with
    `Thread.sleep`.

- **QUAL-08 · SHOULD.** A test window writes only inside its temp folders, never in the real home directory.
  - *Check (code):* the fixture that builds a test window gives it a temp config folder, and points every other
    folder a command writes to (the one a configuration export lands in, say) at a temp folder too. A test that
    asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FxWindowFixture`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FxWindowFixture.java) (a temp config folder and a temp export folder for each window);
    [`CommandSweepFxTest.leftInTheHomeDirectory`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandSweepFxTest.java) looks in the home directory after running every command.

- **QUAL-09 · MUST.** The app has a way to show its real window with nobody at the screen: a capture hook that
  saves a screenshot of it, or a headless fixture that builds it as the app does. That is what verifies UI work in
  the running app ([principle 13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-building-them)), with real key and mouse events,
  before a UI change is called done.
  - *Check (code):* the app has a capture hook (Termina's `DevCapture`) or a headless fixture (Editora's
    `FxWindowFixture`) that builds the real window through the code the app itself starts with.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FxWindowFixture`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FxWindowFixture.java) (the real [`MainController`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) window, headless); Torrenta's
    [`DevCapture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/DevCapture.java) and Termina's [`DevCapture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/DevCapture.java).

- **QUAL-10 · SHOULD.** A guard that cannot fail is decoration. When you add a drift or parity test, break the
  thing it guards once and watch it fail.
  - *Check (by hand):* break what the new test guards, run it, and see it fail.
  - *Reference:* Modula's [`DependenciesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/test/java/com/modula/DependenciesTest.java).

- **QUAL-11 · SHOULD.** A command sweep runs every registered command in a real headless window.
  - *Check (test):* one FX test iterates the registry and runs each command.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandSweepFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandSweepFxTest.java).

- **QUAL-13 · SHOULD.** A settings round trip shows that every switch, number and choice survives a restart.
  - *Check (test):* one FX test sets every control, reloads the settings and reads each back.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`SettingsRoundTripFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsRoundTripFxTest.java); the app template's [`SettingsRoundTripFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SettingsRoundTripFxTest.java)
    (`everyControlSurvivesARestart`), which changes every combo box, switch and field on every Settings page,
    restarts on the same folder and reads each one back.

- **QUAL-15 · SHOULD.** A release supply-chain test keeps the signing and attestation steps where they are.
  - *Check (test):* a test reads the workflows and fails when a signing, notarization or attestation step moves or
    goes.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ReleaseSupplyChainTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/packaging/ReleaseSupplyChainTest.java).

## Performance (PERF)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/: Keep the JavaFX application thread free, coalesce work, bound memory, and measure: the rules that keep every app responsive.

### The UI thread

- **PERF-01 · MUST.** Never block the JavaFX application thread. No file or network I/O, no process start or wait,
  no parsing, searching, hashing or JSON of any size on it, and no `Thread.sleep`, `Future.get()`, `join()` or
  `Process.waitFor()` there. Two exceptions. At start-up, before the first window is shown, `start()` may wait once
  for the config read that [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-16) began before the toolkit, and may read the bundled resources that
  window is built from: its fonts, registered there or by a thread `start()` waits for once
  ([ICON-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-02) requires them before any CSS is applied), the message catalog, the
  keymap and its icons. Nothing else at start-up is excepted: a log file opened, a file or a store of the user's
  read (presets, profiles, schedules, themes the user added), a ledger read, a socket bound or a lock taken blocks
  the thread as it would anywhere, and so does a font registered on it after the first frame. And as the app quits,
  when no frame is left to block, the quit method ([WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-13)) or `Application.stop()` may
  make the last save on it: write the settings, the window state and the session, or wait for a write already
  under way. An app whose `start()` loads its settings itself, whether or not `main` read the file earlier, or
  waits for a read begun after the toolkit, has PERF-16's gap and none here.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rnE 'Files\.[a-z]|File(Input|Output)Stream|File(Reader|Writer)|RandomAccessFile|getResourceAsStream|loadFont|HttpClient|openConnection|openStream|new Socket|SocketChannel\.open|ProcessBuilder|getRuntime\(\)\.exec|\.waitFor\(|Thread\.sleep|\.join\(\)|uture[A-Za-z]*\.get\(|\.get\([^)]*TimeUnit|invokeAndWait|\.await\(' src/main/java`
    lists the candidates: the lines that read or write a file or a bundled resource, open a connection, start or
    wait for a process, sleep, or wait for another thread. Each line is judged by reading what calls it. It is fine
    when only an executor's task or a thread's body reaches it; when `start()` reaches it before the first window
    is shown and it is one of the things the statement allows there, the one `join()` or `get()` on the config
    read begun before the toolkit, or the reading of a resource bundled with the app that the first window is
    built from: the registering of the fonts it draws with (Editora's `Fonts.loadForFirstPaint`) or the one wait
    for the thread that registers them, the message catalog (Editora's `Messages.init`), the keymap (Editora's
    `KeymapManager.loadNamed`) or the window's icons; or when it is the last save, made by the quit method or
    `Application.stop()`, which may do nothing else that blocks. It is a violation when an event handler, a
    listener, a `Platform.runLater` body, a timer's or an animation's callback, or `start()` reaches it on the FX
    thread, itself or through a method it calls: a handler that calls a settings store's `save()` writes the file
    on the FX thread. In `start()` everything else is a violation, before the first window is shown or after: a
    second wait for the config, a log file opened, a file or a store of the user's read (presets, profiles,
    schedules, a folder of themes the user added), a ledger read, a socket bound, a lock taken. Only the settings
    are left to [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-16): a load of them made in `start()` itself, whether or not `main` read the file
    earlier, and a wait for a read of them begun after the toolkit. A font registered on the FX thread after the
    first frame is a violation too. A grep finds only the spellings it is given: read the handlers and listeners
    too for parsing, searching, hashing or JSON done in place, and for a wait under another name.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) §1; its one start-up wait is `takeBootstrap` in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java),
    which joins the `config-prefetch` read, and `Fonts.loadForFirstPaint`, called next, registers its first fonts
    ([`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java)); the `config-prefetch` thread reads the catalog too, and `start()` reads it only when
    that thread picked another language (`Messages.init`). Mirada's `start()` makes the two waits the first
    exception allows: `settings()` joins the settings read, which also reads its catalog (in its jlink image that
    read begins after the toolkit, which is [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-16)'s gap and none here), and `Fonts.ready`, before the
    window is shown, joins the thread that registers its fonts
    ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java), [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Fonts.java)). For the last save, the app template's [`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) waits for the
    settings write on a background thread and exits from there, which needs no exception, and its
    `Application.stop()` then waits for the writer once more on the FX thread (`Running.close` in
    [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), which the second exception allows; Termina's
    [`WindowManager.closeAll`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java), run from `Application.stop()`, flushes its settings on the FX thread, which the second
    exception allows. The app template does its start's file work off the FX thread: `prepare` in
    [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java), which refuses the FX thread and runs on a thread of its own while the toolkit starts, opens the
    Debug Log's session file, reads the settings, the catalog and `pauta.json` and binds the single-instance socket;
    `start()` then registers its first fonts, which the first exception allows (`Fonts.load`), and the remaining
    font is registered off the FX thread after the first frame (`Fonts.loadDeferred`). No app has been read through
    for the rule yet, and none holds it everywhere. Found so far:
    Editora's `start()`, in that `App.java`, does on the FX thread, before its first window is shown, what no
    exception covers: its calls to `DebugLog.attachFile` (the Debug Log's session file),
    `SharedConfig.claimInstance` (the lock on a file in the config folder), `ProcessRegistry.reapOrphans` (the
    ledger of the servers it started), `McpServer.reapStaleEndpoint` (a stale `mcp-endpoint.json`) and
    `Themes.loadUserThemes` (the user themes' folders). Some of its handlers still touch the disk too, for example
    `renameFileTo` (`Files.exists`, `Files.move`) and `openPersonalDictionary` (`Files.writeString`) in [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java)
    and the new-folder prompt in [`ui/ProjectPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java) (`Files.createDirectories`). Torrenta's `start()` reads its
    catalog, which the exception allows, and opens that file the same way (`DebugLog.attachFile` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java));
    its main window's constructor, before the window is shown, reads six stores of the user's (the profiles, the
    labels, the watch folders, the search providers, their definitions and the RSS feeds, in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)),
    and `start()` reads `profiles.json` again once the window is shown (`Startup.profile`). Termina reads its
    settings, its first fonts, its catalog and its imported themes in `Application.init()`, off the FX thread
    (`prepare` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)); building its first window then reads the bundled keymap ([`ui/Keymap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Keymap.java), on
    the first `Keymap.defaultFor`) and decodes the window's icons ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Icons.java), `Icons.applyTo`) on the FX
    thread, which the exception allows, and once the window is shown `start()` deletes a stale socket file and
    binds the socket for later launches there, which it does not (`serve` in [`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/instance/SingleInstance.java)). It also registers
    its remaining font families on the FX thread after the first frame, which no exception covers ([`Fonts.loadRest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Fonts.java), called from that `App.java`).
    Mirada, on macOS, compares two paths on the FX thread when it was started with a file and the OS hands it its
    first one (`Files.isSameFile` in [`os/MacOpenFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacOpenFiles.java)). nux waits up to two seconds for the tray icon's removal in the
    handler of Settings' Save ([`AwtTray.dispose`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/tray/AwtTray.java), reached from [`TrayController.settingsSaved`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/TrayController.java)) and writes its
    `--screenshot` file from an animation's callback ([`ui/Screenshot.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Screenshot.java)).
    Torrenta writes its settings from the listeners
    of its Settings rows (`saveQuietly` in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java)) and asks the file store for the free space
    on each keystroke in a save-folder field (`updateFreeSpace` in [`ui/LocationDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/LocationDialog.java)). Modula reads its
    presets and its schedules in its pane's constructor, before the window is shown (`config.loadPresets` and
    `config.loadSchedules` in [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), writes its presets and settings from handlers
    (`config.savePresets` and `config.saveSettings` in that file) and, building its Settings window, starts
    `ffmpeg -version` and waits up to five seconds for it ([`Encoders.isAvailable`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/audio/Encoders.java)).

- **PERF-02 · MUST.** Touch the scene graph only on the FX thread. Background work hands its result back with
  `Platform.runLater`; nothing else creates, changes or reads live nodes.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rnE 'new Thread\(|Thread\.(ofVirtual|ofPlatform|startVirtualThread)|\.(submit|execute|schedule|scheduleAtFixedRate|scheduleWithFixedDelay)\(|(supply|run)Async\(|\.(thenAccept|thenRun|thenApply|thenCompose|whenComplete|handle|exceptionally)(Async)?\(' src/main/java`
    lists the candidates: the lines that start a thread, hand a task to an executor, or add a step to a future that
    completes off the FX thread. Each line is judged by reading the task's body. It is fine when the body touches
    nothing a scene shows, or touches it only inside `Platform.runLater`. It is a violation when the body, or a
    method it calls, sets a control's value, changes an observable list a view shows, or reads a live node's state
    outside a `runLater`. A callback that a library runs on a thread of its own (a file watcher, a process's reader, a
    logging handler) is a task body too, and the grep does not list those: read the listeners the app gives its
    services as well.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`git/GitService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/git/GitService.java): every task it gives its workers hands the result to its caller
    inside `Platform.runLater`. No app has been read through for the rule yet.

- **PERF-03 · MUST.** A background result is applied under a generation guard, so an answer to an old request never
  overwrites a newer one.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rn 'runLater' src/main/java` lists the candidates: the lines where another thread hands
    something to the FX thread. Each line is judged by reading it. It needs the guard when what it applies answers a
    request that can be made again before the answer comes: a search, a load, a status or completion query that
    typing, a selection or a refresh starts. There each request takes a mark that the next request replaces (a
    counter, as Editora's `AtomicLong.incrementAndGet`, or a helper that keeps the latest request only, as Editora's
    `LatestOnly`), and the answer is applied only while its mark is still the newest, compared inside the
    `runLater`. It is a violation when such an answer is applied with no comparison, or with one made only before
    the `runLater`. A line needs no guard when nothing newer can replace what it hands over: an event, a batch of a
    stream, a result asked for once at start-up.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`git/GitService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/git/GitService.java) (`refresh`, with its `refreshGen` counter), [`search/SearchService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/search/SearchService.java) and
    [`ui/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/LatestOnly.java) ([`LatestOnlyTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LatestOnlyTest.java)); Termina ([`work/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/work/LatestOnly.java)) and Mirada
    ([`ui/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/LatestOnly.java)) carry the same helper. No app has been read through for the rule yet. Found so
    far: nux applies each Refresh of its Events window, and each load of the Energy and Outages tabs of its
    History window, with no mark ([`ui/EventsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/EventsWindow.java), `offFx` in [`ui/HistoryWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/HistoryWindow.java)), beside a
    Charts tab that numbers its loads and applies only the newest.

- **PERF-04 · SHOULD.** Every thread is named and is a daemon.
  - *Why:* a thread dump then says what is running, and a stray worker never keeps the app alive after its last
    window closes.
  - *Check (code):* every `Executors.new…` and `new Thread` gets a name and `setDaemon(true)`, through a thread
    factory such as `daemon("my-feature")`; virtual threads are daemons already.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`terminal/TerminalExecutors.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/terminal/TerminalExecutors.java) (its `daemon(name)` thread factory); the canonical
    shape is in [The UI thread](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#the-ui-thread).

- **PERF-05 · MUST.** Blocking work stays off the common `ForkJoinPool`: no `supplyAsync` or `runAsync` without an
  executor runs a blocking call, and a `Process` subclass overrides `onExit()`, whose inherited version is a
  `waitFor()` on that pool.
  - *Why:* the common pool has one worker fewer than the machine has cores, so a few blocked waits
    (`CompletableFuture.supplyAsync` of a `waitFor`) starve every other user of it.
  - *Check (code):* no `supplyAsync` or `runAsync` without an executor wraps a blocking call (a wait, a read or
    write of a file, a socket or a process), and every class that extends `Process` overrides `onExit()`. An app
    with no `Process` subclass has only the first half to show.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`process/ExitWatch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/ExitWatch.java), [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/gotchas.md). Editora's [`DapManager.reportJavaExit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/DapManager.java) still
    waits up to 3 s for an exit code in a `supplyAsync` on the common pool, and Termina's `handOff` in
    [`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/instance/SingleInstance.java) connects to a socket, writes and reads in one.

### Hot paths

- **PERF-06 · MUST.** Redraws are coalesced to at most one per pulse, with a flag that one request is already
  queued. A redraw is the painting of what the app draws itself, a canvas, a chart or a grid of cells; in an app
  that paints nothing itself, it is the refresh of its list or view.
  - *Check (code):* a redraw request sets a flag (Editora's are named `…Pending`) and schedules one pass, and a
    request that finds the flag set schedules nothing. A handler that paints, or in an app that paints nothing
    refreshes its list or view, straight from its event has no such flag and fails: a chart drawn from its width
    listener and again from its height listener draws twice for one resize. Setting a control's own property in
    a handler (a label's text, a progress bar's value) is not a redraw: JavaFX draws the control once on the next
    pulse.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) §2 (the `redrawPending` shape) and
    [`ui/WindowToolbar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java) (`scheduleEditStateRefresh`, with its `editStateRefreshPending` flag). [`ui/FxThrottle.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FxThrottle.java)
    is another tool: a leading-edge throttle with a maximum wait and no such flag, which runs the first request
    of a burst at once and then at most one per interval.

- **PERF-23 · MUST.** Work driven by text the user types waits for typing to pause (a debounce) when it leaves the
  FX thread or cannot finish within a frame: a search of files, a request to a server, a re-highlight. Filtering a
  list already in memory, as a command palette does, is exempt and runs on every keystroke.
  - *Check (code):* a listener on a text input's text that starts background work, or work too long for one frame,
    restarts a timer (a `PauseTransition`'s `playFromStart`, or the app's debounce helper) and the work runs when the
    timer fires; a listener that only filters or ranks an in-memory list needs none.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SearchInFilesPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchInFilesPopup.java) (150 ms before `runSearch`), [`ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java) (120 ms),
    [`ui/WorkspaceSymbolPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WorkspaceSymbolPopup.java) (150 ms before the language server is asked) and, for the editor's text,
    [`editor/SettledEditDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/SettledEditDispatcher.java), one timer that runs the re-highlight 150 ms after the last edit. Its
    [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) and [`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) filter their in-memory lists on every keystroke: the exempt case.
    Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: the debugger's completion ([`ui/DebugCompletion.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugCompletion.java)) asks the
    debug adapter again on every change of the field's text while its list is open, with no timer, and
    [`ui/FileFinder.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileFinder.java) starts reading a folder as soon as the typed path names another one.

- **PERF-07 · MUST.** An app that shows a stream as it arrives (the output of a process, log records, progress or
  readings from another thread) hands it to the FX thread in batches at least 16 ms apart, never one `runLater` per
  line or record.
  - *Check (code):* in an app that shows a stream, the thread that receives it appends to a buffer that the FX
    thread drains, with a minimum interval of 16 ms or more between drains, or once a pulse (pulses come a frame
    apart); no reader calls `Platform.runLater` once for each line or record. A stream is what arrives at its
    source's pace, however many items that is: a process's output, log records, the results of a scan handed
    over as each is found. A poll the app paces itself, one hand-over for each tick of a timer of 16 ms or more
    (a reading fetched every few seconds), already hands over that far apart and needs no buffer. An app whose
    FX thread is sent no stream, as one whose log window reads its store only when it opens or is refreshed, is
    not covered.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`process/OutputPump.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/OutputPump.java) (`MIN_DRAIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS`), [`ui/ConsoleAppender.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleAppender.java).
    Torrenta doesn't yet for its event log: the bridge in [`ui/EventLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/EventLog.java) (`logBridge`) hands each warning
    it catches to the FX thread in a `runLater` of its own. nux doesn't yet for its network scan: `scan` in
    [`service/DiscoveryService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/service/DiscoveryService.java) hands each server it finds to the FX thread in a `runLater` of its own; its
    poll hands over one reading every five seconds ([`service/PollService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/service/PollService.java)), which is paced already. Mirada's
    Debug Log window ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)) reads the log when it opens and on Refresh, so no log stream
    reaches its FX thread.

- **PERF-08 · MUST.** Work only on what is visible and only on what changed: no O(document) or O(list) work per
  keystroke, scroll or tick, and a list the user or the data can grow without a limit the app sets is shown in a
  virtualized control (`ListView`, `TableView`, a fixed cell size), which builds nodes for the visible rows only.
  Filtering a list already in memory, as a command palette does, is exempt and runs on every keystroke.
  - *Check (code):* `grep -rnE 'textProperty\(\)|KEY_(TYPED|PRESSED)|setOnKey|setOnScroll|vvalueProperty|AnimationTimer|Timeline|PauseTransition|scheduleAtFixedRate' src/main/java`
    lists the first candidates: the listeners on text, keys and scrolling, and the timers. Each line is judged by
    reading what it runs on every keystroke, scroll or tick. It is fine when that handles the edited range or the
    visible rows, or filters or ranks a list already in memory. It is a violation when it reads, measures, styles
    or rebuilds the whole document or every item of a list. An editor's own stream of changes is a text listener
    too (Editora's `plainTextChanges`), which the grep does not list.
    `grep -rnE 'getChildren\(\)\.(add|addAll|setAll)\(' src/main/java` lists the second: the lines that put
    nodes into a pane. It is a violation where a loop makes one node for each item of a list the user or the data
    can grow without a limit the app sets (results, log records, files, transfers), which belongs in a `ListView`
    or `TableView`; it is fine where the pane holds a set of controls the code fixes, or a list the app caps at a
    number it names (a bar of at most five preset chips).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`editor/highlight/HighlightPass.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/highlight/HighlightPass.java), which restyles only as far as an edit reaches.
    No app has been read through for the rule yet. Found so far, each a loop that makes a node for every item of
    a list nothing caps: Modula's preset bar (a chip for each preset, `rebuild` in [`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)); nux's
    dashboard (a card for each saved profile it watches and for each UPS, rebuilt as readings arrive, `setFleet` and
    `setOverview` in [`ui/Dashboard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Dashboard.java)); Torrenta's rule and tags dialogs (a check box for each feed and each
    tag, [`ui/RuleDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RuleDialog.java), [`ui/TagsDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/TagsDialog.java)); and Editora's crontab preview and pull-request checks card
    (a node for each job and each check run, [`editor/structured/CrontabPreview.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/structured/CrontabPreview.java), [`ui/ChecksListCard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ChecksListCard.java)).

- **PERF-09 · SHOULD.** A hot path allocates little: it reuses buffers and arrays, and caches data a repaint only
  reads.
  - *Check (code):* the per-frame and per-keystroke code allocates no new arrays or images when the size has not
    changed.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`editor/minimap/Minimap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/minimap/Minimap.java) (the snapshot image reused at the same size),
    [`MinimapRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/minimap/MinimapRows.java). The app template's palette cells keep their
    text runs, chord chip and tooltip and relabel them as the query changes, making a new run only when a title needs
    more than the cell had ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)).

- **PERF-10 · SHOULD.** CSS stays cheap: no `applyCss()` on a large subtree, stable style classes, and spans of the
  same style merged before they are applied.
  - *Check (code):* `applyCss()` is called only on small nodes; style classes are not toggled per keystroke.
  - *Reference:* Editora `SpanMerger` in [`editor/highlight/TextMateHighlighter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/highlight/TextMateHighlighter.java), [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/gotchas.md). The app template's palette
    draws a title as one text run per change of style, not a node per letter ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)).

### Memory and size

- **PERF-11 · MUST.** Everything that grows is bounded: logs, histories, consoles, caches, undo. The newest is kept.
  - *Check (code):* each store that grows while the app runs (a log, a history, a console's text, a cache, an undo
    stack) has a named cap, and the code that adds to it drops the oldest entry once the cap is passed. A test that
    fills a store past its cap and finds the oldest dropped is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) (200 entries, the oldest dropped; [`MessageLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogTest.java)), [`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java)
    (2,000 records, the oldest dropped; [`DebugLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogTest.java)), and [`test/OutputCap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/test/OutputCap.java), which keeps the head and the tail of one
    test's output (200,000 characters) with a note between them of how much was cut. The note is Editora's choice,
    not part of the rule.

- **PERF-12 · MUST.** In an app that opens files or data the user picks, a large input is guarded before it loads:
  its size is checked before its content is read, or the read is capped, and what will not fit is never read in.
  The app refuses it with a message or opens only the part that fits. Where an input can open with less, without
  features the app runs over its content, as a file in an editor can open without highlighting or a minimap, the
  app steps down as the input grows: those features turn off past one threshold, and past another it opens
  read-only or capped. An input the app can only read in or refuse (an imported theme, a `.torrent` file) has
  nothing to step down to.
  - *Check (code):* the code that loads a picked file or import compares its size against a named limit before
    reading the content, or reads through a cap, and refuses or cuts what passes the limit. Where the app runs
    features over an input's content that the input can open without (an editor's highlighting, its minimap), a
    lower named threshold turns them off and a higher one opens the input read-only or capped. Where it runs
    none, the size check or the cap is the whole of the rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora, whose tiers are the example: [`EditorBuffer.LARGE_FILE_BYTES`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/EditorBuffer.java) (5 MB: no highlighting, no minimap) and
    `HUGE_FILE_BYTES` (50 MB: read-only and cut to 50 MB), and [`ui/LoadHeapGuard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/LoadHeapGuard.java), which caps a load at
    what the free heap affords ([`LoadHeapGuardTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LoadHeapGuardTest.java)). Termina's theme import has nothing to step down to:
    `importFile` in [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Themes.java) reads at most 8 MB and [`theme/ThemeImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/theme/ThemeImport.java) refuses a file over 4 MB.
    Torrenta doesn't yet for a `.torrent` file the user picks: `resolve` in [`session/Session.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/session/Session.java) reads it whole
    (`Files.readAllBytes`) without looking at its size.

- **PERF-13 · MUST.** A closed window releases what it held: listeners, timers, executors, file watchers, native
  resources.
  - *Check (code):* the code that runs when a window closes (its close or hide handler, or the dispose method that
    handler calls) stops every timer and animation the window started, shuts down every executor, thread and file
    watcher it owns, frees its native resources (a process, a socket, a file handle), and removes each listener it
    added to something that outlives it: the shared settings, a service, another window. A test that opens and
    closes windows and finds nothing left running is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`MainController.disposeWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which shuts down each owner of a window's workers in
    turn, one failure never skipping the rest ([`ui/WindowDisposal.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowDisposal.java)). Its tests:
    [`FxWindowFixtureLifecycleFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FxWindowFixtureLifecycleFxTest.java), which finds a disposed window's workers shut down, and
    [`ClosedLspManagers`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/lsp/ClosedLspManagers.java). The app template ([`WindowLifecycleFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/WindowLifecycleFxTest.java)), Termina ([`WindowLifecycleTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/WindowLifecycleTest.java)) and
    Mirada ([`ClosedWindowTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/ClosedWindowTest.java)) have such a test too.

### Start-up

- **PERF-14 · MUST.** The first frame comes first: only what the first window shows is built before it. Everything
  else builds on first open: a closed panel's content, the Settings pages, the dialogs and the other windows.
  - *Check (code):* the code that builds the first window (`start()`, and the main window's constructor and what
    it calls) makes only what that window shows: no Settings window or page, no dialog, no other window and, in an
    app with tool panels, no closed panel's content. Each of those is made by the code that first opens it, through
    a supplier or a field filled on first use. A test that opens the first window and finds none of them built is
    the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora's lazy [`ToolWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindow.java) suppliers, and its Settings pages, built on the first `show`
    ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java)). [`LazyToolWindowsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LazyToolWindowsFxTest.java) asserts the tool-panel part: no closed tool window
    has built its panel. Editora doesn't hold the rule in one place yet: it builds the shared Output console
    (`buildOutput`), an empty tab pane, with the window, because every build writes to it while it is closed, and
    the test leaves that panel out. The template's [`StartupDeferralFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StartupDeferralFxTest.java) and Mirada's [`StartupDeferralTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StartupDeferralTest.java)
    assert it for their first windows. Torrenta doesn't yet: the constructor of its main window makes the Log, the
    Statistics and the Settings windows (`new LogWindow`, `new StatisticsWindow`, `new SettingsWindow` in
    [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)).

- **PERF-15 · MUST.** What nobody waits for starts after the first frame has painted: the update check, extra
  fonts, indexes and caches.
  - *Check (code):* the update check, the loading of fonts the first window does not draw with, and the building
    of indexes and caches start from a callback that runs once the first frame has painted (a pulse after the
    window is shown, as Editora's `loadRemainingAfterNextPaint` waits for), never from `main`, `init()` or the body
    of `start()`. A test that finds the deferred work not started before the first paint is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java), [`Fonts.loadRemainingAfterNextPaint`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java)
    ([`UpdateCheckSchedulerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckSchedulerTest.java), [`FontsDeferredLoadFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FontsDeferredLoadFxTest.java), [`StartupDeferralFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StartupDeferralFxTest.java)). The template
    (`FirstPaint.then` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), Termina (`FirstFrame.after` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)) and Mirada
    (`afterFirstPaint` in [`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java)) defer theirs the same way. Modula
    and nux don't yet: each starts its update check in the body of `start()` (`checkForUpdates` in
    [`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java), `maybeCheckForUpdates` in nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)).

- **PERF-16 · SHOULD.** The config read starts on a thread of its own before the toolkit does, so the two overlap
  and the wait for it that [PERF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-01) allows at start-up, `start()` taking the result, is short. An app
  whose `start()` loads its settings itself does not meet this, whether or not `main` read the file earlier.
  - *Check (code):* `main` starts the config read on its own thread before `launch`, from an entry point that is
    not the `Application` subclass (the launcher starts the toolkit for one before its `main` runs), and `start()`
    takes that read's result instead of reading the files itself. A load `start()` makes only when the earlier read
    failed is a fallback and passes.
  - *Reference:* Editora's `config-prefetch` thread in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) (`prefetchConfig`, joined once by
    `takeBootstrap`), entered through [`Launcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/Launcher.java). Mirada's `settings-read` thread in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java)
    (`readSettings`, joined by `settings()`) does the same in the native image, which enters through `Launcher`; its
    jlink image's main class is `App` itself, so there the toolkit is up before the read starts. Termina reads its
    settings in `Application.init()` (`prepare` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)): off the FX thread, so `start()` waits for
    nothing, but after the toolkit has started. The app template meets it: its [`Main.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java), not the `Application`
    subclass, starts `Startup.readAhead` on a thread of its own before `launch`, and `App.init` takes the result
    (`takePrepared` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), so `start()` reads no settings file. Torrenta
