    ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java)), Modula ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)) and nux ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), which also reads the file once in
    `main` for the language) load their settings inside `start()`. Torrenta's `main` reads the file once as well, on the main thread, for its
    tray and badge settings.

- **PERF-17 · SHOULD.** The app ships precompiled stylesheets (`.bss`). The AOT cache, the other half of a fast
  start, is [REL-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-10).
  - *Check (code):* the build converts the app's `.css` files to `.bss`, and the packaged app carries them.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`scripts/css2bss.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/css2bss.java), run by the `css-to-bss` execution in [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml). The app template's `dist` profile runs its [`ui/StyleCompiler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleCompiler.java) over the built stylesheets, which writes a `.bss` beside
    each `.css`, and [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) loads the `.bss` where there is one ([`StyleCompilerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleCompilerTest.java)). No other app converts its
    own stylesheets yet.

### Measure, don't guess

- **PERF-18 · SHOULD.** Every change on a hot path says what it costs in its pull request: added FX-thread work,
  allocation per keystroke or scroll, extra layout passes, memory. "Negligible" is an answer; no answer is not.
  - *Check (by hand):* read the app's recent pull requests that touch a hot path.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) (its opening paragraph).

- **PERF-19 · SHOULD.** Start-up is measured by a script that takes the median of several cold launches, and by
  phase marks in the app.
  - *Check (code):* the repository has the script, and `main` and the first paint record phase marks.
  - *Reference:* `scripts/measure-startup.sh` in Editora, Termina, Mirada and the app template, whose marks are recorded
    by [`StartupMarks.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/StartupMarks.java) from `main` and the first paint; Editora [`perf/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/perf/Startup.java).

- **PERF-20 · SHOULD.** The app can sample its FX thread when something stalls.
  - *Check (code):* an environment variable or property turns on a sampler of the FX thread's stack.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`perf/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/perf/Startup.java) (`EDITORA_PERF_SAMPLE=1`, with `EDITORA_PERF=1`); Mirada [`perf/FxSampler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/perf/FxSampler.java)
    (`MIRADA_PERF_SAMPLE=1`); the app template's [`ui/FxSampler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FxSampler.java)
    (`-Dexampleapp.fxSampler=<ms>` or `EXAMPLEAPP_FX_SAMPLER`, logging the FX thread's stack on a stall; [`FxSamplerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FxSamplerTest.java)).

- **PERF-21 · SHOULD.** Each hot path that once regressed keeps a headless test.
  - *Check (test):* the fix for a hot-path regression adds a headless test that fails on the old code.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MinimapDeferredRenderFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MinimapDeferredRenderFxTest.java).

- **PERF-22 · SHOULD.** A suspected regression gets a number before and after, from temporary `System.nanoTime`
  instrumentation if nothing better exists.
  - *Check (by hand):* the pull request that fixes it states both numbers.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md).

## Keyboard first (KBD)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/: Commands, the Command Palette, keymaps, focus and accessibility.

### Commands

- **KBD-01 · MUST.** Every user-facing action is a command (an id, a title and a runnable) registered in one
  command registry (Editora's `Command` and `CommandRegistry`).
  - *Check (code):* what a menu item, a toolbar button, a palette row or a key binding does is a registered command:
    the control runs the command's id through the registry, or calls what the command's runnable calls. No button,
    menu row or key handler does work no command can reach.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`command/Command.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/Command.java), [`command/CommandRegistry.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/CommandRegistry.java). Editora doesn't hold the rule
    everywhere yet: the Clear button of its Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) empties the log in its own
    handler, and the Previous Run and Save Output buttons of its build console ([`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)) work the
    same way, with no command behind any of the three. Termina doesn't either. These buttons, among others, do their
    work in handlers of their own with no command behind them: Clear in its Message Log
    ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)), Refresh, Copy, Export and Clear in its Debug Log ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)), and
    Import theme in Settings ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingsWindow.java)).

- **KBD-02 · SHOULD.** Command ids are dotted and grouped by area, as in `file.open`, `view.toggleStatusBar`
  and `help.reportProblem`. A rule that names a command's id requires that id; these three are examples.
  - *Check (code):* every registered id is two or more names joined by dots, and the first is the area the command
    belongs to: `file.open`, and with a sub-area `git.log.checkout`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java).

- **KBD-03 · MUST.** A command's title comes from `command.<id>` and its one-line palette description from
  `command.<id>.desc` in the message catalogs.
  - *Why:* a registered command is then localized and discoverable without extra work.
  - *Check (code):* every registered command has a `command.<id>` and a `command.<id>.desc` key in the message
    catalogs, and the registry reads its title and description from them. A catalog parity test that walks the
    registered commands and fails on a missing key is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`CommandSweepFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/CommandSweepFxTest.java) (`everyCommandIsLocalizedAndRuns`) and Mirada's
    [`CommandCatalogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/CommandCatalogTest.java) (`everyCommandHasItsTitleAndDescriptionInTheCatalog`) walk the registered commands.
    Editora [`i18n/messages.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages.properties); its [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`everyCommandTitleHasAMatchingDescription`)
    walks the catalog instead, so it finds a title with no description but not a registered command with neither.

- **KBD-04 · SHOULD.** A command that cannot run in the current context is shown grayed, with a tooltip that says
  why, not hidden.
  - *Check (code):* the palette and menus list a disabled command with a reason, rather than filtering it out.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java) (`paletteEnabled`, `disabledReason`). The app template's menu
    rows of a command that can't run stay, grayed, with the reason as their tooltip ([`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java), `showAvailability`;
    [`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java), `anUnavailableRowStaysAndSaysWhy`), and its palette lists such a command with the reason.

### Command Palette

- **KBD-05 · MUST.** The Command Palette opens with `M-x` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl+Shift+P` (`Cmd+Shift+P` on
  macOS) in the others; the IntelliJ keymap may use IntelliJ's own Find Action chord, `Ctrl+Shift+A` (`Cmd+Shift+A`),
  instead. An app with one key table and no Emacs keymap, which is a terminal app's own keymap ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-09)) or
  the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files, counts as one of the others: it binds `Ctrl+Shift+P`
  (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS). An app that ships no keymap files owes this chord and fails KBD-09 all the same: KBD-09
  requires the files of every app.
  - *Check (code):* each bundled keymap binds that chord to the palette command, and so does the one key table of an
    app that has no keymap files. An app whose chord opens the palette from a handler, with no palette command
    registered, passes this rule and fails [PAL-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/#pal-01) for the missing command.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/emacs.json) (`M-x`), [`cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.json) and [`vscode.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/vscode.json) (`C-S-p`), [`cua.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.mac.json)
    (`Cmd-S-p`), all to `palette.show`; [`intellij.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/intellij.json) binds `C-S-a`. Termina's one keymap binds
    `Shortcut+Shift+P`, which is `Ctrl+Shift+P` in [`keymap.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.json) and `Cmd+Shift+P` in [`keymap.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.mac.json), and nux,
    which ships no keymap file, binds the same chord in [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java). Torrenta and Modula don't yet: Torrenta's one key
    table opens the palette with `Alt+X` alone ([`ui/Chords.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Chords.java)), and Modula's key filter tests for `Ctrl` on
    every OS, so its chord is `Ctrl+Shift+P` on macOS too ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)).

- **KBD-06 · SHOULD.** The palette matches fuzzily over the command's title and over the words of its id or its
  keywords; the description is shown, not matched. A query that names a command's title outranks a fuzzy hit. Each
  row shows the command's binding in the active keymap. See the
  [Command Palette template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/).
  - *Check (code):* the palette's matcher matches the query fuzzily against each command's title and finds a command
    by a word of its id or a keyword that its title doesn't carry; a query that spells a command's title ranks that
    command above the fuzzy hits; the description is drawn and never matched, and each row draws the binding the
    active keymap gives the command. A ranking test that asserts the order is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`orderedMatches`), [`search/FuzzyMatch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/search/FuzzyMatch.java). It scores the
    title first; when the title doesn't match, the id's namespace word as a keyword ([`Command.keywords`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/Command.java)); then the
    names IntelliJ and VS Code give the command ([`command/OtherIdeNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/OtherIdeNames.java)). It doesn't match the rest of the id
    or the description, which is shown under the list. [`CommandPaletteRankTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPaletteRankTest.java) holds the order
    (`aCommandIsFoundByItsNamespaceWhenItsTitleDoesNotCarryIt`, `aKeywordMatchRanksBelowEveryTitleMatch`, and for a
    typed title `anExactTitleLeadsAnotherCommandsAlias` and `aWholeOneWordTitleLeads`). The app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) (`rank`, with `idWords`) matches the title fuzzily
    and the id's words, never the description, and puts a title that holds the query first ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java),
    `ranksTitlesFirstAndSkipsUnavailableRows`).

- **KBD-07 · MUST.** The palette and every picker (a card that lists choices to filter and pick one from:
  [QOPEN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#qopen-01)) are in-scene overlays in the window's root `StackPane`, never a
  `javafx.stage.Popup`.
  - *Why:* on Windows a Popup does not reliably take OS keyboard focus, and the whole app can stop receiving
    keystrokes.
  - *Check (code):* the palette and every picker add their node to the root `StackPane`; none creates a `Popup`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java), the one host installed in the scene's root `StackPane`, which shows the
    palette ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java)), the picker ([`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java)) and the picker's relatives
    ([QOPEN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#qopen-12)).

### Keymaps

- **KBD-09 · MUST.** Except in a terminal app, Emacs and CUA keymaps ship as JSON resources, `emacs.json` and
  `cua.json`, CUA with a `cua.mac.json` variant where Cmd replaces Ctrl. A terminal's keys belong to the program it
  runs (`C-a`, `M-x` reach the shell), so a terminal app ships one keymap of its own instead, `keymap.json` and
  `keymap.mac.json`, binding its commands to chords programs don't use. Neither file binds a plain `Ctrl` or `Alt`
  (`Option` on macOS) with a letter: off macOS that leaves `Ctrl+Shift+T`, not `Ctrl+T`, and on macOS `Cmd+T`,
  since no program in the terminal receives `Cmd`.
  - *Why:* an Emacs keymap in a terminal would take the shell's own keys away from it: `Ctrl+W` deletes a word,
    `Ctrl+C` interrupts, `Alt+F` and `Alt+B` move by word. The shell reads the same keys on macOS, where `Option`
    with a letter also types a character.
  - *Check (code):* `emacs.json`, `cua.json` and `cua.mac.json` are in the app's resources. In a terminal app,
    `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json` are there instead, and no default binding in either file is `Ctrl` alone or
    `Alt` alone with a letter. Read each chord as the OS reads it: a modifier that stands for the OS's own shortcut
    key (JavaFX's `Shortcut`, as Termina writes it) is `Ctrl` in `keymap.json` and `Cmd` in `keymap.mac.json`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps);
    Termina's [`keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps), whose [`KeymapTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/KeymapTest.java)
    (`offMacOsAnApplicationChordNeverTakesPlainCtrlAndALetter`) holds the `Ctrl` half off macOS; no test holds the
    `Alt` half or reads `keymap.mac.json`, where every chord carries `Cmd` today.

- **KBD-10 · SHOULD.** Except in a terminal app ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-09)), an app also ships IntelliJ, VS Code and Sublime
  keymaps as JSON resources beside its Emacs and CUA keymaps: `intellij.json`, `vscode.json` and `sublime.json`,
  each with its `.mac.json` variant.
  - *Check (code):* `intellij`, `vscode` and `sublime` `.json` and `.mac.json` files are in the resources. An app
    that ships a terminal's keymap, `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json` with no `emacs.json` and no `cua.json`
    ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-09)), needs none of them.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; has() { find src/main/resources -name "$1" | grep -q .; }; if has keymap.json && has keymap.mac.json && ! has emacs.json && ! has cua.json; then exit 0; fi; ! for k in intellij vscode sublime; do for f in "$k.json" "$k.mac.json"; do has "$f" || echo "missing $f"; done; done | grep .`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps). Termina ships the terminal's two files only
    ([`keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps)). The app template ships all five, each IDE keymap with its `.mac.json` (`PRESETS` in
    [`command/Keymap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/command/Keymap.java)). Mirada ships Emacs and CUA and none of these three yet; Torrenta, Modula
    and nux ship no keymap file.

- **KBD-21 · MUST.** A keymap's `.mac.json` variant binds the same commands as the keymap it varies. A chord may
  differ, to put `Cmd` where the other has `Ctrl`, to follow the macOS keymap of the editor it copies, or where
  macOS keeps the chord for itself (`Cmd+Space`, `Cmd+Tab`). See [Same on every OS](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/).
  - *Why:* a command with no chord on one OS is a command that user never finds from the keyboard.
  - *Check (code):* each keymap file and its `.mac.json` variant bind the same set of command ids: no command is bound
    in one and missing from the other. An app that ships no keymap files has no pair to compare and fails with
    [KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-09). A test that loads both and compares the commands they bind is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`KeymapsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/command/KeymapsTest.java) (`guiKeymapsBindSameCommandSetOnBothPlatforms`), Termina's [`KeymapTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/KeymapTest.java)
    (`bothPlatformsBindTheSameCommands`) and the app template's [`KeybindingsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/command/KeybindingsTest.java)
    (`cuaHasAMacVariantWhereCmdReplacesCtrl`). Mirada's [`cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/cua.json) and [`cua.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/cua.mac.json) bind the same commands, with no
    test that compares the two.

- **KBD-11 · MUST.** Keymaps are applied in layers: base keymap → user overrides → plugin keymaps → the user's own
  bindings again. An app without plugins has the first two.
  - *Why:* the user always has the last word, and a plugin can still use a chord the user freed.
  - *Check (code):* one place applies the layers in that order.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/KeymapLayers.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/KeymapLayers.java).

- **KBD-12 · SHOULD.** A keymap editor in Settings lists every command with its chord, is searchable, and warns of
  conflicts.
  - *Check (by hand):* open Settings → Keymap, search, and bind a chord that is taken.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsKeymapsPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsKeymapsPage.java); conflicts from [`KeybindingEdits.conflicts`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeybindingEdits.java), and the
    defaults a chord would take from [`EditorSettingsCoordinator.takenDefaults`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/EditorSettingsCoordinator.java).

- **KBD-13 · SHOULD.** No command's chord is written into translated text. Every other label that shows a chord (a
  hint, the palette, the status bar) shows the binding from the active keymap; tooltips are
  [TBAR-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-03) and menu rows [MENU-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/menus/#menu-15). Fixed keys of a control
  (Enter, Tab, Esc, arrows) and keys meant for another program may be written.
  - *Check (code):* no message catalog value names a command's chord (`Ctrl+`, `Cmd+`, `C-x`, `M-x`); chords are
    rendered by one formatter.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`command/ChordFormat.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/ChordFormat.java), the one place a binding is rendered. Editora's
    `command.edit.universalArgument` title still carries `C-u`.

- **KBD-14 · SHOULD.** A multi-key prefix (`C-x …`) shows a which-key style hint listing the possible next keys.
  - *Check (by hand):* press `C-x` in the Emacs keymap and wait.
  - *Reference:* no app lists the next keys yet. Editora echoes only the pending prefix (`C-x -`) in the status bar
    ([`command/KeyDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeyDispatcher.java)).

### Focus and accessibility

- **KBD-15 · MUST.** Every interactive control is reachable with Tab and operable with Space or Enter. A control is
  the exception when the keyboard does what it does another way: the buttons of a toolbar stay out of the Tab order
  ([TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02), which says what a toolbar is: a bar of labeled buttons is not one,
  and its buttons are held to this rule), and the find-bar and filter controls that
  [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-16) names may leave it. See [Accessibility](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/accessibility/).
  - *Why:* a control that Tab can't reach is one a keyboard-only or screen-reader user can't use at all.
  - *Check (by hand):* first in the source, find every control the keyboard cannot focus: one the app takes out of the
    Tab order (`setFocusTraversable(false)` in the code, `-fx-focus-traversable: false` in a stylesheet), and a label
    or a pane that acts on a click. The keyboard does all that each one does another way: it is a button of a toolbar
    as [The toolbar](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#the-toolbar) defines one ([TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02);
    a bar of labeled buttons, such as nux's, is not one), a find-bar or filter control that
    [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-16) lets leave the Tab order (one that fails FIND-16, such as an option's
    toggle that no command toggles, fails here too), a list whose text field moves its selection with the arrow keys,
    or a control whose every action, the rows of its right-click menu included, a registered command also runs. A
    control only the mouse can work fails the rule, and the source alone shows it. Then in the running app, Tab
    reaches every other control of each window and dialog, and Space or Enter works it.
  - *Reference:* the app template, where each control the keyboard cannot focus has its other way: the status bar's
    echo area, error count and update notice run commands (`view.messageLog`, `help.openNewRelease`:
    [`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StatusBar.java)), its toolbar's buttons are [TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02)'s
    (`Icons.toolbarButton` in [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Icons.java)), a tool window's header buttons run commands
    ([`ui/ToolWindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)), the find bars' buttons are [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-16)'s
    ([`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java)), and the picker's list is moved from its field ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)). Editora doesn't
    hold the rule everywhere yet: the Clear button of its Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) and the Previous
    Run and Save Output buttons of its build console ([`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)) are out of the Tab order with no
    command and no key behind them. Modula doesn't either: it takes every control of its window out of the Tab order
    ([`RadioPane.keepOutOfFocus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)) and gives most of what they do a key or a palette row, but a preset's Rename and
    Remove are rows of its chip's right-click menu alone ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)). Termina doesn't either: the
    regular-expression toggle of its find bar is out of the Tab order, and no command and no key toggles it
    ([`ui/SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java); [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-16) fails for it too).

- **KBD-16 · MUST.** Every button, toggle, menu button, link, combo box, check box, radio button and text field shows
  the focus ring when the keyboard focuses it. The ring is one layer of `:focus-visible` rules in the app stylesheet,
  after every rule that sets a border or background on the same controls, since rules of equal specificity are decided
  by order. Its color and contrast are [ICON-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-12).
  - *Why:* a keyboard user who can't see where focus is can't use the window; the ring's color is a MUST, and so is
    drawing it.
  - *Check (code):* the app stylesheet holds the ring as one block of `:focus-visible` rules that covers each of these
    kinds of control the app uses (buttons, toggles, menu buttons, links, combo boxes, check boxes, radio buttons,
    text fields), and no rule after the block, of the same or higher specificity, sets again what the block sets on
    those controls (the border; on a text field, the background insets). A test that tabs to each control family and
    asserts the ring is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*, one layer for every control), held by
    [`FocusRingFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FocusRingFxTest.java), which tabs to each control family. Termina's [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) and Mirada's
    [`mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css) end with a layer of the same kind; neither app has a test that tabs to a control.

- **KBD-22 · SHOULD.** The focus ring is 2 px wide at the default zoom and sits just outside the control with a
  1 px gap: a border with negative insets, which adds nothing to the control's own, so focusing a control never moves
  the layout. Two kinds of control draw it inside instead, at the same 2 px and still without moving anything: a
  text field, whose own focus border is widened, and a control flush with the window's edge, where a ring outside
  would be cut off.
  - *Why:* a ring drawn on the control's own border is lost on a flat or filled button, and one that takes room
    makes the row jump as Tab moves along it. A text field already draws an accent border on focus, so a second
    ring around it would be one too many.
  - *Check (code):* in the `:focus-visible` rules of [KBD-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-16), the one for the controls that take the
    outside ring (buttons, toggles, menu buttons, links, combo boxes, the boxes of check boxes and radio buttons, as
    many of them as the app has) sets `-fx-border-width: 2` and `-fx-border-insets: -3`; the one for text fields
    widens the field's focus border to 2 px instead
    (`-fx-background-insets: 0, 2px`); and a rule that draws the ring inside a control at the window's edge keeps the
    2 px width and takes the room back out of the control's padding.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*), Termina's [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) and Mirada's [`mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css): the
    same outside ring, and the same text-field rule (Mirada's covers text areas too). Editora alone has the second
    exception: `.tool-stripe-button:focus-visible` draws the ring at `-fx-border-insets: 1` and gives 3 px of
    padding back, since the stripes sit against the window's edge. The app template's
    [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) has the same outside ring and text-field rule; its check boxes and radio buttons take the ring around the
    whole control, label included, not around the box alone.

- **KBD-18 · SHOULD.** A row that turns a setting on or off (in Settings, a panel or a dialog) uses a switch the
  keyboard operates: it takes focus, Space toggles it, and its accessible role is `TOGGLE_BUTTON`.
  - *Why:* a bare AtlantaFX `ToggleSwitch` is mouse-only.
  - *Check (code):* every row that turns a setting on or off uses a switch that takes focus, toggles on Space and sets
    `AccessibleRole.TOGGLE_BUTTON` (Editora has one class for it, `SettingSwitch`); a row that uses AtlantaFX's
    `ToggleSwitch` as it comes fails.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingSwitch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingSwitch.java).

## Accessibility (ACC)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/accessibility/: What a screen reader, a keyboard-only user and a user who turns motion off need from every app, and where each is a rule.

### Rules

- **ACC-01 · MUST.** Every control a person can reach with Tab or the mouse has an accessible name: its own text, a
  `Label` whose `labelFor` is the control, or `setAccessibleText`. A row drawn from a graphic (a `CustomMenuItem`, a
  list cell that lays out its own nodes) carries its text too. A test holds it.
  - *Why:* a screen reader announces an unnamed control as "button", or says nothing.
  - *Check (test):* an FX test opens each window and dialog and fails on a control (a button, a toggle, a field, a
    combo box or any other `Control` a person can focus or click, in the Tab order or out of it) that has no text,
    no accessible text and no label pointing at it, and on a list cell or menu row that reads as nothing. JavaFX
    names a `CustomMenuItem` row from its content's accessible text, and a cell from its text or its graphic's, so a
    row that lays out its own nodes sets `setAccessibleText` on them.
  - *Reference:* Editora names its controls area by area
    ([`NamedControlsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/NamedControlsFxTest.java)),
    and sets each row's text on the macOS system menu bar. Its in-window command rows, each a `CustomMenuItem` that draws an icon,
    a title and a chord ([`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java)), carry no text and no accessible text yet;
    its submenus keep their own. The app template has the test that sweeps every window for every control:
    [`NamedControlsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/NamedControlsFxTest.java) (`everyControlInEveryWindowHasAName`, and
    `everyMenuRowReadsAsItsTitleAndWearsAGlyph` for the menu rows, which [`AppMenus.inWindowRow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) names from their title
    and chord) opens the main window and its panels, the find bars, the Message Log, Settings, About, the Pauta
    window, the Debug Log and Report a Problem, the palette, the switcher, a question and a prompt. Termina's [`IconOnlyButtonsFxTest.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/IconOnlyButtonsFxTest.java) comes nearest: it opens the main window, the menus, Settings and About and
    fails an icon-only button with no name, and no other kind of control. Torrenta's one call to
    `setAccessibleText` is in a helper ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Icons.java), `name`) that names every button of its main toolbar and the
    Search view's Clear button, and no other control; Modula never calls it.

- **ACC-02 · SHOULD.** A control the app builds from panes or draws itself says what it is and does what its role
  offers: `setAccessibleRole` with the role it acts as (`BUTTON`, `TOGGLE_BUTTON`, `LIST_VIEW`, `TREE_ITEM`), its
  state answered from `queryAccessibleAttribute` (selected, expanded, checked), `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged`
  when the state changes, and the role's actions (`FIRE`, `EXPAND`, `COLLAPSE`) handled in `executeAccessibleAction`.
  - *Why:* without a role, a screen reader can't tell a status-bar segment that opens a picker from a label; and it
    presses a control through its action, not a mouse click, so a `BUTTON` that ignores `FIRE` can be found but not
    used.
  - *Check (code):* every `Pane`, `Region`, `Label` or `Canvas` that handles a click or a key sets an accessible
    role and overrides `executeAccessibleAction` for that role's actions.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingSwitch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingSwitch.java) (the `TOGGLE_BUTTON` role; it handles `FIRE`
    only) and [`ui/MapAccessibleRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRows.java) (`FIRE`, `EXPAND` and `COLLAPSE` on each row). Its status-bar segments ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java)) take the
    `BUTTON` role but don't handle `FIRE` yet.

- **ACC-03 · SHOULD.** An app that paints content on a `Canvas` (a map, a strip of images, a terminal grid) gives it
  to the screen reader: an accessible text that sums it up and, where a person moves through items in it, one
  accessible node for each item on screen.
  - *Check (code):* the canvas, or the node that stands for it, sets an accessible text, and where a person moves
    through items it exposes a node with a role and a name for each item on screen. A test that reads the
    accessible text, or the roles and names of those nodes, is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MapAccessibleRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRows.java) (the Project Map's rows on screen, as `TREE_ITEM`
    nodes under a `TREE_VIEW`), read by [`MapAccessibleRowsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRowsFxTest.java).

- **ACC-04 · SHOULD.** Motion follows the OS: while `Platform.getPreferences().isReducedMotion()` is true, an
  animation jumps to its end, and a change to the setting applies at once.
  - *Why:* sliding and fading can make a person dizzy or sick, and they turned motion off in the OS for that reason.
  - *Check (code):* every `Transition`, `Timeline` or `AnimationTimer` that moves, fades or flashes part of the UI
    starts through one helper that reads `reducedMotionProperty()`.
  - *Reference:* no app reads the setting yet. The app template animates nothing, so it has nothing to judge: its
    timelines and pauses are timers that move, fade or flash no part of the UI (the Output sample's lines in
    [`ui/SamplePanels.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SamplePanels.java), the debounce of [`ui/Debounce.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Debounce.java), the sync interval and the update check's delay).
    Mirada fades its on-screen controls in and out
    ([`ui/OnScreenControls.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/OnScreenControls.java), a `FadeTransition`), and Editora's Project Map flashes a revealed row for 900 ms
    ([`ui/MapSurface.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapSurface.java), an `AnimationTimer`); neither reads a motion setting.

- **ACC-05 · SHOULD.** Color is never the only signal: a state shown in color (an error, a changed line, a status)
  also shows a word, a glyph or a shape.
  - *Why:* about one man in twelve can't tell red from green.
  - *Check (by hand):* look at a grayscale screenshot of each window and find every state still told apart.
  - *Reference:* Editora's echo area colors an error and also says what failed ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java); [WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-01)). The app
    template gives a file's Git status its letter beside the color, on a tab ([`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabHeaders.java); [`TabsAndPanelsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsFxTest.java),
    `aTabShowsItsGitStatusAsALetter`) and on the file's row in its Documents window ([`ui/SamplePanels.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SamplePanels.java)).

- **ACC-06 · SHOULD.** In an app whose window has more than one region (the content and at least one panel beside
  it), a command moves focus to the next region, another moves it to the previous one, and every keymap binds
  both.
  - *Why:* Tab walks through every control inside a region; with several panels open, a keyboard user needs a way to
    jump between them.
  - *Check (code):* the two commands are registered and bound in each bundled keymap.
  - *Reference:* the app template's `window.focusNextRegion` and `window.focusPreviousRegion` ([`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java), `focusRegion`
    in [`ui/ToolWindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)), on `F6` and `Shift+F6` in its CUA keymaps and `C-x o` and `C-x S-o` in Emacs, bound in
    every keymap it ships ([`TabsAndPanelsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsFxTest.java), `theRegionCommandsWalkTheDocumentsAndTheOpenToolWindows`). Editora's `window.other` ("Cycle focus between the editor and tool windows",
    [`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)), one command that cycles, bound only in the Emacs keymap (`C-x o`,
    [`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/emacs.json)). `F6`, the Windows convention, is taken in
    every other Editora keymap: CUA and VS Code bind it to `debug.pause`, IntelliJ to `lsp.move` and Sublime to
    `view.toggleSpellCheck`.

- **ACC-07 · SHOULD.** Before a release, a person makes a pass with the screen reader on Windows and on macOS: with
  Narrator and with VoiceOver, open the Command Palette, run a command, and move through Settings, hearing each
  control's name and role. It is a step of its own in `docs/release.md` ([REPO-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/repository/#repo-07)): the
  smoke test of [REL-29](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-29) is a CI step, with nobody there to listen.
  - *Check (by hand):* `docs/release.md` has the step, naming Narrator and VoiceOver, and someone made the pass for
    this release. The file settles the first half: with no such step the rule is unmet, whoever listened. The pass
    itself is a person's to record, as a `checked` entry that carries the app's `version`
    ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-18)).
  - *Reference:* no app yet. No app's `docs/release.md` names either screen reader, and Modula and nux have no
    `docs/release.md`.

- **ACC-08 · SHOULD.** In an overlay list that keeps focus in its text field (the Command Palette, a picker:
  [QOPEN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#qopen-01)), the row the arrow keys select is announced, with its state: the list
  tells the screen reader its focused item moved (`notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(FOCUS_ITEM)`), and a row that
  can't run says so in its accessible text.
  - *Why:* the arrows move the highlight, not the focus, so a screen reader stays on the text field and reads
    nothing as the user moves through the list.
  - *Check (code):* the code that moves the selection calls
    `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(AccessibleAttribute.FOCUS_ITEM)` on the list, the list answers `FOCUS_ITEM`
    with the selected row, and a row that can't run says so in its accessible text.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java), behind its palette and pickers: `select` moves the list's focus
    model and calls `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(FOCUS_ITEM)`, and a row's accessible text is its title, its
    keys and, for a row that can't run, the reason. Editora's palette rows are graphics with no text
    ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java)).

- **ACC-09 · SHOULD.** In Windows' high-contrast mode the app switches to a high-contrast theme, and back when the
  mode ends: it follows `Platform.getPreferences()`'s `Windows.SPI.HighContrast`.
  - *Why:* JavaFX applies its own high-contrast stylesheet only over its built-in Modena theme, which AtlantaFX
    replaces, so without this the app ignores a setting the person turned on to read the screen at all.
  - *Check (code):* a listener on the preference switches the theme, and the theme list has a high-contrast theme.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`WINDOWS_HIGH_CONTRAST`, a listener on `Platform.getPreferences()` that applies its
    `HIGH_CONTRAST` theme while the mode is on and the chosen one when it ends), held by [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java)
    (`theOsHighContrastModeWinsWhileItIsOn`, `theHighContrastThemeReadsAtSevenToOne`). No app does it yet.

## Window shell (WIN)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/: Status bar, themes, title bar, dialogs, Welcome, About, window state, zoom and quit.

- **WIN-01 · MUST.** The main window has a status bar, shown by default; the user may hide it. Its left side is the
  *echo area*: one line of feedback for the last action, errors in red and warnings in amber. Clicking it opens the
  Message Log ([DIAG-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-01)).
  - *Check (code):* the main window builds a status bar that is visible unless the user hid it; the echo label
    switches between an error and a warning style class, and its click handler runs the Message Log command.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java) (`status-echo-error`, `status-echo-warn`; a click runs
    `view.messageLog`) and the [Message Log template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/message-log/). Editora hides and shows the bar
    with `view.toggleStatusBar` and a setting, and Zen mode hides it ([`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java), `statusBar`). Termina doesn't
    meet the rule yet: its status bar is a setting that starts off ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), `showStatusBar`).

- **WIN-03 · MUST.** In an app with a menu bar, the menu bar sits in the title bar by default on Windows and Linux:
  JavaFX 27's `HeaderBar` with `StageStyle.EXTENDED` carries the menu, and a setting that starts on lets the user
  fall back to a decorated window. On macOS the menus are in the system menu bar (`useSystemMenuBar`), and the window
  is decorated, or extended with a header that holds no menus.
  - *Why:* the family looks the same on every OS only if every app starts with the same title bar; an app that
    ships it off looks like another family.
  - *Check (code):* on Windows and Linux the main stage is created `StageStyle.EXTENDED` with a `HeaderBar` that
    holds the menu bar, and the setting that falls back to a decorated window defaults to on (in the title bar); on
    macOS the menu bar sets `useSystemMenuBar`, and a header, where the window has one, holds no menus.
  - *Reference:* the app template ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java), `titleBarMenus = true`, read by
    [`Chrome.usesHeaderBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Chrome.java)). Editora ([`ui/ExtendedWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ExtendedWindow.java), [`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java)), Torrenta
    and Termina have the setting but start it off. Mirada has no setting: its [`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) is a `HeaderBar` on a
    `StageStyle.EXTENDED` stage wherever JavaFX supports one, on macOS too. Its header holds the file name and
    buttons, the main menu's among them, and no menu bar; on macOS [`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java) puts the menus in the system
    menu bar. Modula and nux have no menu bar.

- **WIN-04 · SHOULD.** Native dialogs go through one helper that attaches the app stylesheet. The UI font reaches
  every scene, a dialog's included, by [ICON-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-01).
  - *Why:* a dialog is its own scene and does not inherit the window's stylesheet.
  - *Check (code):* every `Alert` and `Dialog` the app builds passes through the helper.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/Dialogs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Dialogs.java) ([`Dialogs.styled`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Dialogs.java)), which attaches `app.css` only. The UI font reaches an
    Editora dialog another way: [`App.installUiFont`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) adds `ui-font.css` to every window's scene
    ([ICON-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-01)).

- **WIN-11 · MUST.** A dialog's buttons are in the same order on every OS, with Cancel to the left of every action, as
  the [Confirm dialog](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/) draws them (Cancel, Save and Discard where there are three:
  [CONF-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-05)): the dialog's `ButtonBar` gets one fixed order, never JavaFX's
  default for the OS. See [Same on every OS](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/).
  - *Why:* JavaFX orders a `ButtonBar` by the OS it runs on (`BUTTON_ORDER_WINDOWS`, `_MAC_OS`, `_LINUX`), so the
    same confirmation puts its action on the left on Windows and on the right on macOS and Linux.
  - *Check (code):* the dialog helper ([WIN-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-04)), or each dialog, calls `setButtonOrder` on the dialog
    pane's `ButtonBar` with one order string, the same on every OS, in which `C` (`CANCEL_CLOSE`) comes before the
    letter of every action button the dialogs use (`O` for `OK_DONE`, `Y`, `N`, `A`, `U` for `OTHER`).
    `BUTTON_ORDER_WINDOWS` on every OS fails: it puts `Y`, `N` and `O` before `C`.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`ui/Dialogs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Dialogs.java) (`BUTTON_ORDER`, `L_HE+CUYNBXIAO_R`, set by `styled`, which
    every dialog of the template goes through), held by [`DialogsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/DialogsFxTest.java)
    (`everyDialogHasOneButtonOrderAndCatalogWords`). Editora's Git confirmations give their buttons the `OK_DONE`
    and `CANCEL_CLOSE` roles and leave the order to JavaFX.

- **WIN-08 · SHOULD.** The main window's size, position and maximized state are restored on the next launch, and
  in an app that opens documents or sessions, so are the items that were open. `--no-session` skipping the restore
  is [CLI-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-04).
  - *Check (code):* closing the window saves its size, position and maximized flag, and the open items in an app
    that has them, and the next launch reads them back and applies them. A test that saves the state and reads it
    back is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/WorkspaceState.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/WorkspaceState.java) (`windowX` … `windowMaximized`),
    [`ui/WindowSessionCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowSessionCoordinator.java), [`App.noSessionFlag`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java); tests [`AppArgsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/AppArgsTest.java),
    [`NoSessionStartupFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/NoSessionStartupFxTest.java) and, for the window's geometry, [`WindowManagerLaunchFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/WindowManagerLaunchFxTest.java)
    (`aWindowComesBackAtTheSizeAndPlaceItsSessionRecorded`, `aWindowThatWasMaximizedComesBackMaximized`), which
    restore a window from a saved `workspace-state.json`. No Editora test saves the geometry and reads it back. The app template does both: `saveWindowState` in
    [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) writes the size, place, maximized state and the open documents to `session.json`, and the next launch
    restores them ([`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java); [`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theOpenDocumentsComeBackFromTheSessionFile`).

- **WIN-09 · SHOULD.** In an app with content to zoom (text, an image, a terminal), it zooms from the keyboard
  (`Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0`, with `Cmd` on macOS; `=` is the key that carries `+`), kept across launches.
  The UI zoom is [WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-12).
  - *Check (code):* the content's zoom in, out and reset are commands bound in every keymap, and the zoom level is a
    saved setting.
  - *Reference:* Editora `view.textZoomIn`, `view.textZoomOut` and `view.textZoomReset`, kept in
    [`Settings.fontZoom`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java) and bound to `C-=`, `C--` and `C-0`
    ([`keymaps/cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.json)); Termina's `zoomIn`, `zoomOut` and `actualSize`, on `Shortcut+Equals`, `Shortcut+Minus` and
    `Shortcut+0` ([`keymaps/keymap.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.json)), kept in `font.zoom` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java)); the app template's
    `view.zoomIn`, `view.zoomOut` and `view.zoomReset` for its documents' text, bound to `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` (`Cmd` on macOS) in every keymap it ships
    and kept in `textZoom` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java); [`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theDocumentsTextZoomsOnItsOwn`).

- **WIN-12 · MUST.** The app has a UI zoom: one setting scales the whole chrome, the menus
  ([MENU-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/menus/#menu-16)), toolbar, tabs and status bar included. It applies at once, is kept across
  launches, and three commands zoom it in, out and back to the default. In an app with content of its own to zoom
  (an editor's text, a terminal's grid, an image) `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` (`Cmd` on macOS) stay with the
  content zoom ([WIN-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-09)) and this rule fixes no chord for the UI zoom's commands; in an app without,
  those chords are the UI zoom's.
  - *Why:* a person who needs larger text gets it everywhere, and the menus can only follow a zoom that exists.
  - *Check (code):* the chrome's font sizes come from one root size the setting changes, and its fixed sizes are
    multiplied by the zoom, not written as absolute pixels. A change to the setting restyles every open window with
    no restart, and the value is saved with the settings and read back at start-up. Three registered commands zoom
    it in, out and back to the default. The rule names no ids for them: they are the app's own. In an app with a
    content zoom they are three more commands, with ids that are not the content zoom's (Mirada's `view.zoomIn` and
    Termina's `zoomIn` zoom the content), and the keymaps bind `=`, `-` and `0` with `Ctrl` (`Cmd` on macOS) to the
    content zoom's commands; in an app without, to the UI zoom's.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`ui/UiZoom.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/UiZoom.java) and [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java)
    (`zoom`): one setting, `uiZoom` in [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java), scales every pixel size of the stylesheets, the root
    font size among them, and the sizes the code fixes are bound to the zoom; a change restyles every open window
    at once. Its commands are `view.uiZoomIn`, `view.uiZoomOut` and `view.uiZoomReset` ([`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java)), on
    `Ctrl+Alt+=`, `Ctrl+Alt+-` and `Ctrl+Alt+0` (`Cmd+Alt` on macOS) in its CUA keymaps, which leave `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` to its documents' text zoom ([WIN-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-09)); [`UiZoomTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/UiZoomTest.java) holds the scaling. Editora, Termina and Mirada zoom their
    content only (`view.textZoomIn`, `zoomIn`, `view.zoomIn`), and Editora writes its menu font as absolute pixels ([`MainMenuBar.UI_FONT_SIZE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java), `.context-menu`
    in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css)). Torrenta, Modula and nux have no zoom command.

- **WIN-13 · MUST.** Every quit entry point an app has runs one quit method: the Quit row and the `app.quit` command
  ([WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) says which of them an app must have), and the system's own Quit, which on macOS is the
  application menu's and the Dock's. That method asks what the [Confirm dialog](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/) rules
  require ([CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01)), closes open dialogs and runs the save the app runs
  when its window closes, so quitting loses nothing a close would have kept; what an app keeps across launches is
  [WIN-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-08). A tray's Quit is [TRAY-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tray-and-background/#tray-04).
  - *Why:* a second way out skips what the first one does: the question about unsaved work, the saved window, or,
    in a tray app, the quit itself. Quitting from inside a dialog's nested event loop has aborted the JVM.
  - *Check (code):* one quit method. The Quit row and the quit command run it, where the app has them (an app with
    neither fails [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14), not this rule), and on macOS the system's Quit reaches it. JavaFX turns the
    application menu's and the Dock's Quit into a close request on every window
    (`GlassStage.requestClosingAllWindows`) unless the app catches Glass's quit action (`handleQuitAction`), so the
    quit handler calls the quit method, or, in an app with one main window, that window's close request does. In an
    app with one main window and no quit command, what the close request runs is the quit method, and it is judged as
    one; an app with several main windows whose close requests each ask for themselves has no quit method. The method
    itself asks before it discards anything [CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01) covers (unsaved work; an
    app with nothing to lose asks nothing), closes its open dialogs before it exits, and runs the same save a close of
    the window runs (the window state of [WIN-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-08), in an app that keeps it).
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java): the `app.quit` command, which File → Quit runs, and the
    window's close request both call it, so macOS's Quit reaches it as a close request; it hides the other windows
    and dialogs, saves the window state and waits for the last settings write before it exits, and has nothing
    unsaved to ask about. That wait is the last save [PERF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-01) allows as the app quits; the
    template makes it on a background thread all the same.
    Editora's File → Quit and `app.quit` run [`MainController.onQuit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which asks about the quit once and then about each window's unsaved files; macOS's Quit doesn't reach it yet:
    [`MacOpenFiles`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/MacOpenFiles.java) wraps Glass's handler and passes `handleQuitAction` on to JavaFX's own, so each window gets a close
    request and asks for itself. Torrenta ([`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)), Modula ([`ModulaApp.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)) and nux (`Platform.exit`, from
    `app.quit` and from the tray, in [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)) don't catch macOS's Quit either. Termina and Mirada have no quit command
    ([WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14)). Mirada has one main window, and what its close request runs is its quit method: it asks
    about an unsaved edit, closes its tool windows and saves the window's place ([`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java), `mayClose`,
    `release`, `rememberPlace`), and macOS's Quit arrives there as a close request. Termina doesn't meet the rule
    yet: it has several windows and no quit method, so macOS's Quit arrives at each window as a close request and
    each asks for itself ([`TerminalWindow.close`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)).

- **WIN-14 · MUST.** Every app has a Quit, on every OS: the `app.quit` command, in the Command Palette, and, where the
  app has a File menu or a main menu, a Quit row in that menu that runs the command. A main menu is a menu button in
  the window that holds the app's commands as a menu bar would (Mirada's ☰, which it shows on every OS). A menu button
  that lists one kind of thing is not a main menu (nux's Profiles and Commands), and neither is a right-click menu
  (the only menu Modula has): an app with no File menu and no main menu meets the rule with the command alone. What
  Quit does is [WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-13). Closing the last window may end the app as well, but it is never the only way out.
  - *Why:* someone who quits one app of the family from the palette or the File menu looks for the same in the
    next. An app that ends only with its last window has no answer once it has a tray or a second window.
  - *Check (code):* `app.quit` is registered and the palette lists it. Where the app builds a File menu, a row of
    it runs `app.quit`; where it has no menu bar and a main menu instead, a row of that menu does. An app with
    neither menu passes on the command.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`app.quit`) and [`AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (Quit, the File menu's last row); Editora's `app.quit`, the
    last row of its File menu ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)). Torrenta's File menu ends with Quit, and it registers the command as `quit`.
    Termina and Mirada have no Quit. Termina's File menu has Close Window and ends with Settings, Sync Now and
    Configure Profiles ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java)); Mirada's ☰ menu, on every OS ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)), and, on macOS, its File menu
    ([`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)) end with Close (`window.close`). nux has neither menu and meets the rule with `app.quit`
    ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)). Modula has neither menu and no quit command: it quits from its tray and its window's close button
    ([`ModulaApp.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)).

- **WIN-15 · SHOULD.** On macOS, Settings is in the application menu, the one macOS names after the app, and runs
  the same command as the Settings row on Windows and Linux. Its row shows the chord the active keymap binds to
  that command (`Cmd+,` in the CUA keymap: [SET-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-01)), appended to the title as
  [MENU-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/menus/#menu-02) has the system menu bar's rows show theirs, and the item is given no key equivalent
  of its own. About, in the same menu, is [ABOUT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-01), and the Quit JavaFX puts there
  is [WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-13).
  - *Why:* it is where every Mac app has Settings, one of the places
    [the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins). A key equivalent set on the item is an
    accelerator under another name: macOS runs the item before the app's key dispatcher sees the key, and the menu
    goes on showing `⌘,` in a keymap that binds another chord, or none.
  - *Check (code):* on macOS the app inserts a Settings item into the application menu that runs the settings
    command. The item's title carries the chord the active keymap binds to that command and is written again when
    the keymap changes; the item is created without a key equivalent.
  - *Reference:* Mirada [`MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacAppMenu.java) adds the item, and it runs `app.settings`. It doesn't show the keymap's chord yet: it
    creates the item with the native key equivalent `Cmd+,` (`createMenuItem(…, ',', COMMAND)`), which stays
    whatever the keymap binds, and Mirada's Emacs keymap binds `C-,`
    ([`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/emacs.json)). The app template's [`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MacAppMenu.java) meets it: it inserts a Settings item that runs
    `app.settings`, created with no key equivalent, whose title carries the keymap's chord and is written again on a
    keymap change (`refresh`, from [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)). Termina's [`MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MacAppMenu.java) adds About
    only. Editora, Torrenta, Modula and nux add nothing to that menu.

- **WIN-10 · MAY.** The window has modes that change how much chrome it shows: Zen shows none, Expert keeps only
  the status bar, and Simple shows fewer menus, for new users.
  - *Check (code):* each mode is a command, and one truth table decides which chrome each mode shows.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java) (`toggleZen`, `toggleExpert`, `applySimpleMode`) over the truth
    table in [`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java), where Expert hides the menu bar, the toolbar, the tabs, the breadcrumb and the tool stripes
    (`menuBar` keys on both focus modes; in an extended window the title and the window buttons stay).

## Icons and color (ICON)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/: Inter and JetBrains Mono, the Caret & Ink palette, state colors that mean one thing, themes, and the two icon families.

### Type

- **ICON-01 · MUST.** Inter is attached by a *scene* stylesheet on every window's scene, dialogs, popups and
  tooltips included, not by a rule in the app stylesheet.
  - *Why:* dialogs, the Settings window, the palette, context menus and tooltips each live in a scene of their own
    that does not share `app.css`, and a scene sheet is re-applied cleanly when the theme switches at run time
    (`setUserAgentStylesheet`). AtlantaFX neither bundles nor names Inter, and JavaFX does not fall through a
    font-family list, so without the sheet the whole interface renders in the platform's "System" face.
  - *Check (code):* every window's scene gets the font sheet (Editora's `ui-font.css`): a listener on
    `Window.getWindows()` adds it to each window's scene, and to a new scene when the window's scene changes, or every
    window and dialog the app builds adds it itself, none left out. A popup or a tooltip needs no call of its own:
    when JavaFX shows one, it gives it the scene stylesheets of the window it is shown from
    (`PopupWindow.applyStylesheetFromOwner`). No `.root` rule in the app stylesheet (Editora's `app.css`) sets
    `-fx-font-family`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.installUiFont`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), a listener on `Window.getWindows()`, and [`styles/ui-font.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/ui-font.css); the app
    template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`installUiFont`, `hookUiFont`) and Mirada's [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Fonts.java) (`installSheet`) do the same.
    Termina and Torrenta carry the same sheet with no listener: each window and dialog adds it by calling
    `Fonts.installUiFont`, about forty times in Torrenta. Termina doesn't meet the rule yet: its helper is called
    for seven windows and [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java) adds the sheet to its questions, but four dialogs get none: the two
