    alerts and the rename-tab `TextInputDialog` built in [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java), and the `TextInputDialog` in
    [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingsWindow.java).
    Modula doesn't yet: the `.root` rule of its [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) sets IBM Plex Mono for the whole window.

- **ICON-02 · MUST.** The app bundles Inter's four faces and registers them before any CSS is applied; it never
  maps the platform's own UI font.
  - *Why:* an earlier macOS-only sheet used San Francisco, which JavaFX faux-bolds; Inter has a real bold on every
    platform.
  - *Check (code):* `Inter-Regular`, `Inter-Bold`, `Inter-Italic` and `Inter-BoldItalic` `.ttf` are under the app's
    `fonts/inter/` with their `OFL.txt`, and `Font.loadFont` runs on them before the first window is shown.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/fonts/inter/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/fonts/inter), [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java) (`loadForFirstPaint`,
    called from [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)). Termina and Torrenta bundle the same four faces. Modula doesn't yet: its
    [`fonts/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/tree/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/fonts) holds IBM Plex Mono only.

### The palette: Caret & Ink

- **ICON-04 · SHOULD.** A theme file follows the vendored AtlantaFX community themes: a `.root` block of `-color-*`
  tokens, then component rules that reference only those tokens.
  - *Check (code):* the file's first rule is `.root`, and no rule after it holds a `#` hex.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`styles/atlantafx-themes/editora-light.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/atlantafx-themes/editora-light.css), `editora-dark.css`.

- **ICON-05 · SHOULD.** A new app ships the Caret & Ink pair as its default theme, with `editora-light.css` and
  `editora-dark.css` copied unchanged into its own `styles/`.
  - *Why:* the palette is the family's, not the editor's.
  - *Check (code):* the app's two files are identical to Editora's.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`styles/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles) and the app template's [`styles/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/tree/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles), whose two files match Editora's. Torrenta's
    `editora-dark.css` matches too; its [`editora-light.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/editora-light.css) still has the earlier `-color-accent-fg`,
    `-color-warning-fg` and `-color-success-fg`, which Editora has since darkened.

- **ICON-06 · SHOULD.** Brace, the palette's periwinkle for the keyboard (chord chips, the menus' chord column), is
  one token on `.root` (Editora's `-state-key`): a `ladder()` over `-color-bg-default` that picks a deep ink on a
  light ground and a lighter periwinkle the darker the ground gets, and reads at 4.5:1 or more on every bundled
  theme's default and subtle surfaces.
  - *Why:* Brace has no AtlantaFX role, so it has to be a literal.
  - *Check (code):* the token is a `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`, and the color it resolves to on each bundled
    theme's default and subtle grounds is 4.5:1 or more against that ground. A contrast test that resolves the
    ladder against every bundled theme's grounds is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`.root`), [`StyleContrastTest.theKeyboardPeriwinkleReadsOnEveryBundledAppTheme`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

### State colors

- **ICON-07 · MUST.** Each state color is named once, as a token on `.root` (Editora's `-state-*`) that chains to
  one of the theme's roles (or a `ladder()` of its ground), and component rules use the token.
  - *Check (code):* each state color has one token (Editora's `-state-*`), declared once, in a `.root` block of the
    app stylesheet, as a `-color-*` role or a `ladder()` of the ground. A component rule that colors one of those
    states uses the token: none names the role behind it (`-color-danger-fg` for an error) or writes the ladder
    out again.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) (`.root`), held by
    [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`theStateTokensAreDeclaredOnceAtTheTopAndChainToARole`, and `severityColorsComeFromTheStateTokens`,
    which fails a component rule that names a danger, warning or success role). Termina meets it too: its
    [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) declares `-state-red`, `-state-amber` and `-state-green` on `.root`, and no component rule of
    its stylesheets names the role behind one. The other five apps don't yet. Editora's [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css)
    declares its tokens the same way (`.root`), but Editora doesn't hold the last clause: 79 declarations in that
    file's component rules name `-color-danger-fg`, `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-success-fg`
    directly, errors among them (`.crontab-error`, `.md-math-error`). Torrenta's tokens are on `.root` too
    (`-torrenta-*`), and two of its component rules write out the ladder of `-torrenta-up` again
    ([`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/app.css), `.speed-graph-up`, `.speed-graph-legend-up`). Torrenta doesn't hold the last clause either:
    24 declarations in that file's component rules and five in `add-dialog.css` name `-color-danger-fg`,
    `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-success-fg` directly (`.port-dot.port-down`, `.add-fetch-failed`), not the
    `-torrenta-error`, `-torrenta-stall` and `-torrenta-done` tokens that chain to them. Mirada and nux have no
    token for a state (Mirada's one `-state-*` token is `-state-key`, the keyboard's): Mirada's [`styles/mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css) redefines the roles themselves on `.root`, as ladders, and four of
    its component rules name `-color-danger-fg` or `-color-warning-fg` (`.status-echo-error`, `.status-echo-warn`
    and the Message Log's two); nux's [`nux.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/resources/com/nux/nux.css) has no `.root` block, and three of its rules name
    `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-danger-fg` (`.on-battery-note`, `.settings-problem`, `.detail-warn`). Modula's
    [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) has tokens its rules use (`-lock`, `-fault`), set as fixed hexes on `.root` and again on
    `.root.daylight`, chained to no role.

- **ICON-08 · MUST.** App stylesheets take their colors from AtlantaFX `-color-*` tokens, or from tokens the app
  builds on them; no component rule carries a fixed color, whatever its spelling: a hex, an `rgb()`, `rgba()` or
  `hsb()` value, or a named color such as `white`. A fixed color may stand only in a token's definition, on `.root`
  or in a scoped block that sets `-color-*` tokens, and only where the theme has no role to build on: a scrim's or
  a shadow's color, a color drawn over an image or a canvas and not on the theme's ground, or a color inside a
  `ladder()` of the ground ([ICON-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-13)). The ground, ink or accent of the app's own windows given there as
  a fixed color, in place of the theme's role, fails this rule; a state color given so is [ICON-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-07)'s
  failure and is not counted here again. `transparent` is not a color.
  - *Why:* a fixed color suits one theme; the roles track every theme for free.
  - *Check (code):* every color in a component rule of the app's stylesheets is an AtlantaFX `-color-*` role or a
    token, and a fixed color stands only where a token is defined, in a `.root` block or in a scoped block that
    sets `-color-*` tokens: as the plain value of a token for a scrim, a shadow or what is drawn over an image or a
    canvas (an `rgba()` of black, say), or inside a `ladder()` of the ground. A token for the ground, ink or
    accent of the app's own windows whose value is a fixed color and no role fails; a state color's token with no role behind it is [ICON-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-07)'s to judge, not this
    rule's. A fixed color is a hex
    (`grep -nE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b'` over those stylesheets lists them), an `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsb()` or `hsba()`
    value, or a named color such as `white`; `transparent` is not one. No component rule holds one, whichever property
    it sets (a `-fx-*-color`, a `-fx-fill`, an effect's color), inside a `ladder()` or not. A test that fails a fixed
    color outside the token block is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Termina's [`AppCssColorsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/AppCssColorsTest.java) (`componentRulesUseTokensNotLiteralColours`) and Mirada's
    [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`noRuleAfterTheTokenBlockHoldsAFixedColour`) fail a fixed color outside the `.root` block:
    a hex, an `rgb()` or an `hsb()` value, a shadow's color included, and in Mirada's a named color too. Both apps
    keep the scrim behind an overlay and their shadows' colors as tokens on `.root`, and so does the app template:
    `-scrim` and `-shadow` on `.root` in its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css), used by `.overlay-backdrop` and the cards' shadows, with no test that
    holds it. Editora's
    [`StyleContrastTest.severityAndDebugColoursComeFromTheStateTokens`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) holds six selectors it names, and Editora
    doesn't yet pass the whole check: `.breakpoint-marker`, `.debug-menu-logpoint`, `.exec-arrow`, `.view-mode-bar`, `.recent-remove`,
    `.personal-note-tooltip-content`, the fold-gutter markers and the default editor and Markdown preview palettes in
    [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) still carry fixed hexes, other rules an `rgba()` (the scrim of `.overlay-backdrop`, the diff and merge
    tints and shadows among them), and `.breakpoint-condition-mark` a fixed `white`. Torrenta doesn't either: `.speed-graph-up` and
    `.speed-graph-legend-up` in its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/app.css) hold a ladder of two hexes, and `.palette-backdrop` and two
    shadows an `rgba()`. Modula and nux write the palette's scrim as an `rgba()` background in a
    component rule, and a shadow's color the same way (`.palette-backdrop` and `.palette-card` in [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) and
    [`nux.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/resources/com/nux/nux.css)), so neither meets the rule yet; nux also sets `-fx-text-fill: white` on `.status-pill` and `.update-badge`.

- **ICON-09 · MUST.** Readable text uses `-color-fg-muted` or stronger, which is 4.5:1 on the default, subtle and
  overlay grounds in both flagship themes, Editora Light and Editora Dark: a line of UI text is `-color-fg-default`
  and secondary text `-color-fg-muted`. `-color-fg-subtle` (2.7:1 to 3.9:1, under 3:1 on Editora Light's subtle and
  inset grounds) is for disabled or decorative text only. An app whose default light and dark themes are another pair
  is held to the same on that pair. A test holds it.
  - *Check (test):* a contrast test computes muted ink on the default, subtle and overlay grounds of both flagship
    themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or of the app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another
    pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more; and it walks every rule of the app's stylesheets: it fails a rule that sets a text
    fill (`-fx-text-fill`, or `-fx-fill` on text) to `-color-fg-subtle` unless its selector is on a list the test
    names, of disabled and decorative selectors only. A test that checks a list of readable selectors instead passes
    every selector it doesn't name.
  - *Reference:* only the app template's test walks every rule. Editora's
    [`StyleContrastTest.textThatMustBeReadUsesTheMutedRoleNotSubtle`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) computes the ratios and checks six selectors it names (the palette's
    and the switcher's hints, an unbound shortcut, the line numbers of the notes and structure trees, the blame
    date), so it passes while `.encryption-locked-hint` and `.pom-version-unknown` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) set text a
    person reads in `-color-fg-subtle`. The app template's test of the same name
    ([`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java)) walks every rule of its `app.css` and both themes and fails a text fill in
    `-color-fg-subtle` on any selector but the disabled and decorative ones it lists (`SUBTLE_TEXT`), and computes
    the muted role's ratio on the grounds of both themes. Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) has no
    test for this rule, and Termina, Torrenta, Modula and nux have no contrast test of their stylesheets.

- **ICON-10 · MUST.** Text in a role's tint (the theme's `-color-<role>-fg`, for the accent, success, warning and
  danger roles) reaches 4.5:1 on that role's subtle fill (`-color-<role>-subtle`) and on the default and subtle
  grounds (`-color-bg-default`, `-color-bg-subtle`), in both flagship themes, Editora Light and Editora Dark, or, in
  an app whose default light and dark themes are another pair, in that pair. A test holds it.
  - *Check (test):* a contrast test computes each role's `-fg` on its `-subtle`, on `-color-bg-subtle` and on
    `-color-bg-default`, in both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or in the app's own default light
    and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`StyleContrastTest.lightTintedTextReachesAaOnItsOwnGroundAndOnTheSubtleSurface`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java),
    `darkTintedTextStaysAa`. Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`tintedTextReachesAaOnItsOwnFillAndOnBothGrounds`) holds
    it on Cupertino Light and Cupertino Dark, the pair it ships.

- **ICON-11 · MUST.** Ink on an emphasis fill is `-color-fg-emphasis`, never a fixed white: the token is white in the
  light themes and a dark ink in the dark ones, 4.5:1 or more on the emphasis fill of the accent, success, warning and
  danger roles in the two themes [ICON-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-09) names. A test holds it.
  - *Why:* white on the dark accent is 1.68:1.
  - *Check (test):* a contrast test computes `-color-fg-emphasis` on the `-emphasis` fill of the accent, success,
    warning and danger roles, in both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark) or in the app's own default
    light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more; and the rules that paint on an
    emphasis fill use it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`StyleContrastTest.inkOnAnEmphasisFillIsTheThemesOnEmphasisColour`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java), and Mirada's test of
    the same name ([`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java)), on Cupertino Light and Cupertino Dark: each holds 4.5:1.

- **ICON-12 · MUST.** One focus ring color, the theme's `-color-accent-emphasis`, named once on `.root` (Editora's
  `-focus-ring`) and drawn by the `:focus-visible` block in the app stylesheet ([KBD-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-16)), at 3:1
  or better on every surface: the default, subtle, inset and overlay grounds of the two themes [ICON-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-09)
  names (see [Keyboard first](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/)). A test holds it.
  - *Check (test):* a test reads the ring's token from `.root` (Editora's `-focus-ring`) and computes it on the
    default, subtle, inset and overlay grounds of both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or of the
    app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 3:1 or more.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*),
    [`StyleContrastTest.theFocusRingIsAtLeastThreeToOneOnEverySurface`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

- **ICON-13 · SHOULD.** A state color the AtlantaFX theme has no role for (Editora's Git olive and violet) is a
  `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`, never one fixed hex for light themes and another for dark. Brace, the
  periwinkle, is [ICON-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#icon-06).
  - *Why:* the old fixed light hexes read at 3.2:1 on Editora Dark.
  - *Check (code):* each such token is declared as a `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`; none is a fixed hex, or a
    pair of hexes switched by theme. A contrast test that resolves each ladder on every bundled theme's ground is
    the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`-state-olive`, `-state-violet`, `-state-key`),
    [`StyleContrastTest.theGitOliveAndVioletFollowTheAppThemesGround`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

- **ICON-14 · SHOULD.** The contrast tests are pure: they read the stylesheets and do the WCAG arithmetic without
  starting the toolkit, so they run with the unit tests on every OS.
  - *Why:* a test that starts the toolkit is an FX test, tagged and run apart from the unit tests
    ([QUAL-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-06)); a pure one fails the plain unit run on every OS, the first time a color
    changes.
  - *Check (code):* every test class that computes a contrast ratio reads the app's `.css` resources as text and
    starts no toolkit: none is an FX test.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) and Mirada's
    [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java): each reads the stylesheets as text and uses `javafx.scene.paint.Color` for the arithmetic
    alone. The template's key color is held there too (`theKeyColorReadsOnBothThemesGrounds`), and no FX test of its computes a contrast. Mirada's [`AccentTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/AccentTest.java) is pure too, over the accent it derives from the system's, and so is Termina's
    [`ThemeTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/ThemeTest.java), which holds the colors of its terminal schemes and not the chrome's stylesheet. Editora's
    [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) is pure as well, but Editora doesn't meet the rule yet: FX tests compute contrast ratios on
    rendered nodes too, [`ChordChipThemeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ChordChipThemeFxTest.java), [`DebugValuePopupThemeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugValuePopupThemeFxTest.java) and
    [`SettingsFrameFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsFrameFxTest.java) among them.

### Themes

- **ICON-15 · MUST.** The app has light and dark themes and switches between them at run time, without a restart.
  - *Check (code):* the app has a light theme and a dark one, and picking a theme calls
    `Application.setUserAgentStylesheet` in the running app.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java) (`applyAppTheme`).

- **ICON-16 · MUST.** The theme setting offers "follow the system": a choice that applies the light or dark theme
  to match the system's color scheme, and changes with it.
  - *Check (code):* the theme setting has a system value, the place where the user picks a theme lists it, and
    while it is chosen a listener on `Platform.getPreferences().colorSchemeProperty()` re-applies the theme.
  - *Reference:* Mirada [`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java) (`ThemeChoice.SYSTEM`), [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Theme.java); nux [`config/Advanced.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/Advanced.java)
    (`THEME_SYSTEM`), [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Theme.java); Termina [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Themes.java) (`SYSTEM_ID`, `followSystem`), with the
    listener in [`ui/WindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java); the app template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`ThemeChoice.SYSTEM`). Each lists
    the choice in its Settings. Editora, Torrenta and Modula don't offer it yet: Editora's and Torrenta's pickers
    list named themes only ([`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java), Torrenta's [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Theme.java)), and Modula's theme is one on/off
    setting, `daylight` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/Settings.java)).

- **ICON-17 · MUST.** A theme name the app does not know falls back to the first-run default theme.
  - *Check (code):* the lookup from a saved name to a theme ends in the default, not an exception.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`Themes.themeFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java), falling back to [`Themes.DEFAULT`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java) (Editora Light).

- **ICON-18 · SHOULD.** The state colors never decorate: in every theme amber means "not durable yet", a warning
  ([WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-01) requires a warning in the echo area in amber) or an update available in About
  ([ABOUT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-10) asks for it there), red "broken" and green "verified", and nothing is
  colored amber, red or green for any other reason. A theme may change the accent, the ground and the ink, never
  these meanings.
  - *Check (code):* every rule that uses the amber, red or green state token (Editora's `-state-amber`,
    `-state-red` and `-state-green`) marks one of the meanings in the table under [State colors](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/icons-and-color/#state-colors).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css).

### Icons

- **ICON-19 · MUST.** In an app whose icons come in two families, one colored by its stroke and one by its fill, a
  glyph node carries the style class of one family, never both (Editora's two are `icon-line` and `toolbar-icon`).
  An app with one icon family, or with no icons in its window, has nothing to mix.
  - *Why:* a line glyph is colored by its stroke, and any `X .toolbar-icon` fill rule (there are dozens) would paint
    its outline solid. A glyph that moves family moves its CSS with it.
  - *Check (code):* the method that builds a line glyph adds the line family's class alone, the one that builds a
    filled glyph adds the filled family's alone (Editora's `Icons.line` and `Icons.of`), and no other code adds
    the second class to a glyph node. A test that builds every glyph and fails when one carries both classes is the
    surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java) (`line`, `of`) and [`editor/MenuIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuIcons.java), whose glyphs
    [`MenuIconFamilyFxTest.aLineGlyphIsNeverAlsoTaggedAsAFilledOne`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuIconFamilyFxTest.java) holds. Torrenta's [`IconsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/ui/IconsTest.java)
    (`everyGlyphIsAStyledScaledPath`) builds every glyph and fails one that carries both classes or neither.
    Termina, Mirada and Modula draw one family each.

- **ICON-20 · MUST.** The same action wears the same glyph wherever it is reached: Save is one floppy on the
  toolbar, in the File menu and in a tab's menu.
  - *Check (code):* wherever an action is drawn (a toolbar button, a menu row, a tab's menu), its glyph comes from
    one icon class or one lookup keyed by the command. Where a second icon class holds a copy of its own, the copy
    has the same path data and style class. A test that compares the path data and style class of each action's
    glyph across the icon classes is the surest evidence. An app that draws no glyph anywhere has nothing to
    compare and passes.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MenuBarIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarIcons.java) reuses [`Icons`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java); [`editor/MenuIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuIcons.java) (the editor package may not
    depend on `ui`) copies each twin's family and path data verbatim, held by
    [`MenuIconFamilyFxTest.everySharedActionUsesTheSameGlyphInBothIconSets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuIconFamilyFxTest.java). Mirada gives a command's menu row
    and its button one glyph from one lookup ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java), `forCommand`).

- **ICON-23 · SHOULD.** In an app that shows files with an icon each (a project tree, file tabs, a list of files),
  a file's icon comes from a pure function from file name to icon key, unit-tested without the toolkit, and any
  type it does not know gets the generic document glyph, so a new type never regresses the look.
  - *Check (test):* a unit test resolves names to keys, an unknown one to the generic key.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/FileIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileIcons.java): `iconKeyFor(name)` resolves the key, `forFileName` turns it into a
    node; brand logos from Simple Icons, category glyphs (image, archive, PDF, table, lock, JSON, settings) from
    Material. [`FileIconsTest.unknownAndNullFallBackToGeneric`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FileIconsTest.java).

- **ICON-24 · MUST.** Every glyph set and font the app ships is credited in `NOTICE` with its license.
  - *Check (code):* each icon source named in the icon classes and each family under `fonts/` has an entry in
    `NOTICE`. An app that ships no glyph set and no font has nothing to credit here.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`NOTICE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/NOTICE): Material Design Icons (Apache-2.0), Simple Icons (CC0; the logos stay their
    owners' trademarks), Inter and the monospace faces (OFL), and the glyph sets inside the bundled Symbols Nerd
    Font, Octicons and Seti UI (MIT) among them.

## Toolbars and tooltips (TBAR)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/: Icon-only buttons that have a name, groups by spacing, one chrome band, the customizable toolbar, and tooltips that share the menus' card.

### Rules

- **TBAR-01 · MUST.** Every icon-only button, one that shows a glyph or a symbol such as "?" or "···" and no
  word, has a name: one helper sets its tooltip and its accessible text from the same string, the chord included
  where the tooltip carries one ([TBAR-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-03)), so a screen reader says what a sighted user reads.
  - *Why:* a hand-rolled button gets the tooltip and forgets the name, which is how Editora once had seven copies
    of the helper drifting apart, and how a screen reader comes to announce "button".
  - *Check (code):* every icon-only button gets its tooltip and its accessible text in one call that sets both
    from one string (Editora's `Icons.button`, `Icons.toolbarButton` and `Icons.name`). A button with a
    `setTooltip` and no `setAccessibleText` fails, and so does one whose tooltip is written again later, to add a
    chord, while its accessible text keeps the first string.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java) (`button`, `toolbarButton`, `name`), used by its panel toolbars.
    Torrenta's copy of all three ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Icons.java)): its `name` is the one place Torrenta sets an accessible
    text, and it names every button of the main toolbar ([`MainWindow.toolButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)) and names them again
    when the keys change. Termina's [`ui/IconNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) (`name`), which binds both to one string.
    Five apps don't meet it yet. Editora sets the tooltip only on its main toolbar ([`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java)
    and [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java)) and on the floating buttons that leave Zen and Expert mode
    and bring the toolbar back ([`WindowChromeCoordinator.installZenOverlay`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java)), and its stripe buttons' accessible
    text is the tool window's title without the chord the tooltip carries ([`ToolWindowManager.register`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)).
    Torrenta's detail pane gives its "···" button a tooltip and no accessible text ([`ui/DetailPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DetailPane.java)).
    Mirada's [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) (`button`, `name`) makes the accessible text the command's title and puts the chord
    in the tooltip only. nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java) sets the tooltip and the accessible text of its "?" button from one
    string, then its `shortcut` helper writes the tooltip again as "About Nux  (F1)" and leaves the accessible
    text. Modula's transport, Settings and Record buttons have a tooltip and no accessible text
    ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and so has the "+" button of its preset row ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)).

- **TBAR-03 · MUST.** The tooltip of a button that runs a command names the command and its chord, read from the
  active keymap and never typed into a string: "Save (C-x C-s)". The name is the command's title
  ([KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-03)), which a tooltip may show without its category prefix, as a menu row may
  ([MENU-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/menus/#menu-01)): "Save" for "File: Save". An unbound command shows its title alone.
  - *Check (code):* the tooltip shows the command's title, whole or without its category prefix, and the keymap's
    display chord for its id, and is rebuilt when the keymap changes. The chord is the one of the command the button
    runs, and no chord is typed into the string. A fixed key of the control itself (Enter in a find field) is no
    command's chord and may be written, as [KBD-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-13) allows.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java) (the `command.<id>` title, prefix and all) and
    [`ToolWindowManager.tooltipFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java). Its main toolbar ([`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java), `refreshToolbarTooltips`) takes
    the chord from the keymap and the name from a `tooltip.*` catalog key of its own: for most buttons that is the
    title without its prefix (`tooltip.save=Save` beside `command.file.save=File: Save`), for six another name,
    which doesn't meet the rule: "Find / Replace" for `find.show`, whose title is "Find: Incremental Search";
    "Open" for `file.find` ("File: Find File…"); "Close Tab" for `buffer.close` ("Buffer: Close"); "Open Folder as
    Project…" for `project.open` ("Project: Open Folder…"); "New From Template" for `template.new` ("Template: New
    File From Template…"); and "Simple UI mode" for `view.toggleSimpleMode` ("View: Toggle Simple UI Mode").
    Two more buttons miss it another way: `file.clearRecent` ("File: Clear Recent Files") reads "Clear recent
    files", and the pinned tail's Stop button, which stops the run as `run.stop` ("Run: Stop Program") does, is set
    up with no command id, so it reads "Stop the running program" and shows no chord.
    Torrenta's `toolbar.withChord`.
    Mirada's [`Icons.tooltip`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) builds the same
    "label (key)" form with the chord from the keymap in use ([`Command.chord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Command.java)), and [`TitleBar.relabel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) names the
    header buttons again when the keys change; Termina's [`IconNames.withChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) takes the chord from its keymap too,
    but its find bar's arrows don't meet the rule yet: [`ui/SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) names them from `search.older` and
    `search.newer`, "Previous match, up (Enter)" and "Next match, down (Shift+Enter)", not from a command's title,
    and gives each arrow the chord of the command that steps the other way. The up arrow steps to an older match,
    as `findNext` does ([`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)), and shows the chord of `findPrevious`; the down arrow steps to a
    newer one, as `findPrevious` does, and shows the chord of `findNext`. The Enter and Shift+Enter in the two
    strings are the field's own keys. Modula's and nux's tooltips are written in
    the code, not read from a command: Modula's carry no chord ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and nux's add the display
    text of a `KeyCombination` to the button's label ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `shortcut`).

- **TBAR-14 · SHOULD.** Every tooltip shows after the same delay, 400 ms, set where the app makes its tooltips and
  not tooltip by tooltip.
  - *Why:* JavaFX waits a full second, which reads as no tooltip at all on a row of icons, and a delay set here and
    there makes some buttons answer faster than their neighbors.
  - *Check (code):* every `Tooltip` the app creates gets a 400 ms show delay from one place: each is made by one
    factory that calls `setShowDelay`, or the stylesheet's `.tooltip` rule sets `-fx-show-delay: 400ms`. A tooltip
    made with `new Tooltip` outside the factory and given no delay fails, as does any other delay.
  - *Reference:* the app template: its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) sets `-fx-show-delay: 400ms` on `.tooltip`, and the
    tooltips its code makes get the same from one constant, `TOOLTIP_DELAY` in [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Icons.java) (`bindName`, and
    [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabHeaders.java) for a tab's). Termina is nearest among the apps: [`ui/IconNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) (`name`, `SHOW_DELAY`) sets 400 ms on every tooltip it makes,
    and [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) sets the same inline on a tab's folder tooltip, but the tooltip on a disabled row of
    its [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/CommandPalette.java) sets none. Editora sets 300, 350 or 400 ms on some
    ([`editor/LazyTooltip.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/LazyTooltip.java)'s callers, [`ui/StructurePanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StructurePanel.java), [`ui/MapSurface.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapSurface.java), [`ui/DiffViewerPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DiffViewerPane.java)) and leaves
    the rest at JavaFX's second; Mirada sets 250 ms on one ([`ui/MarksBadge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MarksBadge.java)) and none on the others; Torrenta,
    Modula and nux set none. No app's stylesheet sets `-fx-show-delay`.

- **TBAR-06 · SHOULD.** The bars an app stacks at the top of its main window are one chrome band: whichever of
  the menu bar, the toolbar and the tab strip it has share `-color-bg-subtle` and draw no hairline between them.
  The bars it stacks at the bottom, whichever of a breadcrumb, a bottom stripe and the status bar it has, do the
  same. An app with one bar at an edge has nothing to join there.
  - *Why:* three rules within forty pixels read as clutter, not structure.
  - *Check (by hand):* look at the top and the bottom of the main window in a light and a dark theme for a line
    between two bars, or a change of ground from one to the next.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`.menu-bar, .tool-bar`).

### The toolbar

**Applies to:** an app with a toolbar: a bar of icon-only buttons in a window's chrome (its title bar, a band of its own under the title bar or the menu bar, or the header of a panel), each a shortcut to a command. Editora's and Torrenta's `ToolBar`, the toolbars of Editora's panels and Mirada's header buttons are toolbars. So is a [tool window stripe](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tool-window-stripes), on every side: the label its bottom buttons add to the glyph does not change what they are. These are not toolbars: a bar of labeled buttons (nux's `ToolBar`, whose one icon-only button, "?", only [TBAR-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-01) covers); controls that belong to the window's content, icon-only or not (Modula's transport and footer controls, Mirada's controls over the image); the buttons at the end of a tab strip (Termina's "+" and its chevron); and a find bar's buttons ([FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-16) is theirs). Controls that belong to the window's content include a row of preset chips with its add button (Modula's) and the buttons inside a panel's rows (Mirada's info panel), and an image, PDF or Diff viewer's own bar in the content area (Editora's) is content too.

- **TBAR-02 · MUST.** Toolbar buttons stay out of the Tab order: the command, the palette and the menus reach the
  action, and Tab is for the content. The [keyboard page](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#focus-and-accessibility) has the general
  focus rules.
  - *Check (code):* every button on a toolbar is taken out of the Tab order with `setFocusTraversable(false)`,
    where it is built or by the helper that builds it (Editora's `Icons.toolbarButton`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`Icons.toolbarButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java), used by the toolbars of its Git and Markdown lint tool windows;
    Torrenta's copy of it, which builds every button of its main toolbar ([`MainWindow.toolButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)); Mirada's header
    buttons: its [`Icons.button`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) takes Rotate out of the Tab order, and [`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) takes Info and ☰ out
    where it builds them. Editora doesn't yet, on these toolbars among others: the buttons of its main toolbar, built
    by [`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java) and [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java), the stripe buttons, the buttons of
    the Test Results panel's toolbar, built by `Icons.button` ([`ui/TestRunnerPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TestRunnerPanel.java)), and the float, maximize
    and close buttons in the header of every tool window ([`ui/ToolWindowPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowPanel.java)) take focus.

- **TBAR-04 · SHOULD.** A toolbar's groups of buttons are separated by spacing, not rules: where a toolbar holds
  `Separator` nodes, keep them (their padding is the gap) and make the line transparent.
  - *Check (code):* the stylesheet makes the line of every `Separator` on a toolbar transparent (Editora's
    `.tool-bar .separator:vertical > .line`, a transparent border), on a panel's toolbar as on the main one. A toolbar
    that holds no `Separator` (Mirada's header buttons) has nothing to restyle and passes.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css), for its main toolbar. Editora doesn't meet the rule on its Debug panel's toolbar
    yet: the separators there carry a class of their own, `debug-toolbar-separator`, whose one rule sets their padding
    and leaves the line drawn ([`ui/DebugPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugPanel.java)). Torrenta's separators still draw a line
    (`.main-toolbar .separator:vertical > .line` in its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/app.css)).

- **TBAR-05 · SHOULD.** Hiding a button group (Simple mode, a build tool that is not detected) hides the leading,
  trailing and doubled separators it leaves, so no gap stands on its own, and shows them all again when nothing is
  hidden.
  - *Check (code):* every change to a toolbar item's visibility ends in one pass over the bar's separators.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowChromeCoordinator.collapseToolbarSeparators`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java), for its main toolbar.

- **TBAR-07 · SHOULD.** A toggle looks on while it is on: a button that opens an overlay (Find, the palette, a split)
  and the Simple mode button carry a pseudo-class (Editora's `:open`) while their state holds, so the way back out
  does not look like the way in.
  - *Check (code):* each such button sets a pseudo-class from its state, and the stylesheet gives that state a fill.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MainController.OPEN`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), [`WindowChromeCoordinator`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java) (Simple mode), `.button:open` in
    [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css). Torrenta's Simple mode button carries `:on`, which its stylesheet fills (`.toolbar-button:on`), but
    Torrenta doesn't meet the rule yet: its palette button carries no pseudo-class while the palette shows
    ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)). Its `:active` marks the alternative speed limit on a label of the status bar, not on a
    toolbar button.

- **TBAR-08 · MUST.** A toolbar never holds the only way to an action: every icon on it (in Editora, every icon
  of the cluster the user can customize) is also in the menus and the palette.
  - *Why:* that is what makes it safe to hide icons in a narrow window and to let the user remove them.
  - *Check (code):* every button on the toolbar runs a registered command, so the palette lists it, and a menu lists
    that command too: the menu bar, or the app's main menu where it has no bar ([WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) says
    what a main menu is). A button that only opens a menu (Editora's Recent, Mirada's ☰) is no action of its own. In
    an app whose toolbar is built from a catalog (Editora's `ToolbarCatalog`), every catalog item's command id is also
    in the menus' model.
  - *Reference:* Mirada's header buttons, Rotate and Info, which its ☰ menu lists too ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)). Eleven
    of the twelve buttons of Torrenta's toolbar run a command that a menu row runs too ([`MainWindow.buildToolbar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)),
    but Torrenta doesn't meet the rule yet: the twelfth, the palette button, opens the palette from a handler of its
    own, as the View menu's Command Palette row does, and no command does
    ([PAL-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/#pal-01)). Editora [`toolbar/ToolbarCatalog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/toolbar/ToolbarCatalog.java): each item carries the
    `commandId` it runs, and the only items without one are declared special widgets, such as the Recent menu button
    ([`ToolbarCatalogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/toolbar/ToolbarCatalogTest.java)). Editora doesn't meet the rule yet: three catalog items run commands that are in the
    palette and in no menu, `tool.todo`, `tool.bookmarks` and `view.toggleZen`, which [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) doesn't
    list.

- **TBAR-09 · MAY.** The toolbar is customizable: the user reorders, removes and restores its buttons, and the
  layout is saved in Settings and shared by every window.
  - *Check (code):* the user can reorder the toolbar's buttons, remove one and bring the default layout back (Editora:
    a customize mode in which a drag along the bar reorders its buttons and a drag off it removes one, and a menu row
    that restores the default); and the layout is written to the settings, which every window reads. A test that
    drives a reorder and a removal is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java), [`ToolbarCustomizeModeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCustomizeModeFxTest.java), [`ToolbarCustomizationFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCustomizationFxTest.java).
    The cluster is a list of catalog ids in Settings (`toolbarLayout`), sanitized on read. The bar's right-click
    menu offers *Customize Toolbar…* (or *Done*), *Configure…* (the Settings page) and *Restore Default*. In
    customize mode the bar tints, buttons drag to reorder with an accent insertion line and drag off the bar to
    remove; Escape leaves the mode.

### The main toolbar

**Applies to:** an app with a main toolbar: a toolbar ([The toolbar](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#the-toolbar) says what one is) that is a band of its own across the top of the main window, as Editora's and Torrenta's `ToolBar` are. Mirada's header buttons, which share the title bar with the file's name, are a toolbar and not a main toolbar; nux's bar of labeled buttons is neither.

- **TBAR-15 · SHOULD.** The main toolbar's icon cluster and its pinned tail (Settings and the other controls the
  user must always reach) are separate containers: when the window narrows, the cluster's icons go into the
  overflow chevron and the tail keeps every control.
  - *Why:* a `ToolBar` overflows from its end, so with everything in one bar a narrow window hides Settings and the
    project switcher first and keeps icons that are all in the menus anyway ([TBAR-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-08)).
  - *Check (code):* the tail's controls sit in a container of their own beside the `ToolBar` that holds the icon
    cluster, and are not items of that `ToolBar`, so its overflow cannot take them. A test that narrows the window
    and finds the cluster overflowing while the tail's last control stays flush with the bar's right edge is the
    surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowToolbar.appendFixedTail`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java), [`ToolbarOverflowFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarOverflowFxTest.java). Torrenta keeps
    Simple mode and Settings inside its `ToolBar`, after a spacer, so they are the first to overflow.

- **TBAR-16 · SHOULD.** Settings closes the main toolbar at its right end, with the Simple mode toggle just
  before it in an app that has Simple mode, whether the mode is on or off.
  - *Why:* the same two buttons in the same place in every app, and the toggle is the way back out of a mode that
    empties much of the bar.
  - *Check (by hand):* look at the bar's right end with Simple mode off, then on.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowToolbar.appendFixedTail`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java); Torrenta [`MainWindow.buildToolbar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

- **TBAR-17 · SHOULD.** A main toolbar button is disabled while its command can't act (Save on a saved file, Undo
  with nothing to undo, Cut and Copy with no selection, a split on a tab that can't be split), and the events that
  change that state update it; nothing polls. [KBD-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-04) has the same state in the menus and the palette.
  - *Why:* a button that does nothing when clicked reads as a broken button.
  - *Check (code):* each button's disabled state is bound to its command's availability, or refreshed from the
    document's edit, selection and dirty events and on a tab switch.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowToolbar.refreshEditState`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java), `refreshSplitButtons` and `refreshPasteState`,
    which reads the clipboard only on a tab switch, on focus and after a copy, never on a keystroke; the buttons
    added from the catalog ([`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java)) stay enabled. Torrenta
    [`MainWindow.toolButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) binds each button's `disableProperty` to its command's `enabled`.

- **TBAR-18 · SHOULD.** A command hides the main toolbar and shows it again, and the choice is kept across
  launches.
  - *Check (code):* a registered command toggles the bar, and the setting it writes is read back at startup.
  - *Reference:* Editora `view.toggleToolbar` ([`WindowChromeCoordinator.toggleToolbar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java)), with a floating button at
    the top right that brings a hidden bar back; Torrenta `toggle-toolbar`, kept as `settings.toolbar()`.

- **TBAR-19 · SHOULD.** The main toolbar keeps its height when a control in it hides or shows (in Editora, the project
  switcher in Simple mode or with Projects off), so the tabs and the content under it never move.
  - *Check (by hand):* hide and show each control the bar can lose (in Editora, turn Simple mode on and off) and watch
    the top edge of what sits under the bar: it stays where it was.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WindowToolbar.stabilizeToolbarHeight`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java), which pins the row's minimum height to the
    project switcher's.

### Tool window stripes

**Applies to:** an app with tool window stripes.

- **TBAR-12 · SHOULD.** A tool window stripe button takes its name from its tool window: the name its tooltip
  shows ([TBAR-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-03)) is the window's title, with the chord of the command that toggles the window, and it
  follows the title when the title changes. The button's right-click menu has *Open in Split* and *Hide*.
  - *Check (code):* the stripe button's tooltip is built from the tool window's title and the keymap's display
    chord for the window's command, and is built again when the title changes; the button has a right-click menu
    with those two rows.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ToolWindowManager.register`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java) (the menu) and `tooltipFor`, which `refreshTooltips` runs
    again on a keymap switch only. Editora doesn't meet the rule yet: a title change (the Project window becoming
    "Current Folder") reaches the button's accessible text and the bottom stripe's label, not its tooltip.

- **TBAR-13 · SHOULD.** The right stripe's first icon lines up with the editor's first line of text, not with the
  tab strip.
  - *Check (code):* the code that lays out the side stripes pads the stripe's top by the tab strip's measured
    height, so its first button starts where the editor's text does. A test that compares the first stripe
    button's top with the editor's first line is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ToolWindowManager.alignVerticalStripesWithEditorText`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java),
    [`ToolWindowStripeAlignmentFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowStripeAlignmentFxTest.java).

## Tabs and tool panels (TABS)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tabs-and-panels/: The tab strip and its states, reorder and reopen, and the tool panels that dock around the editor.

### Window title

- **TABS-10 · SHOULD.** The window title names the file, the project and the app, with a `●` prefix for an unsaved
  file. An app with no files or projects names what the window shows in their place (a terminal, the working
  folder or the title its program set), or the app alone where there is nothing to name.
  - *Check (code):* the code that sets the stage title adds all three and the marker; in an app with no files or
    projects, what stands in for them, or the app's name alone.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MainController.updateWindowTitle`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java). Termina's title follows the selected tab
    ([`TerminalTitle.window`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalTitle.java): the name the user gave the tab, the title the shell set or the working folder's path, and the
    app's name when it knows none). The app template names the file, its sample project and the app, with the `●` prefix
    (`windowTitle` in [`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java); [`TabsAndPanelsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsTest.java), `theWindowTitleNamesTheFileTheProjectAndTheApp`).
    Modula and nux show the app's name.

### Tabs

**Applies to:** an app whose main window holds documents or sessions in tabs the user opens and closes, as Editora's files and Termina's terminals are. The pages of a Settings window (nux's `TabPane`), the fixed sections of a detail pane (Torrenta's) and a strip that switches the window between views (Torrenta's Transfers, Search and RSS) are not such tabs: the user neither opens nor closes them. The Tabs rules cover every tab of the main window's strip, whatever it shows (Editora's image, hex and PDF viewer tabs as much as its editor tabs), not tabs inside a tool window (those of Editora's Terminal and Build Output panels).

- **TABS-01 · MUST.** Every tab operation is a command, so it can be bound to a chord, is in the palette and has a
  menu row: close, close others, close all, close unmodified, close to the left and right, pin, reopen closed, next
  and previous. The tab's [right-click menu](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/menus/) lists the ones that act on a tab. A terminal app's tabs
  are never saved or unsaved, so a terminal app has no close unmodified, and closing its window closes all its
  tabs, so it needs no close all; the other operations are its commands too.
  - *Check (code):* the registry holds a command for each operation, each has a row in the menu bar or in the
    tab's right-click menu, and that menu (Editora's `TabContextMenu`), on every tab of the strip, lists the ones
    that act on a tab; in a terminal app, each operation but close unmodified and close all.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java) (`buffer.close`, `buffer.closeOthers`, `buffer.closeAll`,
    `buffer.closeUnmodified`, `buffer.closeLeft`, `buffer.closeRight`, `buffer.togglePin`, `buffer.reopenClosed`,
    `buffer.next`), [`ui/TabContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabContextMenu.java). Editora has no previous-tab command yet, and
    its image, hex and PDF viewer tabs have no right-click menu: `openImageTab`, `openHexTab` and `openPdfTab` in
    [`ui/FileWorkflowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileWorkflowCoordinator.java) install none, and `installTabMenu` in [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) is called for
    an editor's tab alone. Termina
    [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (`closeTab`, `closeOtherTabs`, `closeTabsToTheLeft`, `closeTabsToTheRight`, `pinTab`,
    `reopenClosedTab`, `nextTab` and `previousTab` in `menuCommands`; the tab's menu in `buildTabMenu`). Its File
    menu closes the tab, the others, the ones to either side, or the window, which is its close all
    ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java)).

- **TABS-02 · MUST.** The header is the title: the Tab's own text stays empty, and a graphic header carries the
  file-type glyph, the markers and the title in a label of its own (Editora's style class for it is `tab-title`). The
  tooltip is the full path, in which `~` may stand for the home folder. A terminal app's tab shows no file: its header
  has no file-type glyph, its title names the tab (the user's own name for it, the title the shell set, the running
  program or the working folder), and its tooltip is the working folder's full path.
  - *Why:* the graphic is what makes the header a drag handle and lets each state set its own color.
  - *Check (code):* every tab that shows a file, an editor's or a viewer's, gets `setText("")` and a graphic that
    holds the file-type glyph and the title in a label of its own (Editora's `.tab-title`); its tooltip is the
    file's path. In a terminal app: every tab's own text is empty, its graphic holds the title label and no
    file-type glyph, and the tooltip is the working folder of the tab's active pane. A path that writes the home
    folder as `~` is a full path.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabHeaders.java), for its editor tabs (`bufferHeader`, `tooltip`). Its image, hex and PDF
    viewer tabs don't yet: `contentHeader`, which builds their header, sets no tooltip. Termina [`TerminalWindow.addTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (a `tab-title` label as the tab's
    graphic, and `installDirectoryTooltip`) over [`ui/TerminalTitle.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalTitle.java) (`tab`, and `tooltip`, which writes the
    home folder as `~`).

- **TABS-03 · MUST.** A tab's header, the one graphic header of [TABS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tabs-and-panels/#tabs-02), carries the tab's states: a `• `
  prefix in amber italic for unsaved, a pin and bold for pinned, muted italic for read-only. A terminal app's tab is
  never unsaved or read-only, and its header says in their place what the tab is doing: the title is the running
  program's name while one runs, unless the user or the shell named the tab, and a mark beside the title says what
  happened while the tab was not selected (a notification, a bell, or output after a quiet spell), cleared when the
  tab is selected. A pinned terminal tab is drawn as any other pinned tab, with a pin and a bold title.
  - *Check (code):* the code that builds a tab's header marks it unsaved, pinned or read-only (Editora's style
    classes `dirty`, `pinned` and `read-only` on `.tab-header`) and adds the `• ` prefix and the pin, and the
    stylesheet gives each mark the look the rule names. In a terminal app: the stylesheet styles the pinned title,
    the code that names the tab puts the running program before the folder, and the header shows the mark and
    clears it when the tab is selected.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabHeaders.java), [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css); the Unsaved, Pinned and Read-only rows of the
    [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tabs-and-panels/#spec) table. Termina [`ui/TerminalTitle.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalTitle.java) (`tab`), [`ui/TabMarks.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TabMarks.java) and `TabMarkState` in
    [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (a dot after the title, in the terminal palette's magenta, yellow or cyan, and a pin), and
    `.tab-title.pinned` in its [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css).

- **TABS-04 · MUST.** Bulk close skips pinned tabs: close others, close all, close unmodified and close to the left
  or right never close a pinned tab. A terminal app has three of them ([TABS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tabs-and-panels/#tabs-01)), and each skips its
  pinned tabs too.
  - *Check (code):* every bulk close the app has (close others, close all, close unmodified, close to the left and
    to the right) builds the list of tabs it will close without the pinned ones: it tests each tab for pinned
    before taking it (Editora's `closeOtherTabs`, `closeAllTabs`, `closeUnmodifiedTabs`, `eligibleToLeft` and
    `eligibleToRight`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java). Termina [`ui/TabRanges.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TabRanges.java) (`closing`, which leaves
    out every pinned position and which each bulk close of [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) goes through) and
    [`TabRangesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/TabRangesTest.java).

- **TABS-05 · MUST.** Pinning moves the tab to the end of the pinned group, unpinning to just after it.
  - *Check (code):* the code that pins or unpins a tab then moves it to the boundary between the pinned tabs and
    the rest, the index equal to the number of other pinned tabs in its strip: the last place of the pinned group
    for a tab just pinned, the first place after the group for one just unpinned (Editora's `togglePin`, which
    calls `moveToPinBoundary`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) (`togglePin`), [`ui/EditorArea.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/EditorArea.java) (`moveToPinBoundary`).
    Termina [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (`togglePin`, which counts the other pinned tabs and moves the tab to
    that index).

- **TABS-06 · MUST.** Reopen Closed Tab brings back the files whose tabs this window closed, newest first, bounded
  to twenty, a file listed once, with the caret where it was. In a terminal app the *tab* comes back (its shells,
  their directories, the pane arrangement, the names the user gave them, its place in the strip) and not the
  scrollback.
  - *Why:* the process is gone, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so.
  - *Check (code):* each window keeps a list of the tabs it closed, newest first and no longer than twenty; the
    command takes the newest entry and opens it. In an app whose tabs hold files, an entry is the file, whether an
    editor's tab or a viewer's showed it, with the caret where the tab has one; closing a file again replaces its
    earlier entry, and reopening puts the caret back. In a terminal app, an entry holds the tab's panes with each
    one's shell and directory, their arrangement, the names the user gave them and the tab's place in the strip, and
    no scrollback. A test over the list is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/ClosedTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ClosedTabs.java), [`ClosedTabsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ClosedTabsTest.java); `C-S-t` in the CUA keymap. Editora
    doesn't yet for its image, hex and PDF viewer tabs: `rememberClosed` in [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) records
    the file of an editor's tab alone, so a closed viewer tab does not come back. Termina
    [`ui/ClosedTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ClosedTabs.java) and [`ClosedTabsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/ClosedTabsTest.java), on `Ctrl+Shift+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS).

- **TABS-07 · SHOULD.** Tabs reorder by dragging, with this feedback: the dragged header dimmed and an
  accent line on the edge where it will land.
  - *Check (by hand):* drag a tab along the strip and watch the landing edge.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`TabHeaders.enableTabDrag`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabHeaders.java); Termina `installTabDrag` and the pure [`TabReorder.insertIndex`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TabReorder.java).
    In Termina a double-click on a tab renames it, and a pane dragged onto a tab joins it (the whole header
    outlined, `tab-drop-into`).

- **TABS-08 · SHOULD.** In an app whose tabs hold files, a tab shows its file's Git status in the Project tree's
  colors: modified accent, added green, untracked olive, renamed violet, deleted muted, conflict red. A read-only
  tab still shows it; an unsaved one shows amber. The tab's tooltip names the file's Git status too, so color is
  not the status's only sign ([ACC-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/accessibility/#acc-05)). A terminal app's tabs hold no files, so the
  rule passes it by.
  - *Check (code):* the code that styles a tab gives it, for its file's Git status, the style class the Project
    tree gives that file's row, read-only or not, and the stylesheet lets the unsaved tab's amber win over it; and
    the code that sets the tab's tooltip adds the status in words (modified, added, untracked and the rest) when
