Torrenta and nux, which ship no keymap files, bind the same
    chord in code ([`ui/Chords.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Chords.java); nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `Shortcut+Comma`). Modula doesn't yet: its Settings command has no chord
    ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `commands`).

- **SET-02 · MUST.** The Settings window has a sidebar of pages with icons on the left, the open page on the right,
  and a search field on top.
  - *Check (by hand):* open Settings: the pages are listed in a sidebar on the left, each with an icon, the open
    page fills the right, and the search field sits above both.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java), [`ui/SettingsSidebarNav.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSidebarNav.java), [`ui/SettingsIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsIcons.java).

- **SET-03 · MUST.** The Settings window's search finds a row by its title, description, visible text, its card or
  section heading, its page name and English keywords. Title hits rank above description hits; whole words above
  word starts. The page with the best match opens, and every non-matching row, heading and card is hidden.
  - *Check (code):* the Settings search matches a query against each row's title, description, visible text, card
    or section heading, page name and keywords; its score puts a title hit above a description hit and a whole word
    above a word start; and it opens the page of the best match and hides every row, heading and card that does
    not match. A unit test that ranks a title hit above a keyword hit and a whole word above part of one is the
    surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsSearch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSearch.java), [`SettingsSearchTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSearchTest.java)
    (`aTitleHitOutranksAKeywordHitAndAWholeWordOutranksPartOfOne`). Torrenta's search doesn't rank a whole word
    above part of one yet: its score looks only at where the text was found, title, description or keywords
    ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java), `rank`).

- **SET-04 · MUST.** Settings apply live, with no Save button. Text fields commit on Enter or focus loss; invalid
  values are marked and never committed. A setting that cannot apply until a restart says so on its own row.
  - *Check (code):* the Settings window has no Save or Apply button, and each control writes its setting and
    applies it when it changes; a text field commits its value on Enter and when it loses focus (Editora's
    `commitOnEnterOrBlur`), and a value that fails validation is marked and not written; and every setting the app
    reads only at startup (the language, the window's style) names the restart in its own row's text.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`SettingsWindow.commitOnEnterOrBlur`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java); [`SettingsSyncPage`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java)'s branch field marks an invalid
    branch. Rows that wait for a restart say so: Editora's interface language ("Applies after restarting Editora.",
    `settings.uiLanguage.note`), and Torrenta's tray icon, which on Windows and macOS "applies after restarting
    Torrenta" (`settings.general.trayIcon.desc`, in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java)). nux doesn't yet: its Settings
    window writes nothing until its Save button is pressed, and has a Cancel beside it
    ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/SettingsWindow.java)).

- **SET-05 · SHOULD.** A setting changed in one window reaches every other open window of the app.
  - *Check (code):* every window reads its settings from one model the windows share, and a change to that model
    is announced to each open window, which applies it. An FX test that changes a setting in one window and finds
    it applied in the other is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora: every window holds the same [`config/SharedConfig.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/SharedConfig.java), which announces each change
    (`onSettingsChanged`); [`CrossWindowSettingsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CrossWindowSettingsFxTest.java).

### Adding a setting touches five places

- **SET-06 · MUST.** Every setting the Settings window shows has a palette command that flips the field or prompts
  for its value. A key that [SET-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-16) keeps out of the UI has no row, and takes no command.
  - *Check (code):* list the settings the Settings window's rows change and the commands the palette lists; each
    setting has a command that flips it or prompts for its value. A row that only shows something, or runs an
    action, has no setting to give a command to. A test that fails on a row with no command is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`ui/SettingCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingCommands.java), a command for each setting or the reason a row needs none
    ([`SettingCommandsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/SettingCommandsTest.java), `everySettingsRowHasACommandOrSaysWhyNot`), and Mirada [`ui/SettingsPages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/SettingsPages.java), where
    every row names its command ([`SettingsPagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/SettingsPagesTest.java), `everyPageHasRowsAndEveryRowAPaletteCommand`). Editora has its
    `view.toggle…` and picker commands ([`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)) but not one for every setting yet:
    `terminalNotifications`, for one, is only a Settings row. Modula's palette changes one of its settings, the
    daylight theme ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `commands`), and nux's three: the tray metric, the notification rule and
    start at login ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `registerCommands`).

### Config folder and schema

- **SET-07 · MUST.** Config lives in `~/.<app>`, a folder in the user's home on Windows, macOS and Linux alike,
  unless `<APP>_CONFIG_DIR` or a command-line flag ([CLI-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-02)) names another folder. A flag
  wins over the variable, since what is typed on the command line is the more specific instruction: `--config-dir`
  first, then `--dev`, then the variable.
  - *Check (code):* one resolver picks the folder from `--config-dir`, `--dev`, the environment variable and the
    default, with `--config-dir` first, `--dev` next, the variable after it and the default last, whichever of the
    two flags is typed first; and the default is `<user.home>/.<app>` on Windows, macOS and Linux alike: the
    resolver doesn't branch on the OS, or a test resolves the default as each OS and finds the same folder.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`config/ConfigDir.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigDir.java) (`resolve`: `--config-dir`, `--dev`, the variable, then
    `~/.exampleapp`, with no branch on the OS; [`ConfigDirTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigDirTest.java), `configDirThenDevThenEnvironmentThenPropertyThenTheDefault`). No app
    has all of it yet. Editora ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) and [`ConfigManager.configDirFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigManager.java), [`ConfigDirTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigDirTest.java)),
    and Termina ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), `defaultFile`) put
    `--config-dir` first and have one default for every OS, but the variable wins over `--dev`, which only changes
    the default. In Mirada either flag wins over the variable, but the two flags set one value and the one typed
    last wins, so `--config-dir X --dev` gives `~/.mirada-dev` ([`Launch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/Launch.java), `parse`); and its default depends on
    the OS ([`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java), `defaultFile` and `folder`): `~/Library/Application Support/Mirada` on
    macOS, `%APPDATA%\Mirada` on Windows, `~/.mirada` elsewhere. Torrenta has `--config-dir`, the variable and the
    default in that order and no `--dev` ([`store/ConfigDir.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/ConfigDir.java)). Modula and nux read a fixed `~/.modula` and
    `~/.nux`, with no flag and no variable.

- **SET-08 · SHOULD.** Preferences live in one file and session state (where the window was, what was open) in
  another, and every other store has a file of its own. Editora's are `settings.json` and `workspace-state.json`.
  - *Check (code):* preferences and session state are separate files: the file that holds what the user chose in
    Settings holds no window geometry and no list of open items.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/ConfigManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigManager.java) (`SETTINGS_FILE_NAME`, `WORKSPACE_FILE_NAME`), [`config/WorkspaceState.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/WorkspaceState.java);
    Termina [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), which writes the same two names and sorts each key into one of them (`isStateKey`).
    Torrenta and Mirada keep the window's bounds in their preferences file (`ui.window.bounds` and `window.bounds`
    in `settings.properties`). The app template meets it: the window and the open documents go to
    `session.json`, beside `settings.json` and never in it (`SESSION_FILE` in [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java); its
    [`config/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Migrations.java) moves them out of an older `settings.json`).

- **SET-09 · MUST.** Every config file the app writes and reads back carries a schema version, and each version has
  a `v → v+1` migration step. A purely additive field uses an identity step. Which files are config files is in
  [SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-22); a plain list with one item to a line, such as a word list, has no shape to version and is
  exempt.
  - *Check (code):* the store of every config file ([SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-22) says which files those are) declares a schema
    version (`SCHEMA_VERSION` in Editora), writes it into the file and reads it back, and the migrations hold one
    step for every version below the current one, an identity step where the version only added a field.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java), [`ConfigSchema.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigSchema.java) (one entry for each
    store), [`ConfigMigrationsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrationsTest.java); its `dictionary.txt`, one word to a line, is the
    kind of list the rule exempts. Termina ([`config/ConfigJson.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/ConfigJson.java), for `settings.json` and
    `workspace-state.json`) and Mirada ([`settings/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Migrations.java), for `settings.properties` and
    `bookmarks.properties`) do it too, and so does the app template for `settings.json`
    ([`config/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Migrations.java)) and for `session.json` (`SESSION_SCHEMA` in
    [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java)), Settings Sync's `base.json` and `keybindings.json`
    ([`sync/SyncData.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncData.java), `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `migrate`) and the account it pins (`account.json`,
    [`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java)). Nor does Termina for the color schemes it
    imports: each is a file Termina writes whole, in a format of its own, and reads back at start
    (`themes/<name>.properties`, [`theme/ThemeFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/theme/ThemeFile.java)), so a config file by [SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-22), and it carries no
    version. Torrenta's files ([`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java) and
    the other stores beside it) and Modula's ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/ConfigStore.java): `settings.properties`, `presets.txt`,
    `schedules.txt`, each line a record with fields) carry no version, and nux writes `schema=1` into its file and never reads it
    ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/ConfigStore.java), `format` and `parse`).

- **SET-10 · MUST.** A config file whose schema version ([SET-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-09)) is higher than the running build's is
  kept as a backup beside it (Editora names it `<name>.v<n>.bak`) and defaults load.
  - *Why:* an older build never clobbers a newer config.
  - *Check (code):* the load of each config file compares the file's schema version with the build's, and for a
    higher one keeps the file as a backup beside it and loads the defaults. A test that loads such a file and finds
    the backup beside it and the defaults loaded is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ConfigVersioningTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigVersioningTest.java) (`tooNewSettingsAreBackedUpAndDefaultsLoaded`). Termina
    ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java)), Mirada ([`settings/ConfigFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFile.java), `newerBackupOf`) and the app template
    ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java)) do the same, under the same name. Torrenta, Modula and nux read no version
    ([SET-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-09)), so they cannot tell a newer file, and nor can Termina for an imported color scheme, which
    carries none.

- **SET-11 · MUST.** Never trust a config file. Clamp every value to its valid range when it is **read**, not only
  when it is written; an unknown value falls back to its default; a file that cannot be decoded is kept as a backup
  (Editora names it `<name>.corrupt.bak`) and defaults load. A bad file never stops the app from starting.
  - *Why:* config is plain JSON (or properties) and people edit it by hand. A hand-edited two-million-line
    scrollback must not exhaust memory at the next launch (Termina).
  - *Check (code):* the load clamps each value to its range as it reads it and puts the default in place of an
    unknown one; a file the parser cannot decode is kept as a backup and the defaults load; and the load catches
    what the parser throws besides an `IOException` (a malformed `\uXXXX` escape in a `.properties` file throws an
    `IllegalArgumentException`), so no file stops the start. A test that loads out-of-range numbers and an
    unparseable file of that kind is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java) (`keepCorrupt`), [`ConfigLoadProblemsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigLoadProblemsTest.java)
    (`outOfRangeNumbersAreClampedOnLoad`, `anUnparseableFileIsReportedWithItsBackup`); Termina
    [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), [`SettingsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/config/SettingsTest.java) (`aMalformedEscapeNoLongerStopsTheAppStarting`); Mirada
    [`settings/ConfigFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFile.java), which moves a file that will not decode to `<name>.corrupt.bak`
    ([`ConfigFileTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFileTest.java), `aFileThatWillNotDecodeIsKeptAsABackup`). Torrenta, Modula and nux keep no backup, and in
    Torrenta and nux a malformed escape stops the app from starting.

- **SET-22 · MUST.** A config file is written whole or not at all: the app writes a temporary file beside it and
  moves that into place, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half-written file. A config file is any file the app
  writes as a whole and reads back as its state: the settings, the session state, a store of bookmarks or presets,
  what a sync engine keeps beside its clone. A file the app only appends to (a log, a ledger, a word list) is not
  one, and neither is a file in the working tree of a sync repository's clone, which Git holds a committed copy of
  and the next sync writes again. Nor is a file the app writes for one run and deletes at exit, such as one that
  tells another process where this run listens.
  - *Why:* without it, a crash or a full disk in the middle of a save leaves a file that will not decode, and the
    corrupt-file path of [SET-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-11), a backup and then defaults, is what the person gets for it.
  - *Check (code):* every write of a config file as a whole (a store's save, an import, a sync engine's own state
    outside its clone) goes to a temporary file in the same folder and ends in a move onto the target (`Files.move`).
    `ATOMIC_MOVE` is the surest form; a move that only replaces the target passes too, since the statement asks for
    the temporary file and the move. An append to a log, a ledger or a list is not such a write, and neither is a
    write into a sync clone's working tree, nor the write of a file the app deletes when it exits.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/ConfigWriter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigWriter.java) (`writeAtomicOrThrow`: a temporary file of its own beside the target,
    forced to disk, then moved; [`ConfigWriterTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigWriterTest.java), `atomicReplacementFailuresKeepThePreviousConfiguration`), which
    its settings and stores go through. Editora's `mcp-endpoint.json` is not a config file: its MCP server writes it
    for the run when it starts and deletes it when it stops, as the last window closes
    ([`mcp/McpServer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/mcp/McpServer.java), `writeEndpointFile` and `stop`), and one that a crash left behind is deleted at the next
    launch (`reapStaleEndpoint`). Every other
    app's settings store does it too: Torrenta [`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java) (`save`), Termina [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java) (`writeOne`,
    `moveIntoPlace`), Mirada [`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java) (`write`), Modula [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/ConfigStore.java) (`writeAtomically`), nux
    [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/ConfigStore.java) (`save`) and the app template's [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java) (`writePending`, for `settings.json` and
    `session.json`). The template's other whole-file writes go the same way, through [`config/ConfigFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigFiles.java)
    (`write`): an import ([`config/ConfigImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigImport.java), `apply`), Settings Sync's `base.json`, the merge base it
    keeps beside the clone ([`sync/SyncData.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncData.java), `write`), and the account it pins there
    ([`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java)). Termina's [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/SyncEngine.java) and Torrenta's [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncEngine.java) write in place only inside
    the clone, and keep their merge base as a Git ref (`refs/termina/base`, `refs/torrenta/base`).

- **SET-12 · MUST.** Export configuration writes a timestamped `.zip` of the config folder; Import restores from
  one.
  - *Check (code):* the export command writes a `.zip` that carries the time of the export in its name and the
    config folder's files among its entries, and the import command reads such a zip and restores its files. A test
    of each is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/ConfigExporter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigExporter.java), [`config/ConfigImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigImport.java), [`ConfigExporterTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigExporterTest.java)
    (`zipNameDropsLeadingDotAndEmbedsVersionUserTime`, `exportZipsAllFilesWithRelativeEntries`),
    [`ConfigImportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigImportTest.java) (`theTickedPartsReplaceTheirsHereAndNothingElseChanges`: Editora's import restores the parts the
    user ticks).

### Secrets stay out of files

- **SET-13 · MUST.** An app that stores a secret the user gave it (a password, a token, a key) puts none in a config
  file. Each goes to the operating system's keychain: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service
  on Linux. Calls may block on a prompt, so they run off the FX thread. Where no keychain answers, as in a Linux
  session with no Secret Service, the secret is kept in memory for the session only and its row in Settings says so:
  it is never written to a file instead. A run with no window says so on standard error. A key or token the app
  generates itself is not such a secret: it may live in a file only the owner can read, outside the settings files
  (Torrenta's `keys/<name>.key`). Whether a credential is kept from one session to the next is the app's to decide:
  one it keeps is this rule's, and one it only holds for the session, and asks for again in the next, is
  [SET-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-14)'s.
  - *Check (code):* the rule covers an app that keeps a password, an API key or a token the user gave it from one
    session to the next; an app that keeps none is outside it. In an app it covers, no such secret is a field of
    the settings model or is written to any other file; reads and writes go through the secret store, and
    every caller reaches it from a background thread, never from a handler on the FX thread; the store's fallback,
    for when no keychain answers, holds the secret in memory and writes no file, and the secret's row in Settings
    says when it is kept for the session only, as a line on standard error does in a run with no window. A key or
    token the app generates is not judged as such a secret where it is in a file of its own, outside the settings
    files, that the app makes readable by its owner alone (owner-only permissions, where the file system has them).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`secrets/SecretStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/secrets/SecretStore.java), [`config/ApiKeyVault.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ApiKeyVault.java). Editora doesn't yet: [`Settings`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java)
    keeps the AI keys as a fallback for when no keychain answers, and saving a key from Settings writes the keychain
    on the FX thread. Its Settings row does say which of the two holds the key. The bearer token Editora's MCP
    server generates is in a file of its own for the run, `mcp-endpoint.json`, made owner-only where the file system
    has POSIX permissions and deleted when the server stops ([`mcp/McpServer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/mcp/McpServer.java), `writeEndpointFile`), which
    the rule allows. Torrenta uses no keychain: its proxy
    password and the password of its Remote access certificate file (`proxy.password` and `webapi.httpsPassword` in
    `settings.properties`, [`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java)), its Torznab keys (`search-providers.json`) and its remote-profile
    passwords (`profiles.json`) are in plain text in its config folder; of its Remote access password it keeps only
    a hash. The keys Torrenta generates for the updatable torrents it publishes are where the rule allows: a file
    each, outside the settings files and owner-only where the file system has permissions (`keys/<name>.key`,
    [`store/KeyStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/KeyStore.java)). Termina, Mirada and Modula store no secret, so the rule does
    not cover them: Termina's sync signs in through the user's own Git and `gh`
    ([`sync/SyncAccount.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/SyncAccount.java)), and the other two ask for none. nux's one credential is for the session only,
    and so are the SSH passwords and passphrases Editora asks for ([SET-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-14)).

- **SET-14 · MUST.** An app that asks for a credential it does not keep from one session to the next holds it in
  memory for the session only and never writes it. Whether to keep a credential is the app's to decide: one it
  keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-13)'s, in the keychain and never in a config file, and this rule covers only one it does
  not keep. Work that needs such a credential waits until the user has signed in this session; do not "fix" that
  by writing the password to a file.
  - *Check (code):* for each credential the app asks the user for (a login, a password, a passphrase), find whether
    the app keeps it for the next session. One it keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-13)'s and is not judged here. One it does
    not keep is a field of a runtime object, absent from every config class, and no code writes it to a file. An
    app that asks for no credential, or keeps every one it asks for, is outside the rule.
  - *Reference:* nux's UPS login: the user name and password it asks for are two fields of a runtime object
    ([`app/CommandRunner.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/CommandRunner.java)), in no config class. Editora asks for an SSH password or a key's passphrase while a
    login runs ([`vfs/LoginPrompt.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/vfs/LoginPrompt.java)) and stores neither: a saved connection holds the host, the user and the key's
    path ([`config/ConnectionStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConnectionStore.java)). What an app keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-13)'s alone: Editora's AI keys, and
    Torrenta's proxy, Torznab and remote-profile secrets. Termina, Mirada and Modula ask for no credential.

- **SET-15 · MUST.** An app with Settings Sync refuses a repository URL with a password or token in it, and says
  what to use instead: a Git credential helper or an SSH URL ([Settings Sync](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/settings-sync/)). A
  problem report's redaction is [DIAG-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-11).
  - *Check (by hand):* paste `https://user:token@host/repo.git` as the sync repository: the page refuses it, with
    a message that says what to use instead.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java) (`settings.sync.repo.credentials`), which asks
    [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncEngine.java) (`hasCredentials`) as the URL is typed, when the field commits and again at Connect.

- **SET-16 · MUST.** An option that weakens security has no UI: it exists only as a key in the config file, so
  nobody turns it on by clicking. An option weakens security when it switches off a check or a question the app
  otherwise makes to protect the user; a feature, such as remote access or a proxy, is not such an option.
  - *Check (code):* no Settings row or command writes the key of an option that switches off a check or a question the
    app otherwise makes to protect the user, whichever of its values is the weaker one: on for nux's `tlsTrustAll`,
    off for a check the app makes by default.
  - *Reference:* nux's trust-all TLS (`tlsTrustAll` in [`config/Config.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/Config.java)), and Termina's paste confirmation, which
    only its config file turns off ([`SecurityOptionsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/config/SecurityOptionsTest.java), `noControlOrCommandWritesAWeakeningOption`). Editora doesn't yet: *Require
    registry signature* for plugins is a Settings checkbox and the `plugins.toggleRequireSignature` command.

### Settings Sync (Git / GitHub)

**Applies to:** an app with Settings Sync.

- **SET-18 · SHOULD.** Settings Sync is set up by pasting a repository URL, or with **Create on GitHub** through the
  `gh` CLI. The account that can read the repository is pinned per clone, so machines with two GitHub accounts work.
  - *Check (code):* the Sync page takes a repository URL in a field and offers a Create on GitHub action that runs
    `gh`; and the sync code finds which of the signed-in GitHub accounts can read the repository, records it with
    the clone, and uses that account for the clone from then on. A test that remembers the first account that can
    read the repository and uses it without asking again is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`sync/SyncAccount.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncAccount.java), [`SyncAccountTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/sync/SyncAccountTest.java), [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java). The app template's
    [`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java) finds the first signed-in `gh` account whose token can read the repository, records it beside the
    clone and passes it to every fetch and push from then on ([`AccountPinTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPinTest.java), `theFirstAccountThatCanReadIsPinnedAndKept`).

- **SET-19 · SHOULD.** Settings Sync runs automatically (on change and at start) and on demand. Machine-local keys
  (window size, paths) never sync.
  - *Check (code):* a sync starts by itself after startup and after a local change, and a command starts one on
    demand (`sync.now` in Editora); and no machine-local key or file (window size, a path) is among those the sync
    sends to the repository.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsSync.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSync.java) (after startup, after a local change, on an interval, and
    `sync.now`), [`sync/SyncCategory.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncCategory.java); Torrenta [`sync/SyncKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncKeys.java).

- **SET-20 · SHOULD.** When Settings Sync finds one entry changed on both sides, *this machine wins*, and a backup
  is taken before any sync that replaces local files.
  - *Check (code):* the merge keeps this machine's value for an entry both sides changed, and the sync copies the
    local files to a backup before it replaces them. A merge test where both sides changed one entry is the surest
    evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`sync/SyncMerge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncMerge.java), [`SyncMergeTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/sync/SyncMergeTest.java); the app template's [`sync/SyncMerge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncMerge.java) and
    [`ui/SyncController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SyncController.java) (`backUp`, which copies `settings.json` to `backups/` before a merge replaces the local bindings;
    [`SyncControllerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SyncControllerFxTest.java), `aSyncThatReplacesLocalSettingsBacksThemUpFirst`).

- **SET-21 · SHOULD.** Settings Sync shows its status as a pill in Settings and as echo messages; its failures go to
  the Message Log.
  - *Check (by hand):* point Sync at a repository that does not exist: the pill in Settings shows the failure, the
    echo area says it, and the Message Log keeps it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java), [`SyncStatus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SyncStatus.java).

## Diagnostics and support (DIAG)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/: Message Log, Debug Log, update notification, Report a Problem, Doctor and crash recovery.

- **DIAG-01 · MUST.** The **Message Log** is a session-only, bounded history of every echo-area message with
  `HH:mm:ss` times, newest first. Esc closes it; Clear empties it. What opens it, a click on the echo area, is
  [WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-01)'s to require; the [Message Log template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/message-log/) has the rest.
  - *Check (code):* every message the echo area shows is added, with its time, to one log held in memory and never
    written to disk; the log drops its oldest entry past a fixed count and lists the rest newest first with
    `HH:mm:ss` times; and its window closes on Esc and has a Clear action that empties it. A test that records
    messages newest first, evicts the oldest past the cap, and clears is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) ([`MessageLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogTest.java)), [`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java).

- **DIAG-02 · MUST.** The **Debug Log** captures all `java.util.logging` records and uncaught exceptions in memory
  (bounded) **and** mirrors them to a session file in the config folder, keeping the previous session's file so a
  crash is still visible next launch. Editora names the two `<app>-session.log` and `<app>-session.prev.log`.
  - *Check (code):* a handler on the root `java.util.logging` logger and the uncaught exception handler feed one
    bounded buffer in memory and a session file in the config folder, and at start the last session's file is kept
    under a second name before the new one is begun. Tests that bound the buffer and find the session file written
    and the previous one kept are the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java) ([`DebugLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogTest.java), [`DebugLogSessionFileTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogSessionFileTest.java)).

- **DIAG-03 · MUST.** The Debug Log opens in a modeless window with Refresh, Copy, Clear, Export and Report a
  Problem. The window's find bar is [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-01).
  - *Why:* it is the only way to see logs in a packaged build.
  - *Check (code):* the Debug Log's window is a stage with no modality, so the main window keeps working while it
    is open, and it carries the five actions: Refresh, Copy, Clear, Export and Report a Problem.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogWindow.java). Termina's, Mirada's and the app template's windows have the
    five actions too; Torrenta's has no Export ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)). Modula and nux have no Debug Log
    ([DIAG-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-02)).

- **DIAG-04 · MUST.** An **uncaught exception handler** is installed at the start of `main`, before the toolkit
  starts, and routes to the Debug Log and an echo message. Never a stack trace dialog.
  - *Check (code):* `main` calls the install method before any argument handling or `launch`, and the handler
    posts an error to the echo area, and opens no dialog.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`DebugLog.install()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java) for the install and the log. The echo message is posted by Termina
    ([`ui/WindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java), through `DebugLog.onUncaught`), the app template ([`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)) and Mirada
    ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java), `uncaught`). Editora's handler and Torrenta's ([`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DebugLog.java)) log the exception
    but do not yet post one.

- **DIAG-05 · MUST.** The **update check** reads GitHub `/releases/latest`. The automatic check runs once per app
  session (not per window), at most once a day, and starts at least three seconds after the first frame
  ([PERF-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/performance/#perf-15)); a check the user asks for ([DIAG-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-10)) runs when asked. It never
  downloads or installs anything by itself.
  - *Check (code):* the code that starts the automatic check waits for the first frame and then a delay of three
    seconds or more before it asks GitHub's `/releases/latest` for the app's repository (Editora's
    `AfterFirstPaint`, then a pause of five seconds); it asks once for the whole process, however many windows
    open, and not at all when the last check, whose time the app keeps from one session to the next, was less than
    a day ago, or when the setting is off ([DIAG-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-10)); and what it does
    with the answer is show it: no code downloads or installs a release. A test that asserts the wait, the one
    check a session and the two skips is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`update/UpdateCheck.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/update/UpdateCheck.java), [`ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java) ([`UpdateCheckSchedulerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckSchedulerTest.java),
    `waitsForTheFirstPaintThenTheDelayThenStampsAndChecks` and `onlyOnceASessionAndNotWhenOffOrNotDue`),
    [`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java); Editora waits five
    seconds (`UpdateCheckScheduler.DELAY`). Termina ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java), three seconds after its first frame), Mirada
    ([`update/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/update/UpdateCoordinator.java), `scheduleStartupCheck`, five seconds) and the app template
    ([`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java), started from [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java) after the first paint, five seconds) wait the same way. Three apps
    don't wait yet: Torrenta starts its check as soon as its engine is ready ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java),
    `maybeCheckForUpdates`), and Modula ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java), `checkForUpdates`) and nux ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java),
    `maybeCheckForUpdates`) start theirs inside `start()`.

- **DIAG-09 · MUST.** When the update check ([DIAG-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-05)) finds a newer version, the status bar says so,
  naming the version and linking its release. About's line for the last check is
  [ABOUT-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-02).
  - *Check (code):* when a check finds a newer version, the app shows a notice in the status bar that names that
    version, and the notice, or a link beside it in the bar, opens that release's page (Editora's
    `UpdateCoordinator` shows a status-bar segment whose click opens the release).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java). Mirada ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/StatusBar.java)) and the app template
    ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StatusBar.java)) show a link in the bar, and Torrenta a badge there that opens the release
    ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), `updateBadge`). Termina and Modula don't link the release yet: their status message
    names the version and nothing in the bar opens it (Termina's `status.updateAvailable`, posted from
    [`ui/WindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java); Modula's [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `setAvailableUpdate`). nux doesn't meet it
    either: it has no status bar, and shows a button in its toolbar that opens the release
    ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `refreshUpdateNotice`).

- **DIAG-10 · MUST.** **Check for Updates** runs the update check ([DIAG-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-05)) by hand, as a command in the
  palette and in the Help menu, where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the
  app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines), and Settings has an off switch for the automatic
  check.
  - *Check (code):* the command (`help.checkForUpdates` in Editora) is registered and, in an app with a Help menu,
    listed there, and the scheduler skips the automatic check while the setting is off.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`help.checkForUpdates`),
    [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java) (`settings.checkForUpdates`), [`ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java).
    Mirada lists the command in the Help submenu of its main menu ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java), `help`) and in the Help
    menu of its macOS menu bar. nux, which has no menu bar, registers the command for its palette
    (`app.checkUpdates` in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)).

- **DIAG-06 · MUST.** **Report a Problem** is a command, listed in the Help menu where the app has one, that builds a
  report: the app's version, the OS, the runtime, a summary of the settings and the recent Debug Log. Its redaction
  is [DIAG-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-11), its window [DIAG-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-12) and the limit on the issue link's length
  [DIAG-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-13). The same report from the command line, for when the app cannot start, is
  [CLI-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-05).
  - *Check (code):* the command (`help.reportProblem` in Editora) is registered and, in an app with a Help menu,
    listed there, and the text it builds carries the app's version, the OS, the Java and JavaFX versions, a summary
    of the settings and the end of the Debug Log.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/report/ProblemReport.java) ([`ProblemReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/report/ProblemReportTest.java),
    `itCarriesTheEnvironmentTheUsefulSettingsAndTheEndOfTheLog`), the app template's
    [`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/report/ProblemReport.java) and Mirada's [`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/report/ProblemReport.java). Editora's
    ([`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReport.java), `help.reportProblem` in [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)) and Torrenta's
    ([`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/report/ProblemReport.java)) carry the system details and the last two session logs, and no settings
    summary yet. Modula and nux have no problem report.

- **DIAG-11 · MUST.** An app's problem report ([DIAG-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-06)) is **redacted** before it is shown: home paths,
  user names, e-mail addresses, credentials and tokens are replaced.
  - *Check (code):* the text the Report a Problem window shows has been through the redactor, and the redactor
    replaces home paths, user names, e-mail addresses, credentials in URLs and tokens. Redaction tests that cover
    each of the five are the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`report/Redactor.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/Redactor.java) ([`RedactorTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/report/RedactorTest.java)), applied in
    [`ProblemReport.assemble`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReport.java) before the window gets the text. The other four apps with a report do it too:
    Termina ([`RedactorTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/report/RedactorTest.java)), Torrenta ([`RedactorTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/report/RedactorTest.java)), Mirada ([`RedactorTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/report/RedactorTest.java)) and the app
    template ([`ReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/report/ReportTest.java), `redactsPrivateDetails`).

- **DIAG-12 · MUST.** The Report a Problem window shows the report in a field the user can edit. Its submit action
  copies the report, as edited, to the clipboard and opens a GitHub issue prefilled from the repository's
  `bug_report.yml` form. Nothing is uploaded: the user submits the issue.
  - *Check (code):* the window's report field is editable; its submit action puts the field's text on the clipboard
    and opens a new-issue link that names `bug_report.yml` as its template and carries the report in the form's
    fields; and the report's code opens that link in the browser and makes no network request of its own.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java) ([`ReportProblemWindowFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ReportProblemWindowFxTest.java),
    `theEditedReportIsCopiedAndFilledIntoTheIssue`), [`ProblemReport.issueUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReport.java). Termina's
    [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java), Torrenta's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java), Mirada's
    [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java) and the app template's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java) do the same. The
    five differ in one thing the rule does not ask. Only Termina sends everything as the user left it: its
    environment block (version, runtime, OS) is a second editable field. The other four fill the form's environment
    field from the block as the app built it, whatever the user edits: Editora and Torrenta show the block at the top of the editable report, Mirada shows it as a label, and
    the app template does not show it.

- **DIAG-13 · MUST.** When the issue link that Report a Problem prefills ([DIAG-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-12)) would be longer than
  7,500 characters, the report stays out of the link: the form's report field asks the user to paste the report
  from the clipboard, where DIAG-12 has put it.
  - *Check (code):* the code that builds the issue link puts the report in the form's report field while the link
    stays within 7,500 characters, and past that puts the paste hint in that field instead. A test that builds the
    link for a short report and for a long one is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ProblemReport.issueUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReport.java) (`MAX_URL_LENGTH`, 7500; [`ProblemReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/report/ProblemReportTest.java),
    `aShortReportGoesIntoTheIssueLinkItself` and `aLongReportLeavesThePasteHintInstead`). Torrenta
    ([`ProblemReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/report/ProblemReportTest.java), `aShortReportGoesInTheLinkAndALongOneLeavesTheHint`), Mirada ([`ProblemReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/report/ProblemReportTest.java),
    `aLongReportAsksForAPaste`) and the app template ([`ReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/report/ReportTest.java),
    `issueLinkFillsTheFormOrFallsBackToTheClipboard`) do the same at the same limit. Termina has the limit
    (`MAX_LINK_LENGTH`; [`ProblemReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/report/ProblemReportTest.java), `aLongReportFallsBackToTheClipboard`) but not the hint yet: past it,
    its link leaves the form's report field empty, and only its own window says to paste
    ([`report/ProblemReport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/report/ProblemReport.java), `link`; `report.paste`).

- **DIAG-07 · SHOULD.** A **Doctor** page checks the environment (external tools, versions, permissions, paths),
  with a status per row and a fix or link for each failure.
  - *Check (by hand):* open the Doctor with a tool missing and find its row failed, with what to install.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`sync/Doctor.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/Doctor.java) and [`ui/DoctorWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DoctorWindow.java), opened by `help.doctor` and from Settings: a row
    for each tool it uses, `git` failed with what to install and a link when it is missing ([`DoctorTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/sync/DoctorTest.java),
    `aMissingToolFailsItsRowWithWhatToInstall`). Editora `doctor/*`, [`ui/DoctorPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DoctorPane.java).

- **DIAG-08 · SHOULD.** An app with user documents snapshots unsaved work off the FX thread and offers it back after
  a crash.
  - *Check (code):* unsaved documents are written to snapshot files from a background thread while the user works,
    and the first window opened after a crash finds the abandoned session's snapshots and offers them back. A test
    that finds an abandoned session's snapshots and offers them to the first window only is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`recovery/RecoveryService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/recovery/RecoveryService.java) ([`RecoveryServiceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/recovery/RecoveryServiceTest.java), [`CrashRecoveryFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CrashRecoveryFxTest.java)).

## Command line and launch (CLI)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/: The flags every app accepts and the single-instance hand-off.

### Flags

- **CLI-01 · MUST.** `--help` and `--version` print before the GUI starts, in plain English, not translated.
  - *Check (code):* `main` handles both and exits before `launch`, printing fixed English text rather than
    catalog messages.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.main`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), [`App.helpText`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java); [`AppArgsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/AppArgsTest.java).

- **CLI-02 · MUST.** `--config-dir <dir>` uses another config folder, and `--dev` uses `~/.<app>-dev`, a folder in
  the user's home on Windows, macOS and Linux alike.
  - *Check (code):* the config folder is resolved from both flags before anything reads `~/.<app>`, and what
    `--dev` resolves to is `<user.home>/.<app>-dev` on Windows, macOS and Linux alike, with no branch on the OS.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.main`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) ([`ConfigManager.configDirFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigManager.java), [`App.devFlag`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)).

- **CLI-03 · SHOULD.** `--new-instance` starts a second process instead of handing off to the running one.
  - *Check (code):* the flag skips the single-instance hand-off.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.newInstanceFlag`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java).

- **CLI-04 · SHOULD.** An app that reopens what was open in its last session (documents, tabs, folders) takes
  `--no-session`, which starts it without them.
  - *Check (by hand):* launch with `--no-session` and find only the items given on the command line.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.helpText`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java). Mirada reopens nothing from its last session, so the rule does not cover
    it; it takes the flag and does nothing with it ([`Launch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/Launch.java)).

- **CLI-05 · MUST.** `--report` writes a redacted problem report to a file in the current folder, prints the file's
  path and opens the GitHub issue, without starting the GUI. Where the current folder can't be written, the file
  goes to the temp folder.
  - *Why:* the person who ran the command is looking at that folder, and has to attach the file. A report in the
    config folder is hidden from them, and one printed to the terminal is cut by its scrollback.
  - *Check (code):* `main` handles `--report` before `launch`: it writes the redacted report to a file in the
    current folder, or in the temp folder when that one can't be written, prints the file's path and opens the
    new-issue page. A test that runs the report command in a folder and finds the redacted report there, with its
    path printed, is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`report/ReportCommand.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/report/ReportCommand.java) ([`ReportCommandTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/report/ReportCommandTest.java)); Torrenta's
    [`ReportCommand.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/report/ReportCommand.java) does the same, and so does the app template's [`report/ReportCommand.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/report/ReportCommand.java)
    ([`ReportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/report/ReportTest.java), `theReportGoesInTheCurrentFolderAndItsPathIsPrinted` and
    `aCurrentFolderThatCantBeWrittenSendsTheReportToTheTempFolder`). Mirada writes its report beside the settings, and Termina
    prints its report without writing a file ([`ReportCommand.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/report/ReportCommand.java)).

- **CLI-12 · MUST.** An option the app does not know stops the launch: it names the option on standard error, says
  how to get help, and exits with status 2 before the GUI starts. That holds for an option with one dash as for one
  with two: it is never ignored and never taken for a file. Two kinds of argument are not unknown options. In an app
  that opens files named on its command line, a lone `-`, and every argument after `--`, is one of those files,
  whatever it starts with; that sentence does not cover an app that opens none. And the JVM options a launcher can
  leave among the program's arguments, `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p`, are skipped by name, each with its
  value, whether the value is the next argument or follows `=` in the same one (`--add-exports=…`): never refused,
  and the value never opened as a file. On Windows the message prints in the console, which is
  [CLI-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-11).
  - *Why:* a mistyped `--config-dir` that is ignored starts the app on the real settings, which is the one thing
    the flag was typed to avoid. Status 2 is what a script tests for a usage error. `--` is how a file whose name
    starts with a dash is opened at all. A launcher's own option is not the user's mistake, so it must not stop the
    app; it is skipped by name because a parser that skips whatever it does not know is the one that ignores a typo.
  - *Check (code):* the parser `main` runs before the GUI refuses an option the app does not define, with two
    dashes or with one, and `main` then prints the option and how to get help on standard error and exits with
    status 2 before `launch`. In an app that opens files named on its command line, the parser takes a lone `-`,
    and a name that starts with a dash after `--`, for files; in an app that opens none, this part has nothing to
    find. And the parser skips `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p` with their values, in both forms a launcher
    writes (`--add-exports <value>` and `--add-exports=<value>`), with no error and no file. A test that hands the
    parser each of these arguments is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLine.java) does all of it: it refuses an
    unknown option with one dash or two ([`Main.run`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java) prints the message and returns 2) and takes `-` and whatever
    follows `--` for files, and skips `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p` with their values in both forms
    ([`CommandLineTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLineTest.java), `reportsMistakes`, `acceptsTheEqualsFormAndDoubleDash` and
    `skipsTheLaunchersJvmOptionsAndTakesCapitalVForVersion`). No other app does all of it yet. Termina's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/cli/CommandLine.java) and Torrenta's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/cli/CommandLine.java)
    refuse both kinds of unknown option with status 2, and the launcher's options with them. Torrenta, which opens
    the `.torrent` files and magnet links named on its command line, also refuses `-` and `--`: anything that
    starts with a dash and is not a magnet link. Termina opens no files from its command line, so that part of the
    rule does not cover it (it refuses `-` as an unexpected argument and `--` as an unknown option); the launcher's
    options are all it misses. Mirada's [`Launch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/Launch.java) exits 2 on an unknown
    option with two dashes, `--add-exports` and `--add-opens` among them, and takes `-` and whatever follows `--`
    for files, but it takes a single-dash option, `-p` included, for a file too. Editora skips every option it does
    not know without a word, a lone `-` included, and has no `--`
    ([`App.fileTargets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)); that is how it gets past a leaked `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` or `-p`, whose value it opens
    only when a file of that name exists ([`AppArgsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/AppArgsTest.java)). nux reads `--minimized` and `--screenshot=` and ignores
    every other argument ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)), and Modula reads none ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)); neither opens files, so
    what they miss is the refusal.

- **CLI-13 · SHOULD.** The short flags are the same in every app: `-h` for `--help`, and both `-v` and `-V` for
  `--version`.
  - *Check (code):* the command-line parser takes `-h` for `--help`, and `-v` and `-V` for `--version`.
  - *Reference:* Termina's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/cli/CommandLine.java) and Torrenta's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/cli/CommandLine.java); the `--help` text of both
    lists `-h` and `-v` and leaves `-V` out. The app template's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLine.java) takes all three, and its
    `--help` text lists them. Editora takes `-h` and `-V` but not `-v`, Mirada has no short flags, and Modula and nux take neither flag in any form.

- **CLI-11 · MUST.** On Windows, `--help`, `--version` and `--report` print in the console they were typed in, and
  so does the message that refuses an unknown option ([CLI-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-12)). A GUI launcher has no console, so the
  installer also carries a console launcher (jpackage's `win-console`) that runs the same entry point, or `main`
  attaches to the parent's console before it prints.
  - *Why:* without it, the three flags and a mistyped option print nothing from cmd or PowerShell, and the command
    line differs on one OS.
  - *Check (code):* the Windows jpackage configuration adds a launcher with `win-console=true` that runs the app's
    own main class and lets the three flags and an unknown option reach it, or `main` calls `AttachConsole` before
    printing.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta meets it with its second launcher, `torrenta-nox`:
    [`src/jpackage/torrenta-nox-windows.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/jpackage/torrenta-nox-windows.properties) sets `win-console=true`, and its [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/pom.xml) adds that launcher
    to the image on Windows (the `os-windows` profile picks the file), beside the main launcher and on the same
    module and main class. The launcher's own `arguments=--headless` applies only when the person gives none (its
    [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/CLAUDE.md) says so), so `torrenta-nox --help`, `--version`, `--report` and an option it does not know reach
    `main` as typed, and `main` refuses the unknown option and answers the three flags before it looks for
    `--headless` ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java)). The app template does it the same way: its `os-windows` profile in
    [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) adds a second launcher, `exampleapp-cli`, whose [`packaging/windows/exampleapp-cli.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/packaging/windows/exampleapp-cli.properties)
    sets `win-console=true` and nothing else, so it runs the same main class with the arguments as typed. No other
    app has a `win-console` launcher or calls `AttachConsole`. Mirada's
    one Windows executable is its native image, copied over jpackage's launcher ([`native-app-image.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/native-app-image.sh)); whether it prints in
    the console depends on how that image is linked, which Mirada's files do not say, and no Windows run has
    confirmed it.

- **CLI-06 · SHOULD.** An app that opens files or folders (documents, images, a `.torrent`) opens the ones named
  as arguments on its command line, which its `--help` lists as `[files…]`.
  - *Check (by hand):* launch with two files and find both open, and run `--help` and find `[files…]` in its
    usage line.
