  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.fileTargets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java). Termina, Modula and nux open no files, so the rule does not cover
    them.

### Launch

- **CLI-07 · MUST.** One instance runs per config folder, unless a launch asks for another with `--new-instance`
  ([CLI-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-03)). Any other second launch hands its arguments, when it has any, to the running app over a
  local endpoint and exits. In an app that opens files, the `openFiles` Apple Events of macOS reach the running app
  too.
  - *Check (code):* the first launch on a config folder becomes the primary and listens on a local endpoint; a
    second launch without `--new-instance` sends it its arguments and exits; and, in an app that opens files, a
    handler for the macOS open-files event passes them to the running app (Editora's `MacOpenFiles`). A test that
    makes the first launch primary and delivers a second launch's arguments to it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ipc/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ipc/SingleInstance.java) ([`SingleInstanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ipc/SingleInstanceTest.java)), [`MacOpenFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/MacOpenFiles.java).
    nux doesn't yet: its second launch asks the running app to show its window and exits, handing over none of its
    arguments ([`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/instance/SingleInstance.java), `NUX-SHOW`), and what lets a second instance run on the folder is a
    setting (`singleInstance`, read in `main` of [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)), not `--new-instance`.

- **CLI-08 · SHOULD.** An advisory lock tells two processes on one config folder about each other.
  - *Check (code):* each process takes an advisory file lock in its config folder, and can tell that another
    process already holds one there. A test that takes the lock from two processes is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`config/InstanceLock.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/InstanceLock.java) ([`InstanceLockTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/InstanceLockTest.java)).

- **CLI-09 · SHOULD.** `main` sets `java.awt.headless=true` before any AWT class loads. Only these uses make AWT
  headful, in an app that has them: the tray on Windows and macOS, and on macOS the dock badge, the open-file
  handlers and Move to Trash. Linux never needs it. `main` decides once, before that point, which of them the
  settings ask for on this OS. What a tray app says when its tray is turned on after that is
  [TRAY-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/tray-and-background/#tray-14).
  - *Why:* on macOS, AWT's native toolkit and JavaFX contend for the one AppKit run loop and can hang; headless
    Java2D still draws to images.
  - *Check (code):* `main` calls `System.setProperty("java.awt.headless", …)` before `launch` and before anything
    that loads an AWT class, and the value is `"true"` unless one of the listed uses is wanted on this OS: always
    on Linux, on Windows unless the tray is on, and on macOS unless the tray, the dock badge, an open-file handler
    or, in an app that trashes through AWT, Move to Trash is.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`App.main`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), always headless, as Termina ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)) and the app template
    ([`Main.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java)) are. Torrenta [`os/AwtUse.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/AwtUse.java) (`headful`, which its `App.main` asks
    once: never on Linux, for the tray on Windows, and for the tray, the dock badge or the open-file handlers on
    macOS). Mirada [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java) (headless except on macOS, for Move to Trash: [`os/Trash.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/Trash.java), `headless`).
    Modula and nux never set the property, so AWT is headful on every OS, Linux included.

- **CLI-10 · SHOULD.** An app that starts external tools (`git`, a compiler, `ffmpeg`) resolves them through the
  login shell's `PATH` on macOS and Linux. Windows has no login shell's `PATH` to ask for, and the one the app
  inherits is used there.
  - *Why:* a `.app` launched from Finder inherits a stripped `PATH`.
  - *Check (code):* on macOS and Linux, every process the app starts gets a `PATH` that includes the login
    shell's. An app that starts no external tool is outside the rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`process/ProcessRunner.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/ProcessRunner.java) (`augmentedPath`; on Windows its login-shell probe returns
    nothing and the inherited `PATH` is used). The app template's [`sync/ShellPath.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/ShellPath.java) does the same for the `git` and `gh` it
    starts: the login shell's `PATH` before the inherited one on macOS and Linux, the inherited one on Windows
    ([`ShellPathTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/sync/ShellPathTest.java)).

## Internationalization (INTL)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/i18n/: Six languages as the floor, and the rules that keep every catalog in step.

### Languages

- **INTL-01 · MUST.** The app ships a message catalog for each of at least six languages: English (the base),
  Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian and German.
  - *Check (code):* the six `messages*.properties` files are in the app's `i18n` resources.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n).

- **INTL-02 · SHOULD.** A new language is a `messages_<code>.properties` with every key, listed in the Settings
  language picker and in the parity test.
  - *Check (code):* the language's code is in `Messages`' language list (which the picker shows) and in the
    catalog list the parity test walks.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/i18n/Messages.java) (`LANGUAGES`, `available()`); [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java)'s `LOCALES` and
    `ALL_CATALOGS`, after which `translationCatalogsHaveExactlyTheBaseKeySet` holds it to the same keys as the
    others.

- **INTL-03 · SHOULD.** Every value is translated for real: no English value is shipped in another language's
  catalog.
  - *Check (code):* compare each catalog's values with the base; a value identical to the English one is a name, a
    term or a bare pattern that stays the same in that language ("Git: Pull (Rebase)", "{0} · {1}"), never an
    untranslated sentence. No test catches it, so it is also checked in review.
  - *Reference:* Editora `messages_*.properties`.

- **INTL-04 · SHOULD.** The layout holds in every language at 1024 px wide: rows wrap, never cut. German is today's
  longest.
  - *Check (by hand):* run the app in each language with the window 1024 px wide, open each window and Settings
    page, and find no row cut off.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`messages_de.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages_de.properties).

- **INTL-05 · SHOULD.** A Chinese, Japanese or Korean catalog comes with a font fallback for its script.
  - *Why:* Inter has no CJK glyphs. JavaFX falls back to whatever font the OS has, so without a bundled one the
    text looks different on each OS, and a minimal Linux install may have none.
  - *Check (by hand):* run the app in that language and look for missing-glyph boxes.
  - *Reference:* no app yet.

- **INTL-06 · SHOULD.** An Arabic or Hebrew catalog sets `NodeOrientation.RIGHT_TO_LEFT` on every scene.
  - *Check (code):* the scene setup sets the node orientation from the current language.
  - *Reference:* no app yet.

### Rules

- **INTL-07 · SHOULD.** No raw English literal is passed to a control: every string comes from the catalog, by its
  key, through one lookup in one class (`tr("some.key")` in Editora's `Messages`).
  - *Check (code):* no source file passes a string literal in a text position: a control's constructor, `setText`,
    `setPromptText`, `setTitle`, a tooltip, a menu item or a command's label. Each takes its text from the
    catalog's lookup, which is one method of one class (Editora's `Messages.tr`). A test that scans the sources
    and fails on such a literal is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/i18n/Messages.java). The tests that hold the rule are Torrenta's
    [`UiStringSweepTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/UiStringSweepTest.java) (`noStringLiteralInATextPosition`) and nux's [`NoLiteralUiTextTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/test/java/com/nux/i18n/NoLiteralUiTextTest.java)
    (`userFacingTextGoesThroughTheCatalogue`). Editora's
    [`MessagesTest.everyLiteralKeyUsedInTheSourcesExists`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java) checks only that every key a `tr("…")` call names is in
    the base catalog, not that no literal reaches a control.

- **INTL-08 · MUST.** Every catalog has every key of the base catalog, and no more, each with a non-empty value.
  - *Check (code):* compare each translated catalog's keys with the base catalog's: none is missing, none is
    extra, and no value is empty. A parity test that fails the build on any of the three is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MessagesTest.translationCatalogsHaveExactlyTheBaseKeySet`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java),
    `translationsAreNonEmptyAndDistinctFromKeys`.

- **INTL-09 · SHOULD.** In a catalog value with a placeholder, a literal apostrophe is doubled; in a value without one,
  it is written once. Inside a `{0,choice,…}` limb ([INTL-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/i18n/#intl-12)) that itself holds a placeholder, it is
  written four times; in a limb without one it is doubled, like the rest of the value.
  - *Why:* a value with a placeholder is a `MessageFormat` pattern, where a lone apostrophe starts a quoted section
    and can swallow the placeholder after it; a value without one is shown exactly as written. A choice limb that
    holds a placeholder is parsed a second time as a pattern of its own, and each pass halves the apostrophes.
  - *Check (code):* in every catalog, a value with a placeholder has no lone apostrophe and a value without one has
    no doubled apostrophe; a choice limb that holds a placeholder writes a literal apostrophe four times, and a
    limb that holds none writes it twice. Catalog tests that fail each of the four mistakes are the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MessagesTest.aValueWithAPlaceholderNeverHasALoneApostrophe`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java),
    `aValueWithoutAPlaceholderNeverDoublesAnApostrophe`. The choice limbs are held by Torrenta's
    [`MessagesTest.apostrophesInsideChoiceLimbsAreQuotedForTheRightNumberOfPasses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`diagnosis.unavailable` in its
    [`messages_fr.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/i18n/messages_fr.properties) writes "n''''est" in a limb with `{1}`); Editora's test has no such case.

- **INTL-10 · SHOULD.** Identifiers such as line numbers and ports use `{0,number,#}`, so they are not
  digit-grouped.
  - *Check (code):* in every catalog, a placeholder the code fills with an identifier (a line number, a port)
    carries the `number,#` format, as in `{0,number,#}`, and is never a bare `{0}`. A test that formats each
    identifier argument in every locale and fails on a grouped number is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MessagesTest.identifierArgumentsAreNeverDigitGrouped`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java).

- **INTL-11 · SHOULD.** Technical identifiers stay untranslated: command ids, setting keys, file names and protocol
  names read the same in every language. The `--help` and `--version` text is [CLI-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/command-line/#cli-01).
  - *Check (code):* compare each translated catalog with the base, key by key: a command id, a setting key, a file
    name or a protocol name in the base value appears, spelled the same, in the translated value. A made-up
    example name inside a value (`name.gpg`) is not an identifier, and may be translated.
  - *Reference:* Editora's catalogs ([`messages.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages.properties) and its translations).

- **INTL-12 · SHOULD.** A message with a count words it for the count, with a `{0,choice,…}` limb for each form the
  language needs: never "file(s)".
  - *Why:* "(s)" is English; other languages change more than one ending, and the translator can only get it
    right with the forms written out.
  - *Check (code):* no catalog value has a placeholder and `(s)`; a message with a count has a `{0,choice,…}`
    pattern with a limb for each form its language needs, and every such pattern parses. A catalog test that fails
    a value with a placeholder and `(s)`, and parses every `choice` pattern in every catalog, is the surest
    evidence.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta's `omni.targets.matching` in [`messages.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/i18n/messages.properties), parsed in every language by
    [`MessagesTest.placeholdersMatchAcrossLanguagesAndEveryPatternParses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/MessagesTest.java). That test only parses the patterns: no
    app has the `(s)` test yet, and Editora's base catalog has 22 values with a placeholder and `(s)`
    (`find.replaced`, "Replaced {0} occurrence(s)").

- **INTL-13 · SHOULD.** A chord's modifiers read the same in every language: `Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift` and the macOS
  glyphs are never translated ("Ctrl", not "Strg").
  - *Why:* the keymaps, the docs and the screenshots use one spelling, and a user who changes the language keeps
    the chords they learned.
  - *Check (code):* the code that writes a chord out takes its modifier names from constants, not the catalog, and
    no catalog value writes a modifier in another language: a catalog test looks for Strg, Umschalt, Maj, Mayús and
    Maiusc.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`command/ChordFormat.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/ChordFormat.java) writes chords with untranslated modifiers. Its catalogs do not
    hold the rule yet: they translate modifiers in prose ("Strg+D", "Mayús+Tab", "Maj+Entrée") and in the Project
    Map help's key names ([`messages_de.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages_de.properties), `project.map.help.key.control=Strg`, read by
    [`ui/ProjectMapHelp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectMapHelp.java)). No app has the catalog test yet.

- **INTL-14 · MUST.** The app starts in the language the user chose in its settings, where it offers that choice;
  with none chosen, in the system's language when it ships a catalog for it; otherwise in English. The locale that
  formats dates and numbers keeps the system's region: with no language chosen it is the system's locale whole,
  whatever language the menus are in, and with one chosen it is still the system's locale when that is the system's
  own language, and the bare language only when it is another. That locale is the JVM's default once the app has
  started: the app sets it wherever it is not the locale the JVM started with. The message catalog formats its
  values with it too, never with a locale of its own made from the bare language.
  - *Why:* `de-AT` collapsed to `de` writes an Austrian's numbers and dates the German way, and an English UI on a
    French system has no reason to change how its dates are written. Apps that settle this differently format the
    same date two ways side by side, and so does one app whose catalog formats a message's number with another
    locale than the rest of the window.
  - *Check (code):* the start-up code takes the stored choice, the system's locale and the catalogs the app ships
    and gives the language and the locale as the four cases ask: none chosen with a catalog for the system's
    language (the system's locale whole); none chosen without one (English, the system's locale kept whole); the
    system's own language chosen (its region kept); another language chosen (the bare language). It sets that
    locale as the JVM's default (`Locale.setDefault`) as it starts, wherever that is not the locale the JVM started
    with: an app that offers no language choice and ships no catalogs leaves the default alone, which is the
    system's locale whole, and meets this part. And the catalog's lookup formats a value with
    the default locale (`new MessageFormat(pattern)`, or `MessageFormat.format`), not with one it builds from the
    language code (`Locale.forLanguageTag`). A test that covers the four cases is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/i18n/Messages.java) (`resolve`, `defaultLocale`, and `tr`, which formats with the default
    locale) with [`MessagesTest.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`automaticKeepsTheOperatingSystemsLocaleWhole`,
    `anExplicitChoiceMovesTheLocaleButKeepsAMatchingCountry`). Torrenta carries the same two functions and tests
    and sets the default from them ([`Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/Startup.java), `language`), but doesn't meet the rule yet: its catalog formats
    every message with the bare language ([`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/i18n/Messages.java), `locale`), so a number inside a message loses the
    region the rest of the window keeps. nux's [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/i18n/Messages.java) (`uiLocale`, [`UiLocaleTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/test/java/com/nux/i18n/UiLocaleTest.java)) keeps the region when the
    language is the system's, but with none chosen and no catalog for the system's language it sets bare English.
    Editora ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)) and Mirada ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java)) set the default to the bare language every time, so the
    region is lost; Mirada's catalog formats with the bare language as well ([`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/i18n/Messages.java)). The app
    template meets it: its [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/i18n/Messages.java) gives the four cases (`locale`), sets the result as the JVM's
    default where it differs (`start`) and formats with `new MessageFormat(value)` (`render`); its
    [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`theFormattingLocaleKeepsTheSystemsRegion`) covers the four. Modula ships no catalogs and offers no language choice, and leaves the JVM's
    locale as the system set it, which is the locale the rule asks for: it meets this rule, and its missing
    catalogs are [INTL-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/i18n/#intl-01)'s.

## Command Palette (PAL)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/: The family's command palette: a 620 px in-scene card that finds and runs any command from the keyboard.

### Rules

- **PAL-01 · MUST.** Every app has a Command Palette, one in each main window, opened by the `palette.show` command.
  A Settings, About or log window needs none of its own. Its chords, `M-x` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl+Shift+P`
  (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS) in the others (`Ctrl+Shift+A` allowed in the IntelliJ keymap), are
  [KBD-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-05).
  - *Check (code):* each main window builds one palette, and the command registered as `palette.show` opens it (in
    Editora the window controller builds one `CommandPalette`). A window that is not a main window (Settings,
    About, a log, a history or events window) is not judged.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), built once in [`MainController`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java).

- **PAL-02 · MUST.** The palette lists every registered command, with its title and description
  ([KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-03)).
  - *Check (code):* the palette's rows come from the whole registry, filtered only by the query; a command that
    cannot run stays listed, grayed; each row shows its command's title; and the palette shows the description of
    the command under the cursor, in the row or in a line of the card. A palette that shows no description fails
    this rule; that every command has one is [KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-03)'s.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`registry.all()`), [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java); the page's [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/#spec).
    Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's palettes don't yet. Torrenta's lists only the commands that can run now: `show` in
    [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/CommandPalette.java) drops every disabled command, after `offeredCommands` in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) has
    dropped what the engine cannot run and what Simple mode hides; and it shows no description, since its
    [`Command`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Command.java) has none. Modula's leaves out one (`stereo`, while its
    control is disabled, in [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and its rows show a title and a shortcut, with no description
    ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/CommandPalette.java)). nux's lists its whole registry, and each row shows the title and the
    command's id, with no description: its commands have none ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandPalette.java), `CommandCell`;
    [`command/CommandRegistry.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/command/CommandRegistry.java)).

- **PAL-10 · SHOULD.** The palette is 620 px wide, its rows 36 px high with 8 visible before the list scrolls, at
  the default zoom ([WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-12)), and its field's prompt reads "Run command…", in words
  from the catalog (Editora's key for them is `palette.prompt`).
  - *Why:* the palette is the one window every app shares; a different width or prompt is the first thing a person
    moving between apps notices.
  - *Check (code):* the palette's width, row height and visible rows come from constants of these values, and its
    prompt is read from the catalog, where the English is "Run command…". The rule asks for the words, not for a
    catalog key.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`ROW_HEIGHT`, `VISIBLE_ROWS`), Torrenta,
    Termina and the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java). Mirada's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/CommandPalette.java) matches the three
    sizes and reads the same words from the catalog under another key, `palette.runCommandPrompt`. Modula's is
    420 px with a literal "Type a command…", and nux's 540 px with a `palette.prompt` that reads "Type a command…".

### Behavior

- **PAL-04 · SHOULD.** Every open starts with an empty query: the palette does not keep the last one, so it opens
  on the whole list ([PAL-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/command-palette/#pal-02)).
  - *Check (code):* `show` clears the field and filters on the empty query before the card appears.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java).

- **PAL-05 · SHOULD.** Typing in the palette filters its list, and the first *enabled* match is selected.
  - *Check (code):* after each filter the palette selects the first row whose command can run, stepping over
    disabled rows at the top (Editora's `selectFirstEnabled`). A test that asserts it, with a disabled command at
    the top, is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette.selectFirstEnabled`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), [`CommandPaletteDisabledFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPaletteDisabledFxTest.java).

- **PAL-06 · SHOULD.** The active keymap's line and page chords move the selection, as do ↑ ↓ and Page Up/Down,
  which always work. In Editora they are the chords of its `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and
  `nav.pageUp` commands, `C-n` and `C-p` among them in the Emacs keymap. Enter, or a click on an enabled row, runs
  the command. The palette closes first, then the command runs.
  - *Check (code):* the palette's key handler looks a press up in the active keymap and moves on the commands it
    binds for a line and a page up and down, not on fixed letters, and on ↑ ↓ and Page Up/Down whatever the keymap;
    the run path hides the card before it calls the registry, and does nothing on a disabled row.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette.runSelected`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), [`PickerKeys.resolve`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java), and the app template's [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`resolve`, for its [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)), which reads the
    keymap's `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and `nav.pageUp` beside the fixed keys: the two palettes that
    ask the keymap. The others move on fixed keys: Termina's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/PaletteKeys.java) and Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java) on a
    fixed table of Emacs chords beside them (`EMACS`: `C-n`, `C-p`, `C-v`, `M-v`); Torrenta's
    [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`onKey`) on the arrows and `Ctrl+N` and `Ctrl+P`, with no page keys; Modula's
    [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/CommandPalette.java) and nux's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandPalette.java) on the arrows alone.

- **PAL-07 · SHOULD.** The active keymap's cancel chord, Esc or a click on the scrim cancels the palette, and focus
  returns to where it was. In Editora the chord is that of its `edit.cancel` command, `C-g` in the Emacs keymap.
  - *Check (code):* Esc, the chord the active keymap binds to the cancel command, and a press on the backdrop all
    hide the overlay, and hiding focuses the node that had focus before it opened. In an app with one key table (a
    terminal app's keymap, or the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files), the chord is the one that
    table binds to a cancel command; where it binds none, Esc and the backdrop are all there is to test.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`PickerKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`isCancel`), [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`previousFocus`), and the app template's [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`cancelOn`, which
    [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) hands the keymap's `edit.cancel` chord, `C-g` in its Emacs keymap, and `hide`, which gives the
    focus back): the two that ask the keymap for the chord. `Ctrl+G` is fixed in the `EMACS` table
    of Termina's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/PaletteKeys.java) and Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java). Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's
    palettes cancel on Esc and on a press on the backdrop: none of the three apps has a keymap or a cancel command, so the
    chord asks nothing more of them.

- **PAL-08 · SHOULD.** In the palette, a help chord opens the selected command's page in the docs on the website,
  for the running version. The chord is the first of `Ctrl+H`, `F1` and `Shift+F1` that the active keymap leaves
  free. It is the same on macOS, where `Ctrl+H` is the Control key and has no `Cmd` form (`C-h` in Emacs notation).
  - *Check (code):* the palette's help chord is the first of the three that the active keymap neither binds nor
    starts a longer chord with, and the URL it opens is built from the app's versioned docs address and the
    selected command's id.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) ([`PickerKeys.freeChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) over `C-h`, `f1` and `S-f1`; `docsUrl`), [`AppInfo.docsUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java).
    The app template's [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`HELP_CHORDS`, `helpChord`) picks the chord the same way, and the
    palette opens the command's page under its versioned docs ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java), `helpTitleCurrentValueAndTheEnds`). No other
    app's palette has a help chord yet.

- **PAL-09 · SHOULD.** A live keymap switch re-renders the palette's key chips, its opener chip and its key legend.
  - *Check (code):* applying a new keymap calls the palette's rebind method, which rebuilds the opener, the legend and
    the rows.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CommandPalette.refreshBindings`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), called from [`SettingsReapply`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsReapply.java); the app template's `Picker.rebind`
    ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)), which its palette runs on a keymap change with the new opener, rows and legend ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)).

## QuickOpen picker (QOPEN)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/: The family's list picker: the palette card with a title and a prompt, for choosing one thing from a list by typing.

### Rules

- **QOPEN-01 · SHOULD.** One picker serves every list choice: recent files, themes, keymaps, a setting's values, a
  branch to compare with.
  - *Check (code):* those choices are instances of one generic picker class; there is no second list-picker class or
    `ChoiceDialog` for them.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) (one generic class, instantiated more than seventy times), driven by
    [`PickerKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java). Editora still asks with a `ChoiceDialog` in three places: the Git reset mode and the
    merge parent to revert against ([`ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java)), and the settings backup to restore
    ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)).

- **QOPEN-02 · SHOULD.** In an app with a picker (a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list
  by typing; a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's
  completion list), the picker is the palette's card in the shared in-scene overlay host, with a title naming the
  command over the field and a prompt in the field. That it is never a `javafx.stage.Popup` is
  [KBD-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-07).
  - *Check (code):* each picker shows its card through the overlay host the palette uses and sets a title and a
    prompt text.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.setOverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java); the page's [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#spec). The app template's
    pickers (theme, keymap, language, Bind Key) are titled cards of its [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) in its [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java).

### Behavior

**Applies to:** an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).

- **QOPEN-03 · SHOULD.** A picker reads its items fresh on every showing and snapshots them, so typing filters a
  stable list. A source that answers late (an outline the language server has not returned yet) has the picker read
  its items again and keep the query (`reload()` in Editora).
  - *Check (code):* showing a picker calls its items supplier, and a late source makes the picker read the items
    again while it keeps the query (Editora's `show` and `reload`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpen.reload`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java).

- **QOPEN-04 · SHOULD.** With nothing typed, a picker's list keeps the supplier's own order (recency for recent
  files, document order for symbols), with the current value pre-selected when there is one.
  - *Check (code):* a picker's empty query passes the items through unsorted and selects the value in force when
    the picker was given one (Editora's `setCurrentItem`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), `setCurrentItem`; the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) (`current`),
    whose theme, keymap and language pickers open on the choice in force ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java), `helpTitleCurrentValueAndTheEnds`).

- **QOPEN-05 · SHOULD.** Typing in a picker ranks its rows by fuzzy score, and ties keep the supplier's order, so
  rows do not shuffle under the cursor between keystrokes.
  - *Check (code):* the last tiebreak of the picker's sort is the supplier's index.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java).

- **QOPEN-06 · SHOULD.** In a picker, the active keymap's line and page chords move the selection (in Editora, the
  chords of its `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and `nav.pageUp` commands), as do ↑ ↓, Page Up/Down and
  `Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End` (`Cmd` on macOS), which always work; plain Home and End stay with the field's caret. Enter
  or a click on a row chooses; the card hides first, then the choice runs, so focus is already back where it
  belongs.
  - *Check (code):* the picker's key handler moves on the commands the active keymap binds for a line and a page up
    and down, and on the fixed keys whatever the keymap; the accept path hides the card before it calls the choice
    handler.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) (`hide()` then `onChoose`), [`PickerKeys.resolve`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java), the only picker that asks
    the keymap. The app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) asks the keymap the same way, through its [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`resolve`), and takes
    `Ctrl+Home` and `Ctrl+End` (`Cmd` on macOS); Mirada's picker is its palette, whose [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java)
    carries a fixed table of Emacs chords (`EMACS`) beside the fixed keys. Termina, Torrenta, Modula and nux have
    no picker ([Uses](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#uses)).

- **QOPEN-07 · SHOULD.** The active keymap's cancel chord, Esc or a click on the scrim cancels a picker, and the
  overlay host restores focus. In Editora the chord is that of its `edit.cancel` command, `C-g` in the Emacs
  keymap. A picker that previewed something undoes it.
  - *Check (code):* Esc, the chord the active keymap binds to the cancel command, and a press on the backdrop each
    hide the picker; hiding gives the focus back to the node that had it before the picker opened; and a picker
    that previewed a row runs its undo when it is dismissed without a choice. A test that asserts the undo is the
    surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`previousFocus`; it cancels on [`PickerKeys.isCancel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java)),
    [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java) (`dismissingRestoresWhatWasPreviewed`). The app template's
    [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java) cancels its pickers on Esc, on the scrim and on the keymap's `edit.cancel` chord (`cancelOn`), and
    gives the focus back; none of its pickers previews anything. `Ctrl+G` is fixed in the `EMACS` table of Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java).

- **QOPEN-08 · MAY.** A picker previews the highlighted row as the selection moves and undoes the preview on cancel
  (Editora's Recent Locations shows each place and returns to the origin on Esc). A preview without an undo is
  worse than none, and nothing is previewed for the row the picker opens on, only for one the user moved to.
  Editora's theme and keymap pickers do not preview; they apply on Enter.
  - *Check (code):* a previewing picker previews from its selection listener once it is showing, never for the row
    it opens on, restores what it previewed when dismissed, and does not restore after a choice. A test that
    asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.setPreview(onPreview, onCancelled)`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java).

- **QOPEN-09 · MAY.** A row action acts on the highlighted row and keeps the picker open (Editora's breakpoints
  picker enables or removes one), re-reading the list afterwards and keeping the cursor in place.
  - *Check (code):* a row action's key runs the action on the highlighted row without hiding the card, and the
    picker then reads its items again and keeps the cursor on that row. A test that asserts it is the surest
    evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.addRowAction(key, legend, action)`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java)
    (`aRowActionActsOnTheHighlightedRowAndKeepsThePickerOpen`).

- **QOPEN-10 · SHOULD.** A picker that can open on an empty list shows a placeholder sentence in it, never a blank
  card. A picker with nothing to offer may instead say so in the status line and not open.
  - *Check (code):* each picker whose source can be empty either calls `setPlaceholder` or returns before `show` with
    a status message.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`QuickOpen.setPlaceholder`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) ([`BreakpointsPicker`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BreakpointsPicker.java)); [`NavigationCoordinator`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/NavigationCoordinator.java)
    (`status.nav.noRecentLocations`).

- **QOPEN-11 · SHOULD.** The overlay host a picker shows in holds one card at a time; opening a picker replaces
  whatever card was up.
  - *Check (code):* showing a card in the overlay host removes the previous card before it adds the new one, and
    keeps the original focus owner (Editora's `OverlayHost.show`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`OverlayHost.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java).

- **QOPEN-12 · SHOULD.** A picker's relatives, the other list overlays an app has (in Editora the open-files
  switcher, the find-file field, the multi-select picker, and the branch and stash popups), move, accept and
  cancel with the same keys as the picker.
  - *Check (code):* each of those overlays moves, accepts and cancels on the keys the picker does: the moves of
    [QOPEN-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#qopen-06), Enter, and the cancel chord and Esc of [QOPEN-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/quick-open/#qopen-07). In Editora each maps its
    keys through the helper the picker uses (`PickerKeys`), which is one way to hold it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`Switcher`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Switcher.java), [`FileFinder`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileFinder.java), [`MultiSelectPicker`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MultiSelectPicker.java), [`BranchPopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BranchPopup.java), [`GitStashPopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitStashPopup.java).

## Welcome page (WELC)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/: The family's start page: Start actions with their chords, recent items a digit away, Customize and Help, shown when there is nothing to restore.

### Rules

- **WELC-01 · SHOULD.** An app that opens files or projects in tabs shows a Welcome page when there is no session
  to restore.
  - *Check (code):* startup with nothing restored opens the Welcome page.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/WelcomePane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java), [`MainController.addWelcomeTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java).

- **WELC-02 · SHOULD.** An app whose window *is* its content, and can start with nothing in it (a list with no
  items, a viewer with nothing open), shows its own empty state in place of a Welcome page ([WELC-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/#welc-01)),
  with the same ingredients: the ways in, each with its chord.
  - *Check (by hand):* start the app with nothing in it and read the empty state's keys. An app that always opens
    into content (a terminal with its shell, a radio, a monitor) has no empty state to judge.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`ui/Welcome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Welcome.java); Mirada [`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java) (`offerToOpen`,
    `viewer.emptyHint`); both are described under [In the apps](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/#in-the-apps).

### Behavior

**Applies to:** an app with a Welcome page ([WELC-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/welcome/#welc-01)).

- **WELC-03 · SHOULD.** The Welcome page is shown at startup when there is no session to restore (so always with
  `--no-session`), by the `view.welcome` command (Help → Welcome Page where the app has a Help menu, in the place
  [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-07) gives it), and when a switch to another project leaves the tab strip
  empty (Editora's project swap). In an app that can start straight into one view, as Editora does for a
  standalone diff, that startup suppresses the page while its worker reads the files.
  - *Check (code):* those three paths open the one Welcome tab, and where the app has a Help menu, a row inside it
    runs `view.welcome`; a startup that goes straight to a view holds a flag that skips the page.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MainController.addWelcomeTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), `showWelcomeIfNoTabs`; [`WindowSessionCoordinator`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowSessionCoordinator.java)
    (`suppressWelcome`). Editora's menu row is in View, not in Help yet ([`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)). The app template shows
    the page when there is no session to restore ([`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java)), registers `view.welcome` ([`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java)) and lists it in
    the Help menu ([`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java); [`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theWelcomePageIsInHelpClosesAloneAndIsRebuiltWhenShown`); it has no
    project swap and no view to start straight into.

- **WELC-04 · SHOULD.** Closing the last tab does not bring the Welcome page back. The empty content area shows its
  own quiet hint instead: the app's ways in, each with its chord (in Editora: Open File, Open Folder, Command Palette
  and Welcome Page), and takes focus so chords still reach the window.
  - *Check (code):* closing the last tab shows the hint in the empty content area, not the Welcome page, and gives
    it the focus; opening a tab hides it. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/EditorEmptyState.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/EditorEmptyState.java), [`EditorEmptyStateFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/EditorEmptyStateFxTest.java); the app template's [`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java) (`emptyHint`,
    which lists its ways in with their chords and takes focus when the last tab closes).

- **WELC-05 · SHOULD.** The page is rebuilt on every show, so the recents, the Projects and Git toggles, the keymap and
  the theme are current. A refresh keeps the focus where it was.
  - *Check (code):* showing the page calls `refresh`, which re-requests focus when the page had it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WelcomePane.refresh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java); the app template's `refreshWelcome`
    ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)), run on every show ([`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theWelcomePageIsInHelpClosesAloneAndIsRebuiltWhenShown`).

- **WELC-06 · SHOULD.** The recent lists offer no file that no longer exists and no project whose root is gone. Remote
  files are kept unchecked.
  - *Check (code):* the recent files pass through the same filter as the toolbar's dropdown; projects are kept only
    when their root is a directory.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`RecentFiles.showable`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/RecentFiles.java), [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java).

- **WELC-07 · SHOULD.** Remove from recent files asks first, through the caller, then refreshes the page.
  - *Check (code):* the remover the page is given shows a confirmation before it removes the entry.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WelcomePane.setRecentRemover`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java); [`MainController`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) (`dialog.removeRecent.*`).

- **WELC-08 · SHOULD.** The digits 1 to 9 open the numbered entries: typed characters only, with no modifier, so chords
  and Enter are untouched.
  - *Check (code):* the digit handler is on `KEY_TYPED` and ignores Ctrl, Alt and Meta.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WelcomePane.onKeyTyped`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java).

- **WELC-09 · SHOULD.** In an app with saved remote sites, they appear as their own section; a click opens the
  connection form prefilled. The section is hidden when there are none.
  - *Check (code):* the page adds a Remote Sites section only when the saved-sites list is not empty.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java) (`remoteSites`, `welcome.remote`).

- **WELC-10 · SHOULD.** The Welcome page's Customize links run the commands that pick the keymap and the app
  theme (Editora's are `keymap.select` and `theme.setAppTheme`); a change made there re-renders the page, chords
  included.
  - *Check (code):* the two Customize links run the app's keymap and theme picker commands through the registry,
    and applying a keymap or a theme refreshes the Welcome page.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java) (`customizeRow`), refreshed by [`SettingsReapply`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsReapply.java).

- **WELC-11 · SHOULD.** The Welcome tab is not a document: its menu is Close only, with no Save, Rename or Pin, and the
  title bar shows the app or project name, not a file.
  - *Check (code):* the Welcome tab's context menu holds one Close item.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MainController.addWelcomeTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java); the app template's [`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java),
    whose Welcome tab's menu holds `buffer.close` alone, is not pinned, and leaves the title to the project and the app.

## About window (ABOUT)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/: The family's About panel: identity, update status, license, links and copyable environment details.

### Rules

- **ABOUT-01 · MUST.** Every app has an About window, reached by the `help.about` command, by Help → About where the
  app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which
  [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines), and on macOS by the About item of the application menu, the one macOS
  names after the app. The app adds that item itself: JavaFX builds the menu with Hide and Quit and no About.
  - *Why:* on macOS that menu is where every app keeps About, so it is one of the places
    [the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins).
  - *Check (code):* `help.about` is registered and opens the About window; where the app has a Help menu, a row
    inside that menu runs the command (a row beside a Help submenu is not in it); and on macOS the app inserts an
    About item into the application menu that opens the same window.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`help.about` ends the Help menu), and the
    app template's [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) and [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java), do the Help row and the command, and the template's
    [`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MacAppMenu.java) inserts the macOS item, which runs `help.about`, so the template meets the whole rule.
    Editora doesn't add the macOS item yet, and nor do Torrenta, Modula and nux. Termina ([`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MacAppMenu.java)) and Mirada ([`os/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacAppMenu.java)) add it too: JavaFX has no
    public API for that menu, so the three insert the item into the one Glass keeps (`MacApplication.getAppleMenu`).
    Neither of those two is the whole rule: Termina's command is `about`, not `help.about`, and Mirada's About row sits beside
    the Help submenu of its main menu, not in it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java), `finish`).

- **ABOUT-02 · MUST.** About shows the version and build, the runtime, the license, links to the app's home page,
  its source code and its releases, and the result of the last update check. The Pauta edition is
  [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-05).
  - *Check (code):* the About window shows the version and the build as the build recorded them (in Editora both
    come from `AppInfo`, which `--version` prints from too); the Java and JavaFX versions; the license; a link that
    opens the app's home page (its website, or its repository's page on the host where About links no website),
    one that opens its source code (the repository) and one that opens its releases (the repository's releases
    page or its latest release), each there whatever the update check answered; and the update checker's last
    answer whatever it was (an update, up to date, a failed check or not checked yet), not only an update that is
    available. One link meets two of the three when the page it opens is both: the repository's page is the home
    page and the source code where About links no website, and a releases page of the repository holds its source
    too (Editora's "Source code and releases"). A link to the running build's release notes, and a link shown only
    when an update is available, are not the link to the releases.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java), [`AppInfo`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java) (`HOMEPAGE`, its website, and `RELEASES_PAGE`, the
    repository's latest release, behind "Source code and releases"); the page's [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#spec). Four apps lack a
    link. Termina's About ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its website and not its source code, and its releases
    only when an update is available. Mirada's ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its repository and the running build's
    release notes, and its releases only when an update is available. Modula's About
    ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its repository and never its releases; it also shows no Java version, and it
    shows the update check only when an update is available. nux's ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/AboutWindow.java)) has the runtime lines
    and links its repository; it shows the update check, and with it the link to its releases, only when there is
    a newer version.

- **ABOUT-03 · SHOULD.** About's *Copy details* button copies the environment block and leaves the window open; its
  label becomes "Copied".
  - *Check (code):* the button's handler puts the environment block's text on the clipboard and sets the button's
    label to the copied text (Editora's `about.copied`); the button sits in the content, not the dialog's button
    bar, so pressing it can't close the window.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`AboutDialog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) (`about.copyDetails`, `about.copied`).

- **ABOUT-04 · SHOULD.** About's update status claims nothing before a check has answered: with no answer, or with
  the check switched off, it says it has not checked, never "up to date".
  - *Check (code):* About's update status falls back to the not-checked text when the checker has no result.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`AboutDialog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) (`about.notChecked`); the [Update status states](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#update-status-states).

- **ABOUT-10 · SHOULD.** In About, an available update stands out: "Update available" is bold in amber, a color no
  link or label in About uses, while the links stay in the accent, "up to date" is green, a failed check red and
  the last-checked line muted (Editora's tokens for the four are `-state-amber`, `-state-accent`, `-state-green`
  and `-state-red`).
  - *Why:* in the accent every link wears, the one line that asks for action reads as one more link.
  - *Check (code):* the style of About's update-available line (the app template's `.about-update-available`) is
    bold in the amber token, and no other About style uses that token; the up-to-date line is in the green token,
    a failed check in the red and the last-checked line in the muted color, and the links keep the accent.
  - *Reference:* the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s `.about-update-available` in [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css), set by [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java).
    No released app does yet: Editora's `.about-update` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) is `-state-accent`, the links' color.

### Pauta edition and conformance

- **ABOUT-05 · MUST.** About names the Pauta edition in two places: a link, *Built to Pauta x.y.z*, among its other
  links (at Partial it reads *Working toward Pauta x.y.z*, [ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-09)), and a line `Pauta: x.y.z` in the
  environment block, right after the commit, so *Copy details* carries it.
  - *Check (code):* one of About's links reads *Built to Pauta* and the edition, or *Working toward Pauta* and the
    edition at Partial, in words from the catalog, and About's environment block writes a `Pauta:` line right after
    the commit line. The rule asks for the words, not for a catalog key: the app template's and Termina's key is
    `about.pauta`, Mirada's `about.pautaLink`.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java); Termina's [`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/AboutWindow.java) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java);
    Mirada's [`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/AboutWindow.java) (`about.pautaLink`) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java).

- **ABOUT-06 · MUST.** About's edition link ([ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-05)) opens the edition's own address,
  `https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/`, which never changes, not `latest/`, which moves on to newer editions.
  - *Check (code):* the URL About's edition link opens is built from the edition number (`pauta.version`) and never
    contains `latest`. An About with no edition link has nothing to open: the rule fails with
    [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-05), which requires the link, and the evidence names that rule.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`); Termina's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`);
    Mirada's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`).

- **ABOUT-07 · MUST.** The Pauta edition About names is the edition the app meets, not the newest. Moving to a
  newer edition means reading its changelog for new or stronger MUSTs, meeting them, then changing the number. An
  app at Partial names the edition it is working toward instead, and says so ([ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-09)).
  - *Check (code):* read which words About uses for the edition ([ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-09)). *Working toward* meets
    the rule. An About that names no edition claims none: this rule has nothing to judge and passes, and the
    missing edition is [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-05)'s finding. *Built to* is judged last, from the audit's other results:
    audited against the edition the app names (`pauta.version`), with that edition's own rules
    (`https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/rules.json`), not the newest edition's, the app has no MUST that is `fail` or `pending`. The evidence names the MUSTs that are. An
    audit of part of the edition judges the rule from the MUSTs in its scope and says so. Only the rules of the
    edition the app names settle a *Built to*: an audit run against another edition reports the rule as
    `not-checked` and names the edition whose rules would settle it.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template), at Complete: its About says *Built to Pauta 6.0.0*
    ([`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java), `editionKey`) and so does its README, and its audit against 6.0.0's own rules finds no
    MUST that is `fail` or `pending` ([`docs/pauta-audit.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.md)). Termina and Mirada don't meet it yet.
    Termina's About says "Built to Pauta 2.0.2" ([`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/pom.xml), `pauta.version`), an edition that already
    required a find bar in its Debug Log, the UI font on every scene and the command ids `help.about` and
    `palette.show`, none of which it has. Mirada's says "Built to Pauta 4.0.1", an edition that already required
    its settings in `~/.mirada` on every OS.

- **ABOUT-08 · MUST.** The Pauta edition an app names has one source: a `pauta.version` property in `pom.xml`,
  which the build filters into the app's resources and the app reads from there, like its own version
  (`build-info.properties` and `AppInfo` in the app template). The README's badge and "Built to" line, which name
  that edition too, are [PAUTA-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-15).
  - *Check (code):* `pom.xml` defines `pauta.version`; a resource the build filters carries it (the app template's
    `build-info.properties`); and the edition the app shows is read from that resource (the template's `AppInfo`),
    never from a literal in its code.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml), `build-info.properties` and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java); Termina's the same, with [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java),
    and Mirada's, with its [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/pom.xml) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java).

- **ABOUT-09 · MUST.** About shows the app's conformance, Complete, Core or Partial, as the conformance helper
  computes it from `pauta.json` ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-02)) and never higher: a link, *Pauta
  conformance: Core*, right after the edition's link, that runs the `help.pauta` command and so opens the Pauta
  window ([PWIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/pauta-window/#pwin-01)), and a line `Pauta conformance: Core (2 exceptions)` in the
  environment block, right after the `Pauta:` line; with one it says `(1 exception)`, with none `(no exceptions)`.
  At Partial the edition's link reads *Working toward Pauta x.y.z*: the app does not meet that edition yet, so it
  does not say it is built to it.
  - *Why:* [*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps).
  - *Check (code):* About calls the conformance helper and holds no conformance name of its own; its conformance
    link runs `help.pauta`; the environment block has the conformance line after the `Pauta:` line; and at Partial
    the edition's link reads *Working toward Pauta* and the edition (the app template's key for it is
    `about.pautaWorkingToward`).
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`PautaConformance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/PautaConformance.java) (`environmentLine`). Termina's and Mirada's About show the edition but not the
    conformance.

## Pauta window (PWIN)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/pauta-window/: The window that shows which edition of Pauta the app implements, how fully it conforms, and every exception it records, opened from About, the Help menu and the Command Palette.

### Rules

- **PWIN-01 · MUST.** Every app has a Pauta window, opened by the `help.pauta` command: from the Command Palette like
  every command, and from a *Pauta Conformance* row in the Help menu where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a
  menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-14) defines). The row's
