  place in that menu is [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-07), and About's *Pauta conformance* link, which runs the
  same command, is [ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-09).
  - *Check (code):* a command with the id `help.pauta` is registered and opens the Pauta window, and where the app
    has a Help menu, a row inside that menu runs the command (the app template's Help menu is a list of command
    ids that holds `help.pauta`). A row beside a Help submenu is not in it.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`help.pauta`, which runs `openPauta`) and [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (`help.pauta` in
    `menu.help`, just above `help.about`). No released app has a Pauta window yet.

- **PWIN-02 · MUST.** The Pauta window shows the edition, the conformance with one sentence that says what it
  means, a count of exceptions by kind, and every exception: the rule's ID, its level (MUST or SHOULD), the kind,
  the reason, and for a deviation or a pending exception its link.
  - *Check (by hand):* open the Pauta window and compare it with the app's `pauta.json`, entry by entry.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java).

- **PWIN-03 · MUST.** The Pauta window reads the exceptions from `pauta.json` and the edition from the build, as
  About does ([ABOUT-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-08); `AppInfo` in the template), and takes the conformance from the same
  helper as About ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-02)). No edition, conformance or exception is written in
  the window's own code.
  - *Check (code):* the Pauta window loads the exceptions through the one loader of `pauta.json`, reads the edition
    where About reads it, and calls the conformance helper; its code holds no rule ID, edition number or conformance
    name of its own.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) (`PautaConformance.of`).

- **PWIN-04 · MUST.** Every link in the Pauta window opens a fixed address, never one under `latest/`: the
  edition's link opens the edition's own address, the one [ABOUT-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/about/#about-06) gives About's link, and
  each rule ID opens the rule's address in that edition (the entry's `url` in `pauta.json`). The edition's link, in
  the Pauta window and in About, runs the `help.pautaRules` command, so the palette reaches it too.
  - *Why:* an app built to an edition answers to that edition's rules; `latest/` moves on.
  - *Check (code):* `help.pautaRules` is registered and opens the edition's address, built from `pauta.version`;
    the edition's link in the Pauta window and the one in About both run that command; and each rule ID in the
    Pauta window opens its entry's `url`.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`help.pautaRules`, which opens `AppInfo.pautaUrl()`), run by the edition's link in [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) and
    [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java); `PautaWindow` opens each rule ID at its entry's `url`.

- **PWIN-05 · SHOULD.** The Pauta window lists pending exceptions first, then deviations, then app-only (in a
  template), then not-applicable; within a kind, MUSTs before SHOULDs, then by ID.
  - *Why:* what the app still owes is what a reader came to find.
  - *Check (code):* the list the Pauta window draws is sorted by kind in that order, then MUSTs before SHOULDs,
    then by rule ID (the app template's `PautaConformance.sorted`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/PautaConformance.java) (`sorted`, by the order of its `Kind`), tested by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java)
    (`pendingFirstThenDeviationsThenAppOnlyThenNotApplicableMustsBeforeShouldsThenById`).

- **PWIN-06 · SHOULD.** The Pauta window's *Copy as text* button copies the edition, the conformance and the list
  as Markdown, one line per exception, and leaves the window open; its label becomes "Copied".
  - *Check (code):* the button's handler copies the edition, the conformance and one line per exception as Markdown
    and sets the button's label to the copied text (the template's `pauta.copied`); the button sits in the content,
    not the button bar, like About's *Copy details*, so pressing it can't close the window.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) (`pauta.copy`, `pauta.copied`), built
    like Editora's About *Copy details*.

- **PWIN-07 · SHOULD.** A *Conformance in the docs* link runs the `help.pautaDocs` command, which opens the app's
  docs page ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/conformance/#pauta-13)) for this version, `/docs/v-<version>/pauta/`, where the site
  serves versioned docs ([DOCS-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/documentation/#docs-03)), and `/docs/pauta/` until it does. The README's
  badge links the unversioned page, which always shows the latest release.
  - *Check (code):* `help.pautaDocs` is registered and builds the URL from the app's docs base, like Help →
    Documentation.
  - *Reference:* the app template's [`AppInfo.pautaDocsUrl()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java), registered as
    `help.pautaDocs` in [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java).

- **PWIN-08 · SHOULD.** With no exceptions, the Pauta window says so in one line where the list would be, naming
  the app and the edition (for an app called Mirada, "No exceptions: Mirada meets every MUST and SHOULD of Pauta
  x.y.z."), and its copy button still works.
  - *Check (by hand):* with an empty `exceptions` array in `pauta.json`, open the Pauta window.
  - *Reference:* The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) (`pauta.none`).

## Confirm dialog (CONF)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/: The family's question before a destructive action: it names the thing, the button names the action in red, and Escape cancels.

### Rules

- **CONF-01 · MUST.** Before anything the user made is removed, deleted, discarded or overwritten, the app asks first,
  unless the action can be taken back instead.
  - *Check (code):* each destructive action calls a confirmation before it changes anything, or records an undo.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/CloseCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java) (unsaved changes, Quit) and [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java);
    Torrenta [`ui/RemoveConfirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java), which asks it for the torrent list, the RSS tab and every list in Settings.
    Modula and nux don't yet: the Remove row of a Modula preset's menu ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java), `removePreset` in
    [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)) and nux's Profiles → Delete (`withProfileRemoved`, called from [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)) remove
    at once, with no question and no undo.

- **CONF-02 · MUST.** In an app that asks before a destructive action (before it removes, deletes, discards or
  overwrites something, ends a running program, or runs a command that cannot be taken back), the question names the
  thing and what happens to it. A question that warns before something is run or pasted and destroys nothing
  (Termina's before a multi-line paste), and a question before a harmless command (nux's before a UPS command it does
  not count as risky), are not questions before a destructive action. This list says which questions the rules on a
  question's form cover; it is wider than what [CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01) requires a question or an undo for, which is only
  what the user made.
  - *Check (code):* the string of every question before a destructive action names the thing, by an argument for
    its name or count or in its own words ("Quit Editora?"), and says what happens to it.
  - *Reference:* Editora `dialog.unsaved.header`, `dialog.discard.tracked`; Torrenta [`RemoveConfirm.question`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java),
    [`Actions.removeQuestion`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Actions.java).

- **CONF-03 · MUST.** In an app that asks before a destructive action, the question's confirming button carries
  the action's own verb (Delete files, Remove, Discard, Quit), never OK or Yes, and is drawn in red, the danger
  style (Editora's style class for it is `danger`).
  - *Check (code):* in every question before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02) says which those are), the
    confirming button's `ButtonType` is named with the action's verb, never OK or Yes, and its button is given the
    red danger style (the `danger` style class in Editora). Where the buttons' words come from is
    [CONF-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-14)'s.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`RemoveConfirm.ask`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java) meets it: the action is named with its verb and styled `danger`. Four other
    questions of Torrenta's, in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java) (disconnecting sync, Reset to Defaults, Reset All
    Shortcuts and taking a shortcut back from another command), don't yet: the confirming button says OK and is
    not red. Its question before connecting sync is not one of them: it destroys nothing (what the repository
    holds comes to this machine, and a value that differs here is kept), like Editora's
    ([`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java)). Termina's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java),
    Mirada's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Confirm.java) and the app template's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Confirm.java) meet it too: the action is named
    with its verb and styled `danger`. Editora meets it in some questions and not in others.
    [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java), which every destructive Git action asks through,
    [`MainController.styleUnsavedChangesButtons`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) and `styleQuitButtonAsDanger` name and style the action, and so do
    its Local History purges ([`ui/HistoryCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/HistoryCoordinator.java)). It doesn't yet where the answer is the stock OK, as in
    these among others: the Project panel's file delete (`confirmDelete` in [`ui/ProjectPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java)), deleting a project ([`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java)),
    deleting a note ([`ui/NotesCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/NotesCoordinator.java)), deleting a macro ([`ui/MacroSettingsPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MacroSettingsPane.java)), Replace in Files
    ([`ui/SearchCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchCoordinator.java)), and Revert and overwriting a file from Save As (`confirmRevertDialog` and
    `confirmOverwrite` in [`ui/FileWorkflowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileWorkflowCoordinator.java)); nor where the
    action is named and not red, as in: deleting a remote site ([`ui/RemoteSitesPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RemoteSitesPane.java)), deleting a TODO pattern
    ([`ui/TodoSettingsPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TodoSettingsPane.java)), resetting the settings ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)), discarding recovery records
    ([`ui/RecoveryCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RecoveryCoordinator.java)) and removing a plugin ([`ui/PluginDialogs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PluginDialogs.java)). nux's risky-command question
    names Run, with no red ([`ui/CommandConfirmation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandConfirmation.java)).

- **CONF-14 · MUST.** Every dialog with two or more buttons words each button from the message catalog, never with
  JavaFX's stock OK, Yes, No, Cancel, Apply or Close, which are worded in the JVM's locale. That is every JavaFX
  `Dialog` the app shows, whatever it is for: a question, before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02)) or not,
  a text prompt, a pick from a list, a form. Only a message with one button is outside the rule. Like
  [CONF-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-08) and [CONF-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-12), it reaches past the question before a destructive action.
  - *Why:* a stock button is labeled from JavaFX's own resources, in the JVM's locale, so under menus in the language
    chosen in Settings a dialog can still say "Cancel" in another.
  - *Check (code):* in every `Dialog` the app shows with two or more buttons (an `Alert` of any type, a
    `TextInputDialog`, a `ChoiceDialog`, a `Dialog` the app fills itself), each button shows a string from the
    message catalog: its `ButtonType` is built with one, or its button's text is set from the catalog before the
    dialog is shown. None is left as `ButtonType.OK`, `ButtonType.YES`, `ButtonType.NO`, `ButtonType.CANCEL`,
    `ButtonType.APPLY` or `ButtonType.CLOSE`, and none is the stock OK or Cancel that an `Alert` of type
    `CONFIRMATION`, a `TextInputDialog` and a `ChoiceDialog` come with. A dialog whose stock buttons are swapped
    for catalog-worded ones before it is shown passes (Torrenta's `StockButtons.translate`). A dialog with one
    button is not judged. An app that shows no dialog with two or more buttons has nothing to judge, and passes.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta: [`RemoveConfirm.ask`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java) names the action from the catalog and takes Cancel from its
    [`StockButtons`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/StockButtons.java) (`cancel()`, the catalog's word on the `CANCEL_CLOSE` role), and every other dialog of two
    buttons goes through `StockButtons.translate`, which swaps the stock OK and Cancel for the catalog's: the four
    alerts that ask in its Settings ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java): connecting and disconnecting sync, Reset to
    Defaults and the shortcuts), its nine text prompts and its two picks from a list ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java),
    [`ui/DetailPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DetailPane.java) and `ui/SettingsWindow.java`). Modula's one dialog is a message with one button, so it
    has nothing to judge. The app template meets it: every dialog it shows goes through
    [`Dialogs.styled`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Dialogs.java), which words the stock OK, Cancel, Yes, No, Apply and Close from the catalog before the dialog is
    shown and again when its buttons change, and its [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Confirm.java) names the action from the catalog
    ([`DialogsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/DialogsFxTest.java), `everyDialogHasOneButtonOrderAndCatalogWords`). Termina and Mirada meet it in their questions
    and not in their text prompts. Termina's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java), which its removals, its close-running-program question and its
    multi-line paste warning ask through, names both buttons from the catalog, and so does its Import configuration
    question ([`ui/ConfigTransfer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ConfigTransfer.java)); its Rename Tab prompt words OK from the catalog and keeps the stock
    Cancel (`askForTabName` in [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)), and the prompt its setting commands ask a value
    through (`settingHost` in the same file) and its Create on GitHub prompt (`createSyncRepositoryOnGitHub` in
    [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingsWindow.java)) are `TextInputDialog`s with the stock OK and Cancel. Mirada's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Confirm.java)
    and its note form ([`ui/NoteDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/NoteDialog.java)) name both buttons from the catalog; its Rename prompt (`rename` in
    [`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java)) is a `TextInputDialog` with the stock OK and Cancel. Editora doesn't
    yet. Its unsaved-changes and Quit questions
    name every button from the catalog (`unsavedAlert` and `confirmQuit` in [`ui/CloseCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java)), but of its
    64 `CONFIRMATION` alerts, 26 keep the stock OK and Cancel, the Project panel's file delete (`confirmDelete` in [`ui/ProjectPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java)) and Replace in Files
    ([`ui/SearchCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchCoordinator.java)) among them, and 22 more name the action beside a stock `ButtonType.CANCEL`, among
    them [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java), which every destructive Git action asks through. Its warnings
    that ask do the same: the four trust questions of [`ui/TrustPrompts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TrustPrompts.java) name the action beside a stock
    Cancel, and the question before its MCP server is enabled (`confirmEnableMcp` in [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java))
    keeps the stock OK and Cancel. So do its prompts and forms, these among them: the Create on GitHub prompt
    ([`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java)), the reset-mode and revert-merge picks ([`ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java)), the
    pick of a settings backup ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)), a macro's command picker ([`ui/MacroSettingsPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MacroSettingsPane.java))
    and the Java cleanups form ([`ui/JavaCleanupsDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/JavaCleanupsDialog.java)) keep the stock OK and Cancel, and the login form
    ([`ui/RemoteCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RemoteCoordinator.java)) and the forms that export and import the configuration
    ([`ui/ExportConfigDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ExportConfigDialog.java), [`ui/ConfigImportFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConfigImportFlow.java)) name the action beside a stock
    `ButtonType.CANCEL`. nux doesn't in any of its four dialogs of two buttons: the question before a risky command
    names Run beside a stock `ButtonType.CANCEL`, the one before a harmless command is a `CONFIRMATION` alert
    with the stock OK and Cancel ([`ui/CommandConfirmation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandConfirmation.java)), its credentials form adds `ButtonType.OK` and
    `ButtonType.CANCEL` ([`ui/CredentialsDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CredentialsDialog.java)), and its Save Profile prompt is a `TextInputDialog` with the
    stock pair (`saveCurrentAsProfile` in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)).

- **CONF-04 · MUST.** In an app that asks before a destructive action, Cancel is the way out of the question:
  Escape and the window's close button both answer Cancel, and nothing is lost on a dismissal.
  - *Check (code):* in every question before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02) says which those are),
    Cancel has the `CANCEL_CLOSE` role, and the result defaults to Cancel when the dialog closes any other way
    (`showAndWait().orElse(cancel)`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java), [`CloseCoordinator.unsavedAlert`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java); Torrenta
    [`RemoveConfirm.ask`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java).

- **CONF-13 · MUST.** In an app that asks before a destructive action, every such question has one default button,
  and it is never the red one (Editora's `danger` style class): Cancel where the only action is destructive, Save
  where saving is an option ([CONF-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-05)). The dialog opens with keyboard focus on the default button, so
  Enter in a question that has just opened keeps what the user has, on every OS, and the red action runs only from
  its own button: a click, or the focus moved to it with Tab and then Space, which presses the focused button on
  every OS.
  - *Why:* Enter is the key a hurried hand presses, and Escape already cancels ([CONF-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-04)): with Cancel as
    the default, no single key destroys anything. JavaFX makes a button with the `OK_DONE` role the default by
    itself, so a named action is the default unless the dialog says otherwise. It also presses a focused button on
    Enter on Windows and Linux but not on macOS, so a question with no default button answers Enter differently on
    each OS. With Cancel as the default one difference is left, and it is JavaFX's: once Tab has put the focus on the
    red button, Enter runs it on Windows and Linux and answers Cancel on macOS. Space is the key that does the same
    everywhere.
  - *Check (code):* in every question before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02) says which those are), the
    code calls `setDefaultButton(true)` on Cancel, or on Save in the unsaved-changes question, and
    `setDefaultButton(false)` on the destructive action, so that one is not left a default button too, and it does
    both before the dialog is shown. JavaFX gives the opening focus to the first button that is a default button, so
    with one default button the dialog opens with the focus on it. No such question leaves the red action, or no
    button at all, as the default.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java) (`Options.cancelIsDefault`, which its close-running-program question sets), the app template's
    [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Confirm.java) (`dialog`, which every destructive question of the template asks through) and nux
    [`ui/CommandConfirmation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandConfirmation.java) (a risky UPS command): each unsets the action's default and sets Cancel's as it
    builds the dialog, before it is shown. Editora does it in about twenty of its questions, each by
    hand: deleting for good what the trash cannot take ([`ProjectPanel.cancelByDefault`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java)), closing a terminal with a program running
    ([`ui/TerminalCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalCoordinator.java)), resetting settings ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)), trusting a folder
    ([`ui/TrustPrompts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TrustPrompts.java)) among them. The rest don't yet: Editora's Git confirmations and Local History
    purges ([`ui/HistoryCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/HistoryCoordinator.java)), Torrenta's `RemoveConfirm`, Mirada's `Confirm`, and
    Termina's removals and its Import configuration question leave the red action as the default, so Enter runs it;
    Torrenta's four Settings questions ([CONF-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-03)) leave OK as the default, and so do questions of
    Editora's that keep the stock OK, its delete to the trash (`confirmDelete` in [`ui/ProjectPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java), which
    moves the default only when a file cannot go to the trash), its Revert and its Save As overwrite among them;
    Editora's unsaved-changes and Quit questions have no default button. nux's question before a command it does not count
    as risky leaves the stock OK as the default too, but it is not a question before a destructive action
    ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02)).

### States

- **CONF-05 · SHOULD.** A question before unsaved changes are lost, where saving is an option, has three answers,
  drawn in this order: Cancel, Save in green and Discard in red (Editora's style classes for the two are `success`
  and `danger`), with Cancel to the left of the actions as in every dialog
  ([WIN-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-11)). A Save that fails leaves the tab open.
  - *Check (code):* the unsaved-changes alert draws Cancel, Save and Discard in that order, on the `ButtonBar`'s one
    fixed order and not the order its `ButtonType`s were added in, and styles Save and Discard; and when Save is
    chosen and the save fails, the close is abandoned, so the tab stays open.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`CloseCoordinator.unsavedAlert`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java), [`MainController.styleUnsavedChangesButtons`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), for
    the three answers and their styles; it still draws them Save, Discard, Cancel.

- **CONF-06 · SHOULD.** A question about ending a running program, which is not the user's data, words the button
  Close, in red like every confirming button ([CONF-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-03)). Cancel is its default button, as in every
  question with a red action ([CONF-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-13)), so dismissing the dialog by any route keeps the program alive.
  - *Check (code):* the close-running-program alert names its action Close. Its red and its default button are
    [CONF-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-03)'s and [CONF-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-13)'s to judge.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (`dialog.closeAnyway`), through [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java).

- **CONF-07 · SHOULD.** Where the action can be taken back, the app asks nothing and offers Undo instead.
  - *Check (by hand):* close a clean tab and reopen it with Reopen Closed Tab; in Mirada, trash an image and undo.
  - *Reference:* Mirada moves an image to the trash at once and offers Undo; Torrenta asks before removing a torrent
    but also keeps the removal on its undo stack for ten minutes ([`UndoStack.KEEP_MS`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/UndoStack.java)); Editora [`ClosedTabs`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ClosedTabs.java).

### Behavior

- **CONF-08 · SHOULD.** Every confirmation question, whether or not it is before a destructive action, comes before
  anything changes, and its action runs only on the action button. For a question before a destructive action both
  are MUSTs already ([CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01), [CONF-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-04)); what this rule adds is every other question, such
  as a warning before something is pasted or run.
  - *Check (code):* every confirmation helper returns true on the action button alone, and its caller acts only on
    true, for the questions that are not before a destructive action as for those that are.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`RemoveConfirm.ask`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java); Editora [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java). For a question
    that is not before a destructive action: Termina's multi-line paste warning, asked through [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java),
    whose `ask` is true for the action button alone, and nux's question before a harmless command
    ([`ui/CommandConfirmation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandConfirmation.java), `confirmed`).

- **CONF-09 · SHOULD.** One gesture asks one question. An action on many things asks once with the count ("Remove these
  3 torrents?", Torrenta's "Apply to many torrents" for a bulk command). Closing every tab asks per unsaved buffer,
  selecting each tab first so the user sees what the question is about, and remembers a Discard answer for exactly
  the state that was shown.
  - *Check (code):* a bulk command builds one question with a plural count; the close-all sweep selects each tab
    before it asks.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`Actions.removeQuestion`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Actions.java); Editora [`CloseCoordinator.confirmSweep`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java).

- **CONF-10 · SHOULD.** A delete that cannot be undone says so; one that leaves the files says that instead.
  - *Check (code):* "This cannot be undone." appears only in the strings of actions that cannot be undone.
  - *Reference:* Editora `dialog.discard.tracked`; Torrenta `actions.removeQuestion.delete`.

- **CONF-11 · SHOULD.** A dangerous alternative (Force with Lease, Delete Anyway) is offered beside the safe one (Pull,
  then Push), in red, and only once the safe one has failed.
  - *Check (code):* the force path is reached only from the safe command's failure result.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`GitBranchCoordinator.offerAfterRejection`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitBranchCoordinator.java) (Force with Lease after a rejected push),
    `confirmForceDelete` (Delete Anyway after `NOT_FULLY_MERGED`).

- **CONF-12 · SHOULD.** A confirmation question can be tested without a screen: its words come from pure code, and a
  capture hook answers the dialog, so a UI test never presses a native button.
  - *Check (code):* the header and the question of every kind are built by pure functions, which need no dialog to
    call, and the confirmation helper has a hook that answers the dialog in a test without showing it. A test that
    asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`RemoveConfirm.header`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java), `question`, `answerForCapture`; [`RemoveConfirmTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirmTest.java).

## Find bar (FIND)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/: The family's find bar: in-scene, incremental, with a count; Enter and Shift+Enter step, Escape gives the keyboard back.

### Rules

- **FIND-01 · MUST.** Wherever there is text to search (an editor, a read-only console, a terminal's scrollback, a
  log shown as text, such as the Debug Log), the app has a find bar that is part of the window, never a popup. A log
  shown as a list of entries is narrowed by a filter instead ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-03)).
  - *Why:* every app has a Debug Log ([DIAG-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-03)), and a log is read by searching it.
  - *Check (code):* each view of searchable text, the Debug Log window among them, has a find bar that is a node in
    its window's scene graph (docked or floating); no `Popup` or `Stage` is created for it. A log drawn as a
    `ListView` or a `TableView` is not such a view. An app with no Debug Log window has no find bar there either,
    so it does not meet this rule: it fails with [DIAG-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-03), which requires the window,
    and the evidence names that rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/FindReplaceBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (the editor's find and replace), with [`ui/ConsoleFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java)
    and [`ui/TerminalFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) as the same shape over a console and a terminal; Termina [`ui/SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java).
    Editora doesn't meet it in every console yet: the build console has the bar
    ([`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)); the Run, External Tools and Debug consoles ([`ui/RunPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RunPanel.java), [`ui/ExternalToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ExternalToolPanel.java),
    [`ui/DebugPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugPanel.java)) are read-only text areas with none.
    The app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) is one bar over a text area, a row in the window: over each document
    ([`ui/DocumentView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentView.java)), over the Output console ([`ui/SamplePanels.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SamplePanels.java)) and over its Debug Log
    ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)). No released app's Debug Log has a find bar yet. Editora's Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) and Torrenta's log
    window ([`ui/LogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/LogWindow.java)) are lists, which [FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-03) covers.

- **FIND-02 · MUST.** A find bar searches as its query is typed and shows a match count.
  - *Check (code):* in each find bar the app has, the query field's text listener runs the search and updates the
    count label. A view where [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-01) asks for a find bar and the app has none fails this rule with
    FIND-01, and so does an app with no find bar and no Debug Log window at all; the evidence names that rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (`debounce`, `find.count`); Termina [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) (`search.count`); the
    app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) (`searching`, `find.count`), in each of its three bars.

- **FIND-03 · MUST.** A list is narrowed by a filter box where text is searched by a find bar. In an app whose main
  content is a list, a filter box over that list takes the place of a find bar there, with the same field and the same
  Escape. The main content is a list when it is a list or a table of items that grows without bound and that the user
  finds things in; Torrenta, with its torrents, is the one such app today. In every app, a log shown as a list of
  entries (a Message Log, an event log, a Debug Log drawn as a list or a table) is covered the same way: a filter
  field over the list narrows it, and it needs no find bar. An event log and a log tab that lists one item's events
  count as logs shown as a list (nux's event log, the Log tab of Torrenta's detail pane); a table of readings or of
  history does not.
  - *Check (code):* in an app whose main content is a list (a list or a table of items that grows without bound and
    that the user finds things in), a filter field sits over that list and filters it as it is typed, and Escape
    pressed in it leads back to the list, as it leads back to the text from a find bar ([FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-07)). Whether
    the first Escape empties the box before the next one leaves it is [FIND-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-14)'s. In every app, each log
    shown as a list or a table of entries has a filter field over it that narrows the entries as it is typed; check
    boxes that narrow a log by level are not one. An event log and a tab that lists one item's events are such logs; a
    table of readings or of history is not judged.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`Omnibox`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Omnibox.java), [`FilterQuery`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/FilterQuery.java), [`MainWindow.onOmniboxKey`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).
    Over a log shown as a list: Editora's [`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java), a filter field over its `ListView`
    (`applyFilter`), and the Message Logs of Torrenta ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)), Mirada ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java))
    and the app template ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java)), each a filter field over a `ListView`. Four logs don't
    meet it yet: Torrenta's [`ui/LogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/LogWindow.java) filters its table by level with three check boxes and has no field
    to type in; the Log tab of Torrenta's detail pane ([`ui/DetailPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DetailPane.java), `buildLog`) lists the selected torrent's
    events with no filter; and Termina's Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)) and nux's event log
    ([`ui/EventsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/EventsWindow.java)) are a list and a table with no filter.

### Behavior

- **FIND-04 · SHOULD.** A command opens each find bar, and run while its bar is already open it finds the next match.
  For the main window's own text (the editor; the terminal in a terminal app) the command is `find.show`, bound to
  `C-s` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl/Cmd+F` in CUA, Sublime, VS Code and IntelliJ, with `F3` as well in CUA and
  Sublime (`Cmd+G` in place of `F3` in CUA on macOS); a terminal binds it to `Ctrl+Shift+F`, `Cmd+F` on macOS, since
  a plain `Ctrl+letter` belongs to the shell. Any other bar (over a log window, or over a console or a terminal
  panel beside the editor) has a command with an id of its own, as the app template's `debugLog.find` is for its
  Debug Log.
  - *Check (code):* each bundled keymap binds that chord to `find.show`; every other find bar is opened by a
    registered command of its own; and each of these commands, run while its bar is shown, steps to the next match.
  - *Reference:* Editora `keymaps/*.json` and [`MainController.findShowOrNext`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which finds the next match while the
    editor's bar is open. The app template's bars all do: `find.show`, bound in each of its keymaps, over the
    documents, `output.find` over the Output console and `debugLog.find` over the Debug Log each open their bar and,
    run while it is open, step to the next match (`openOrNext` in its [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java); [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java);
    [`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java)). No other app's bar does both yet. Termina's find command ([`TerminalWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java), `menu.find`,
    [`MenuAction.appChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuAction.java)) runs [`TerminalView.showSearch`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java), which puts the caret back in the field of a bar that is
    already open. So does Editora's `terminal.find` over its terminal panel ([`TerminalCoordinator.find`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalCoordinator.java)). The
    template's Debug Log window also runs `debugLog.find` ([`MainWindow.findInDebugLog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)) on a fixed `Ctrl/Cmd+F`. Editora's console bar has no command: the find command's chord pressed in the console opens
    it (`ConsoleNav.onCommand` in [`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)), as does a button in the panel's header.

- **FIND-05 · SHOULD.** Typing in a find bar highlights every match, the active one distinctly, and selects and
  scrolls to the match the search starts on. In a document (an editor, a console, a log) that is the first match at
  or after the caret as it was when the bar opened, so refining the query does not run away down the document. In a
  terminal it is the newest match at or above the bottom of the view, since a terminal is searched upward
  ([FIND-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-06)). A view that can draw one selection and nothing else, such as a log in a plain text area,
  shows the active match alone, and the count ([FIND-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-02)) says how many there are.
  - *Check (code):* every match in view is painted while the bar is open, not only the active one, unless the view
    can draw a single selection only. In a document the
    search starts from an anchor saved when the bar opens, not from the current selection; in a terminal, from the
    bottom row of the view.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (`searchAnchor`, `recompute`) over the editor. Over a terminal, Editora's
    [`terminal/TerminalView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/terminal/TerminalView.java) (`startIndex`, `drawSearch`) and Termina's [`TerminalView`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java) (`drawSearchMatches`)
    with [`ScrollbackSearch.initial`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ScrollbackSearch.java). The app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) saves the
    caret as its `anchor` when the bar opens and `refine` searches from it ([`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java),
    `theSearchStartsAtTheCaretAndTheFieldKeepsItsEditingKeys`). Editora's [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) doesn't yet: it searches
    from the current selection (`refine`), not from an anchor saved when the bar opened. Editora's console is a `CodeArea`, which could paint every match, and
    its bar paints the active one only. The template's documents, Output and Debug Log are each a `TextArea`, which
    draws one selection and nothing else, so its bar rightly shows the active match alone.

- **FIND-06 · MUST.** In a find bar, Enter steps to the next match and Shift+Enter to the previous one, wrapping
  around at the ends. In a find bar over a terminal the directions are up and down the scrollback: Enter steps up
  to older output, Shift+Enter down.
  - *Check (code):* in each find bar the app has, the query field's key handler steps to the next match on Enter
    and to the previous one on Shift+Enter (over a terminal, up to older output on Enter and down on Shift+Enter),
    and a step past the last match goes on to the first, and back. A view where [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-01) asks for a
    find bar and the app has none fails this rule with FIND-01, and so does an app with no find bar and no Debug
    Log window at all; the evidence names that rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java), [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java); Termina [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java). Editora's editor bar
    ([`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java)) does not yet: its field steps forward on Enter, and back only with the previous button,
    `find.showBackward` (`C-r`, `Shift+F3`) or `find.previous`. Alt+Enter there turns every match into a caret. The
    app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) steps and wraps the same way (`step`), in each of its three bars.

- **FIND-07 · MUST.** Escape or the close button closes a find bar: its highlights go, a search still pending is
  canceled so nothing moves after the bar is gone, and focus returns to the text the bar searched (the editor, the
  console, the shell or the log). In a find bar over a terminal, the Escape that closes the bar does not reach the
  shell.
  - *Check (code):* in each find bar the app has, the close path, run by Escape in the field and by the close
    button, stops the debounces, cancels the running search, clears the highlights and focuses the text the bar
    searched. In a find bar over a terminal, the field's key handler consumes the Escape it closes the bar on, so
    the terminal never sends that key to the shell. A view where [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-01) asks for a find bar and the
    app has none fails this rule with FIND-01, and so does an app with no find bar and no Debug Log window at all;
    the evidence names that rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FindReplaceBar.hideBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java); the app template's
    [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) (`close`), in each of its three bars. Over a terminal, Termina's [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) (`onKey`) and Editora's
    [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) each close the bar on Escape and consume the key.

- **FIND-08 · SHOULD.** A terminal with a find bar keeps its own key and mouse filters off the bar: they leave
  every event aimed at the bar alone, so what is typed or clicked there never reaches the shell. The Escape that
  closes the bar is [FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-07)'s.
  - *Check (code):* no key or mouse filter of the terminal acts on an event aimed at the find bar: the filters
    return early for an event whose target is inside the bar (Termina's `fromSearchBar`), or the bar is outside the
    node the filters are on, so its events never pass them.
  - *Reference:* Termina [`TerminalView.fromSearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java), which its key, mouse and scroll handlers ask first.

- **FIND-09 · SHOULD.** In a find bar's fields, the keymap's caret and editing chords (`C-a`, `C-e`, `C-k`, `C-y`
  in the Emacs keymap; `Ctrl+V/X/C/Z` in CUA, `Cmd+V/X/C/Z` on macOS) act on the field, not on the document. Find's
  own chords stay global, so next, previous, replace and close work while the field has focus.
  - *Check (code):* in each find bar's fields, the active keymap's caret and editing chords are handled by the
    field and never run the document's commands (Editora installs its shared text-input keymap on the fields),
    and the commands for next, previous, replace and close still run while a find field has the focus.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`TextInputKeymap.installShared`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/TextInputKeymap.java), installed on [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java)'s find and replace fields.
    Editora's [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) and [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) don't yet: neither installs it on its field. Nor does
    Termina's find field: its [`TextInputKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TextInputKeys.java) is installed on the palette only. The app
    template's [`ui/TextInputKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TextInputKeys.java) (`install`) is on the field of each of its find bars, and its key dispatcher leaves a
    text field's editing chords to the field ([`TextInputKeysTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TextInputKeysTest.java); [`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java),
    `theSearchStartsAtTheCaretAndTheFieldKeepsItsEditingKeys`).

- **FIND-10 · SHOULD.** Nothing found is one status-line message ("Not found: x") or the count "No matches". No beep,
  no dialog.
  - *Check (code):* the no-match path sets `find.notFound` or `search.none` and opens nothing.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (`find.notFound`); Termina [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) (`search.none`).

- **FIND-11 · SHOULD.** In a find bar that replaces (an editor's), Replace keeps each match's case when *AB*
  (preserve case) is on.
  - *Check (code):* with preserve case on, the replace path gives each replacement the casing of the match it
    replaces (Editora's `PreserveCase.apply`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`FindReplaceBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBarFxTest.java) (`preserveCaseFollowsEachMatchesCasing`).

- **FIND-12 · SHOULD.** In a find bar that replaces, Replace and Replace All run under a time budget, as the search
  does: a replacement that outruns it stops and says so in the status line (in Editora's words, "Replace stopped:
  the pattern is too slow") instead of hanging the window. How long the budget is is the app's own.
  - *Check (code):* Replace and Replace All match under a time budget, as the search does, and when it runs out
    they stop and say so in the status line (Editora's `find.replaceTimeout`) instead of hanging the window. A test
    that asserts it, with a catastrophic regular expression in Replace All, is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora `find.replaceTimeout`, [`FindReplaceBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBarFxTest.java)
    (`catastrophicRegexInReplaceAllAbortsInsteadOfHanging`).

- **FIND-13 · SHOULD.** In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are), the
  filter box filters the names as plain words are typed, turns `key:value` terms into chips and runs a command after
  `>`. A command puts the focus in the box (`filter` in Torrenta), bound to `Ctrl+K`, `Cmd+K` on macOS, and the box
  draws that command's chord as a key badge.
  - *Check (code):* the box's text listener filters the names by the plain words, turns a `key:value` term into a
    chip and runs the command typed after `>`; a registered command focuses the box, on `Ctrl+K` (`Cmd+K` on
    macOS); and the badge in the box is read from that command's chord, not written out.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`Omnibox`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Omnibox.java), [`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

- **FIND-14 · SHOULD.** In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are),
  Escape in the filter box peels one layer: a box with something in it empties, an empty one gives the list back.
  - *Check (code):* the box's Escape handler clears a non-empty box and otherwise focuses the list.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`MainWindow.onOmniboxKey`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

- **FIND-15 · SHOULD.** In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are), the
  filter box is out of the Tab order, so a fresh launch does not land every keystroke in it, and the window's own
  chords (in Torrenta, undo and the saved views' `Ctrl+Alt+1…9`, `Cmd+Alt+1…9` on macOS) do not fire while a text
  field has focus: `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS) there is the field's own undo.
  - *Check (code):* the box is not focus-traversable, and the window's chord handlers return early when the focus
    owner is a `TextInputControl`.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) window chords.

- **FIND-16 · MUST.** A control of a find bar or of a filter box leaves the Tab order only when the keyboard does
  what it does another way: a registered command does the same, or the bar's own field handles a key that does. So
  the Next, Previous and Close buttons may leave it, since Enter, Shift+Enter and Escape in the field do the same
  ([FIND-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-06), [FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-07)), and so may a field's clear button, since the field's editing keys
  empty it. An option's toggle (match case, whole word, regular expression) stays in it unless a command toggles
  that option. A list app's filter box leaves it ([FIND-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-15)) because its command puts the focus there
  ([FIND-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-13)). A terminal's bar is no exception: Tab belongs to the shell only while the terminal has the
  focus, so a toggle taken out of the Tab order there needs a command like any other.
  - *Why:* [KBD-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/keyboard/#kbd-15) lets a control out of the Tab order only when the keyboard does its work
    another way. A toggle that is out of it with no command can be changed with the mouse alone.
  - *Check (code):* for every control of a find bar or filter box that is set not focus-traversable, a registered
    command does what the control does, or the bar's field handles a key that does: Enter, Shift+Enter or Escape for
    Next, Previous and Close, the editing keys for a clear button. A toggle that is not focus-traversable has a
    command that toggles its option. An app with no find bar and no filter box has no such control: nothing
    breaks this rule and it passes, the missing bar being [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/find-bar/#find-01)'s finding.
  - *Reference:* Editora's [`FindReplaceBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) keeps every button and option box in the Tab order, all but the
    clear button inside each field. Its [`ConsoleFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) and [`TerminalFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) take Previous, Next and Close
    out of it, which Shift+Enter, Enter and Escape in the field do, and leave the field and the match-case toggle
    in. The app template's [`FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) takes the same three out: Previous and Next run its bar's step
    commands (`find.previous` and `find.next` over a document, `output.findPrevious` and `output.findNext`,
    `debugLog.findPrevious` and `debugLog.findNext`), Close is the field's Escape, and the Match Case box stays in.
    Torrenta's filter box is out of it and reached by its `filter` command
    ([`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)). In Mirada's [`BookmarksWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/BookmarksWindow.java) the three kind toggles are out of it and
    have a command each (`bookmarks.listAll`, `bookmarks.listBookmarked`, `bookmarks.listNotes`). Termina's
    [`SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) leaves only its field in the Tab order: the two arrows and Close are the field's Enter,
    Shift+Enter and Escape, and the arrows its `findNext` and `findPrevious` commands too, but its regex toggle
    doesn't meet the rule yet: it is out of the Tab order and no command toggles it.

## Message Log (MLOG)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/message-log/: The family's Message Log: the session's status-bar messages, newest first, opened from the status bar.

### Spec

- **MLOG-08 · SHOULD.** The Message Log is a card in the window's in-scene overlay host, anchored just above the status
  bar's echo area, never a separate window: 773 px wide, its list 336 px high, at the default zoom, holding the
  newest 200 messages of the session (the cap [DIAG-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/diagnostics/#diag-01) asks for).
  - *Why:* the log answers "what just happened?" next to the line that said it; a separate window, or another size
    and cap, makes the same log look and behave differently from app to app.
  - *Check (code):* the log adds its node to the overlay host (no `Stage`), with width 773, list height 336 and a
    cap of 200.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java) (`WIDTH`, `LIST_HEIGHT`) and
    [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) (`MAX_ENTRIES`); the app template's [`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java).
    Torrenta's card is 640 × 300, and Termina's log is a separate window that keeps 500 messages.

### Behavior

- **MLOG-02 · SHOULD.** A click on the status bar's unread-error count opens the Message Log, as a click on the
  echo area does ([WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/window-shell/#win-01)), and so does the `view.messageLog` command.
  - *Check (code):* the unread-error count runs `view.messageLog` on a click, and the command is registered.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`StatusBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java) (`echo`, `unreadErrors`), [`StatusBar.showMessageLog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java).

- **MLOG-03 · SHOULD.** The active keymap's cancel chord or a click outside closes the Message Log, as Esc does.
  - *Check (code):* the Message Log closes on the chord the active keymap binds to its cancel command, not on a fixed
    `Ctrl+G`, and a press outside the log closes it: on the backdrop, where the log is the in-scene card
    [MLOG-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/message-log/#mlog-08) asks for. In an app with one key table (a terminal app's keymap, or the built-in table of
    an app that ships no keymap files), the chord is the one that table binds to a cancel command; where it binds
    none, Esc and the press outside are all there is to test.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java), which hides the card on a press on its backdrop and on [`PickerKeys.isCancel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java): Esc,
    or the chord the keymap binds to `edit.cancel` (Editora's id; `C-g` in its Emacs keymap). Its [`MessageLogPopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)
    also closes on `Ctrl+G` whatever the keymap, though the CUA keymap binds `C-g` to `nav.goToLine`; its handler
    reads `Alt+G` too, which the Emacs keymap's `M-g` prefix takes first. The app template's Message Log
    ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java)) is shown through its [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java), which closes it the same way, on the
    keymap's `edit.cancel` chord (`cancelOn`). Elsewhere the chord is fixed: `Ctrl+G` in Termina
    ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)) and Mirada ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java)). Torrenta's
    ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) closes on Esc and on a press on its backdrop: Torrenta has no keymap and no cancel
    command, so the chord asks nothing more of it.

- **MLOG-04 · SHOULD.** The Message Log copies the selected entries on the platform's copy chord, `Ctrl+C`
  (`Cmd+C` on macOS), in every keymap, and on the active keymap's copy chord too.
  - *Check (code):* the Message Log's key handling copies the selected entries on C with the platform's shortcut
    modifier down (`isShortcutDown`), whatever the active keymap binds to copy, and also on the chord the active
    keymap binds to its copy command (`M-w` in an Emacs keymap), read from the keymap and not written into the
    handler.
  - *Reference:* for the platform's chord, Editora [`MessageLogPopup.copySelection`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java), on a fixed shortcut-down C, and
    the Message Logs of Torrenta ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)), Termina ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)), Mirada
    ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java)) and the app template ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java)), each the same way. For the
    keymap's chord, no app yet: none of the five reads the keymap's copy binding in its log, and Editora's Emacs
    keymap binds copy to `M-w`, which its log does not read. The app template meets the rule all the same: none of its
    keymaps binds a copy command, so there is no second chord to read, and its key dispatcher steps aside while the
    log, an overlay, is open (`KeyDispatcher`), so `Ctrl+C` reaches it under the Emacs keymap's `C-c` prefix too. Editora doesn't hold the first half under that keymap
    on Windows and Linux either: the keymap starts longer chords with `C-c`, a prefix the window's key dispatcher
    ([`command/KeyDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeyDispatcher.java)) consumes in a scene filter, ahead of the log's own.

- **MLOG-05 · SHOULD.** A message's severity comes from its key: a `status.*` key whose last segment contains `fail`
  or `error` is an error, one containing `cannot` or `invalid` a warning. Name new keys accordingly, or post the
  message as an error directly (Editora's status bar has an error channel for that).
  - *Check (code):* one function gives a message's severity from its key by those rules (Editora's
    `StatusSeverity.ofKey`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
