  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/StatusSeverity.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusSeverity.java) (`ofKey`), [`StatusSeverityTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StatusSeverityTest.java).

- **MLOG-06 · SHOULD.** Opening the Message Log, or clearing it, resets the unread-error count.
  - *Check (code):* opening the Message Log marks it read, and clearing it zeroes the count (Editora's `markRead`
    and `clear`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MessageLog.markRead`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java), [`MessageLog.clear`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java), [`StatusBar.showMessageLog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java).

- **MLOG-07 · SHOULD.** An unread error is never evicted from the Message Log silently: the unread-error count
  keeps it even when the entry drops off the end.
  - *Check (code):* the Message Log counts unread errors apart from the entries it holds, so dropping an unread
    error at the cap leaves the count as it was. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`MessageLogSeverityTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogSeverityTest.java) (`anEvictedErrorStillCounts`).

## Settings Sync (SYNC)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/settings-sync/: The family's Sync settings page: keep user data the same on every computer through a Git repository the user owns.

### Rules

- **SYNC-01 · SHOULD.** An app with user data worth carrying between computers offers Settings Sync, on a page of its
  own in the Settings window that the Settings search finds by "sync". Such data is what a person builds up in the
  app by hand and would set up again on another computer: snippets, templates, shortcuts, profiles, presets,
  bookmarks, saved views.
  - *Check (by hand):* open Settings, search "sync", and land on the Sync page. An app that keeps none of the data
    the statement lists is outside the rule.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ui/SettingsSync.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSync.java) (the service) and [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java), built by
    [`SettingsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java) (`Category.SYNC`). Termina, Torrenta and the app template have Settings Sync
    too. Modula, Mirada and nux keep such data (presets, bookmarks, profiles) and have no Settings Sync yet.

- **SYNC-02 · SHOULD.** In an app with Settings Sync ([SYNC-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/settings-sync/#sync-01)), the store is a Git repository the user
  owns, reached through their own Git credentials (a credential helper or an SSH key), with no server or account of
  ours. Refusing a URL with a password or token in it is [SET-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/settings/#set-15).
  - *Check (code):* the app's sync code runs `git` against the URL the user gave, with their own Git credentials,
    and talks to no server or account of the app's own.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`sync/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync) package ([`SyncEngine`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncEngine.java), [`SyncMerge`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncMerge.java), [`SyncAccount`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncAccount.java)), [`SyncEngine.hasCredentials`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncEngine.java);
    Termina carries the same package, Torrenta its own [`sync/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/tree/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync) with [`SyncEngine`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncEngine.java) and [`SyncAccount`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncAccount.java); the page's
    [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/templates/settings-sync/#spec).

## Packaging, signing and release (REL)

https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/: jpackage, JReleaser, the five-target matrix, macOS/Linux/Windows signing and CI.

### Targets

- **REL-01 · MUST.** jpackage builds the installers for five targets, Linux x64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64,
  and Windows x64, each on its own runner, through a Maven profile that packages the app (`dist` in Editora).
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow's build matrix has a leg for each of the five targets (`linux-x64`,
    `linux-arm64`, `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64` and `windows-x64` in Editora), each on a runner of that OS and
    architecture, and each leg builds with a profile of `pom.xml` that runs jpackage, whatever the profile is
    called. The runner images under [Targets](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#targets) are Editora's:
    another image of the same OS and architecture meets it (Termina, Torrenta, Mirada, Modula and nux build macOS
    arm64 on `macos-latest`).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) (the `build` job), [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml) (`dist`). The template
    and the five other apps name their profile `dist` too.

- **REL-02 · SHOULD.** Downloads are named `<App>-<version>-<target>.<ext>`.
  - *Check (code):* the release-asset check builds the expected names this way.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`scripts/release/CheckRelease.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/release/CheckRelease.java) (`expectedAssets`).

- **REL-03 · MUST.** **JReleaser** (`jreleaser.yml`) builds nothing: it creates the GitHub release, attaches every
  file and `checksums_sha256.txt`, and runs the packagers of [REL-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-12) and [REL-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-13) where the app
  has them.
  - *Check (code):* `jreleaser.yml` has no step that compiles or packages the app: it attaches the build matrix's
    files and the checksums file, and its `brew` and `winget` packagers, where the app has them, take those same
    files. The job that runs it needs the build jobs.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/jreleaser.yml), the `release` job in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml).

- **REL-04 · SHOULD.** The release notes are the version's section of `CHANGELOG.md`.
  - *Check (code):* the release job gives that section to the step that publishes (JReleaser, by
    [REL-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-03)) as the release's notes.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`scripts/release/ReleaseNotes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/scripts/release/ReleaseNotes.java). Editora's release notes are still its commit list.

- **REL-05 · MUST.** The Maven version is the single source of truth: a tag `vX.Y.Z` releases the version in
  `pom.xml`.
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow fails when the tag and the pom version differ.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Check the tag against the pom version" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml).

- **REL-06 · SHOULD.** The default branch carries a `-SNAPSHOT` version, and a post-release job opens the pull
  request that bumps it to the next snapshot.
  - *Check (code):* the pom's version on the default branch ends in `-SNAPSHOT`, and `release.yml` has the bump job.
  - *Reference:* Editora's `bump` job in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml).

- **REL-07 · SHOULD.** A **release-asset check** fails the run before publishing when an expected file is missing.
  - *Why:* GitHub releases are immutable.
  - *Check (code):* a step before the one that publishes compares the gathered files with the expected list.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Verify the expected release assets" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml).

- **REL-08 · SHOULD.** On Linux, a `.desktop` file's `StartupWMClass` is the JavaFX app class.
  - *Why:* the running window then belongs to the menu entry and shows its icon.
  - *Check (code):* `packaging/linux/<App>.desktop` sets `StartupWMClass` to the fully qualified name of the app's
    own class that extends `Application`: `com.editora.App` in Editora, `com.modula.ModulaApp` in Modula.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`packaging/linux/Editora.desktop`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/packaging/linux/Editora.desktop), Torrenta [`packaging/linux/Torrenta.desktop`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/packaging/linux/Torrenta.desktop),
    Modula [`packaging/linux/Modula.desktop`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/packaging/linux/Modula.desktop). The template, Termina, Mirada and nux set theirs the same way.

- **REL-09 · SHOULD.** On Linux, AppStream metainfo has the id `io.github.adriandeleon.<App>`.
  - *Check (code):* `packaging/linux/io.github.adriandeleon.<App>.metainfo.xml` carries that `<id>`.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta [`packaging/linux/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/tree/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/packaging/linux). Editora's metainfo id (`com.editora.Editora`) predates the rule.

- **REL-10 · SHOULD.** Packaging trains an **AOT cache** (JDK 25 Leyden) to cut start-up time; Linux legs run the
  training under `xvfb`.
  - *Check (code):* the packaging build (Editora's `dist` profile) runs a training launch with
    `-XX:AOTCacheOutput`, and the Linux release legs install `xvfb`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`scripts/aot_build.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/aot_build.java); Termina's and Mirada's [`scripts/aot-train.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/aot-train.sh).

### Install methods

- **REL-11 · MUST.** The GitHub release offers every download of every target: the `.dmg`, `.msi`, `.deb`,
  `.rpm`, `.AppImage` and `.tar.gz`, with checksums. Which target gets which type is under [Targets](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#targets).
  - *Check (code):* the files the release attaches include each of these types and a checksums file: the files
    `jreleaser.yml` lists or, in a workflow that publishes another way, the ones its publishing step uploads. That
    JReleaser is what publishes is [REL-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-03).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/jreleaser.yml).

- **REL-12 · SHOULD.** On macOS (Apple Silicon) the app installs with
  `brew install --cask adriandeleon/tap/<app>`: JReleaser's `brew` packager writes the cask to
  [`adriandeleon/homebrew-tap`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/homebrew-tap). A cask takes exactly one artifact,
  so it serves Apple Silicon, and Intel Macs use the `macos-x64` DMG.
  - *Why:* the official homebrew-cask repository has notability rules a new project does not meet, so the family
    shares one personal tap.
  - *Check (code):* `jreleaser.yml` has a `brew` packager for that tap; `jreleaser package --basedir .` writes the
    cask locally, to check it without releasing.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta and Termina `jreleaser.yml`; Editora has no packager yet.

- **REL-13 · SHOULD.** On Windows x64 the app installs with `winget install AdrianDeLeon.<App>`: JReleaser's
  `winget` packager opens a pull request on [`microsoft/winget-pkgs`](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs)
  from the `adriandeleon` fork. The package identifier is `AdrianDeLeon.<App>`, the moniker the app's lower-case
  name.
  - *Check (code):* `jreleaser.yml` has a `winget` packager with that identifier; `jreleaser package --basedir .`
    writes the manifests locally.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta and Termina `jreleaser.yml`; Editora has no packager yet.

- **REL-14 · SHOULD.** The Homebrew and winget packagers ([REL-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-12), [REL-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-13)) read one
  repository secret, a classic personal access token with `repo` scope (`PACKAGES_TOKEN` in Torrenta, Termina and
  the app template). Without it JReleaser skips both packagers, and the GitHub release still publishes.
  - *Why:* the workflow's own token cannot write to the tap or open a pull request on the fork.
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow passes a secret of the repository to JReleaser as the two packagers'
    token, whatever the secret is called, and leaves both packagers out when it is empty.
  - *Reference:* the publishing jobs of Torrenta's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml), Termina's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/release.yml) and the app
    template's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml), which read `PACKAGES_TOKEN` and exclude the packagers without it.

### Signing

- **REL-15 · MUST.** The macOS `.dmg` is signed with the Developer ID Application certificate (team 8JKSF797L8),
  with the hardened runtime and per-app entitlements, notarized with `notarytool`, stapled and checked with
  `spctl`; then the notarized app is launched once.
  - *Check (code):* `release.yml`, or a script it runs, imports `MACOS_CERT_P12` and `MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD`,
    notarizes with `APPLE_API_KEY_P8`, `APPLE_API_KEY_ID` and `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, staples, runs `spctl` and
    launches the app.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Import signing certificate (macOS)" and "Notarize DMG (macOS)" steps in
    [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml), [`packaging/macos/Editora.entitlements`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/packaging/macos/Editora.entitlements). All six apps sign, notarize,
    staple and run `spctl`; Editora, Termina, Mirada, Modula and nux then launch the notarized app. Torrenta does not
    yet: its "Smoke-test the packaged app" step launches the signed app before it is notarized, and its "Notarize the
    dmg (macOS)" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml) ends at `spctl`. Mirada's steps are in [`scripts/sign-mac.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/sign-mac.sh) and
    [`scripts/notarize-mac.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/notarize-mac.sh).

- **REL-16 · MUST.** Linux downloads are signed with the one shared OpenPGP release key ("Adrian De Leon (release
  signing)") in a job of their own, apart from the build legs (`sign-linux` in Editora): `rpmsign` for the `.rpm`, a
  debsigs origin signature for the `.deb`, and an armored `.asc` beside every file. The public key is committed as
  `packaging/linux/signing-key.asc` and attached to each release.
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow has a job apart from the build legs, whatever it is called, that reads
    the release key and its passphrase from the repository's secrets (`LINUX_GPG_KEY` and `LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE` in
    Editora), signs each `.rpm` and `.deb` and writes an `.asc` beside every Linux file; and
    `packaging/linux/signing-key.asc` exists, and the release attaches that public key (as
    `editora-signing-key.asc` in Editora).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`scripts/release/sign-linux-packages.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/release/sign-linux-packages.sh), [`scripts/release/check-linux-signatures.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/release/check-linux-signatures.sh).
    Done in Editora, the app template, Torrenta, Termina, Mirada and Modula, all with the same key; nux has no `sign-linux` job and no
    committed key yet.

- **REL-17 · SHOULD.** The Windows `.msi` is signed with Authenticode, once the certificate is chosen.
  - *Check (code):* the Windows leg signs the `.msi` before it is uploaded.
  - *Reference:* no app signs one yet. The app template's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml) has the step: once the repository
    holds a certificate (`WINDOWS_CERT_PFX`), it signs each `.msi` with `signtool` before the upload. **Open decision**: SignPath Foundation (free for OSS), a Certum Open Source
    certificate, or Azure Trusted Signing. Until then MSIs are unsigned and SmartScreen warns.

- **REL-18 · MUST.** Every download has a GitHub **build provenance attestation**
  (`actions/attest-build-provenance`), which `gh attestation verify` checks.
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow has an `actions/attest-build-provenance` step whose subjects cover every
    file the release attaches. The test that keeps the two lists the same is [QUAL-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/quality/#qual-15)'s.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Attest build provenance" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml), [`ReleaseSupplyChainTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/packaging/ReleaseSupplyChainTest.java). Done in
    Editora, the app template, Termina and Mirada.

### CI/CD (GitHub Actions)

- **REL-19 · MUST.** The CI workflow (`ci.yml` in Editora) runs on every push to the default branch and every pull
  request, with two checks: the format check of [PLAT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-10) (`spotless:check`; the job Editora
  names **Format**) and the build with its tests (`./mvnw verify`, coverage gate included; Editora's **Build &
  Test**), on the JDK [PLAT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-01) names. Both are required status checks for the default branch.
  - *Check (code):* the CI workflow triggers on `push` to the default branch and on `pull_request`. One of its jobs
    is the Format job of [PLAT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-10), which runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests,
    and its jobs between them run the whole suite and `verify` with the coverage gate: one
    job that runs `./mvnw verify`, or, as in Editora, jobs that run `test` in shards and one that runs `verify` over
    their results. What the jobs are called is the app's own. A workflow that lacks a trigger or one of the two
    checks fails the rule. That the default branch requires both is a repository setting, which no file shows. An audit
    run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `master` (its `format` job, its four `tests` shards and its `build` job, which
    runs `verify` over the shards' results); the app template's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and Termina's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `master`, and
    Mirada's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `main`, each with a job for `spotless:check` and one for `verify`. Torrenta
    ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml)) and nux ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) don't yet: none has a format check
    of its own. Torrenta's and Modula's one test job runs `./mvnw verify`, which their poms bind `spotless:check` to,
    so a single status stands for both checks; nux's pom has no Spotless, and its job runs `./mvnw test`, not `verify`.
    Modula's and nux's builds have no coverage gate either ([PLAT-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-12)). No file of any of them
    shows the required checks.

- **REL-20 · MUST.** The tests run on all three OSes: the pure suite (no JavaFX toolkit) on Linux, macOS and
  Windows, and the FX suite on Linux and at least one more. They run there every day or on every pull request. How
  the runs are split is the app's own: one workflow that runs everything on every pull request meets this, and so
  does a quick workflow for pull requests with a fuller one on a schedule. A release waits for these runs on its own
  commit, on all three OSes: that it waits at all is [REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-30).
  - *Why:* path separators, line endings, case-insensitive file systems and process spawning fail on one OS only, and
    the pure suite is where they show; the FX suite catches layout and focus differences. The FX suite is the slow
    one (three shards on macOS in Editora), so it is asked on two OSes and not three: the third is covered by the
    pure suite alone.
  - *Check (code):* taken together, the workflows' test jobs run the pure suite on `ubuntu-*`, `macos-*` and
    `windows-*` runners and the FX suite on `ubuntu-*` and one more, under a `schedule` or a `pull_request` trigger
    that needs no label; and the tests a release waits for ([REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-30)) ran on those runners, in the release
    workflow itself or in the run it reads.
  - *Reference:* Editora splits them: [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the whole suite on Linux on every pull request, and
    [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) the pure suite on Windows and macOS and the FX suite on macOS, in three shards, daily, on
    a pull request labeled `full-ci` and before every release: the "Check that the Full tests passed on this
    commit" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml). It lists flaky tests in the job summary
    ([`scripts/ci/ReportFlakes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/ci/ReportFlakes.java)). The app template splits them the same way, and its release calls
    [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) itself. Termina ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Torrenta ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Mirada
    ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml)) and nux ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) run the
    whole suite on the three OSes on every pull request.

- **REL-21 · MUST.** The release workflow (`release.yml` in Editora) runs on a version tag (`v*` meets it; the
  version-shaped `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*` is the better pattern, since a tag like `vendor-import` doesn't match
  it), with `workflow_dispatch` as a dry run that builds and signs and publishes nothing. The tag matching the pom
  is [REL-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-05), the tests it waits for [REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-30), the release-asset check [REL-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-07), and the
  bump to the next snapshot [REL-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/release/#rel-06).
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow triggers on a tag pattern that starts with `v` and on
    `workflow_dispatch`. A dispatched run goes through the build and signing jobs and publishes nothing: the step
    that publishes runs in a mode that publishes nothing (JReleaser's `--dry-run`), or the job that publishes runs
    only for a tag (an `if:` on the ref).
  - *Reference:* Editora [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml), whose "JReleaser" step takes `release --dry-run` on a dispatch; the
    template, Termina, Torrenta and Mirada pass JReleaser `--dry-run` the same way. Modula's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) and nux's
    [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml), which have no JReleaser, run their publishing job only for a tag
    (`if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/…')`).

- **REL-30 · MUST.** A release is cut only from a commit whose tests passed: the release workflow runs the suite
  before it builds the installers, or a preflight job reads CI's result for the tagged commit and stops when it is
  not green.
  - *Why:* the build legs often skip the tests (`-DskipTests`), and a tag can be pushed on any commit, so without
    this a release can be cut from code whose checks failed or never ran.
  - *Check (code):* in the release workflow, every job that publishes needs, directly or through the jobs between, a
    job that settles the tests on the tagged commit: it runs them (a Maven run that reaches the `test` phase,
    `./mvnw test`, `package`, `verify` or `install`, with no `-DskipTests` and no `-Dmaven.test.skip`, or a call to
    the full-tests workflow), or it reads the conclusion of the CI run on `GITHUB_SHA` and fails on anything but
    success.
  - *Reference:* both ways are in use, and all seven release workflows meet it. A preflight that reads CI: Editora's
    "Check that CI passed on this commit" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) ([`scripts/release/CheckRelease.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/release/CheckRelease.java) `ci`, which waits up to 30
    minutes for the required checks; its build legs run `-DskipTests`), and Torrenta's "Require CI on this commit"
    step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml), which reads the newest `ci.yml` run on the commit and starts one when there is none. The
    suite in the release: the template's `full-tests` job in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml) calls `full-tests.yml` before `build`;
    the "Build, test and package" step of Termina's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/release.yml) and Mirada's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs `./mvnw … verify` on
    every build leg; Modula's "Build the installer" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs `package` with the tests; nux's build
    legs run a "Test" step (`./mvnw test`) before they package, in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml). In each of the five the job that
    publishes needs the build legs, directly or through the signing and asset-check jobs. Mirada's [`codecs.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/codecs.yml) also creates a GitHub release, of the codec libraries its build
    downloads by checksum: that is a dependency, not a release of the app, and the app's own release runs the suite
    with them.

- **REL-22 · MUST.** Every workflow pins each third-party action to a commit SHA, with its version in a comment
  (`actions/setup-java@b843ebf… # v6.1.0`).
  - *Check (code):* every `uses:` in `.github/workflows/`, and in a composite action under `.github/actions/` where
    the repository has one, ends in a 40-character SHA and a comment naming its version (`# v6.1.0`, `# 2.5.0`, `# v2`), never a
    branch such as `# main`. The `v2` in Editora's and Torrenta's `jreleaser/release-action … # v2` names that
    action's `v2` line, whose head the SHA is; the template, Termina and Mirada pin its 2.5.0 release.
  - *Command:* `[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d .github/workflows ] || { echo 'no .github/workflows'; exit 1; }; ! grep -rhE '^[[:space:]]*-?[[:space:]]*uses:' .github/workflows .github/actions 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'uses:[[:space:]]*\./' | grep -vE '@[0-9a-f]{40}[[:space:]]+#[[:space:]]*v?[0-9]'`
  - *Reference:* Editora [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows).

- **REL-23 · MUST.** Dependabot updates `github-actions` and `maven` weekly.
  - *Check (code):* `.github/dependabot.yml` lists both ecosystems with `interval: weekly`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`.github/dependabot.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/dependabot.yml).

- **REL-24 · MUST.** Every workflow starts from `permissions: contents: read`, or from less; only a job that needs
  write access asks for it, in its own block.
  - *Check (code):* each workflow has a top-level `permissions` that grants no write: `contents: read`, or less
    (`permissions: {}`); and every `write` sits in a job's own `permissions`.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml): `release` (publish), `bump` (the pull request) and `preflight` (start a
    Full tests run). Modula's [`notify-catalog.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/notify-catalog.yml) starts from `permissions: {}`.

- **REL-25 · SHOULD.** Every `actions/setup-java` step caches Maven's repository (`cache: maven`). The JDK it sets
  up is [PLAT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.1.0/platform/#plat-01)'s.
  - *Check (code):* each `setup-java` step has `cache: maven`.
  - *Reference:* Mirada ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula, nux and the app template ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml),
    [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml)), on every step. Editora ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml),
    [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml)), Termina and Torrenta each have a `setup-java` step without it. Editora
    sets up Temurin for its tests and Liberica for the release build, for linux-aarch64 coverage.

- **REL-26 · MUST.** Every job that runs steps has `timeout-minutes`. A job that calls a reusable workflow
  (`uses:` in place of `steps:`) takes no `timeout-minutes`: GitHub does not accept the key there, and the called
  workflow's own jobs carry theirs.
  - *Check (code):* in every workflow, every job with `steps:` sets `timeout-minutes` on the job itself; a timeout
    on one of its steps does not stand for it. A job with `uses:` and no `steps:` is not judged.
  - *Reference:* every job of Editora's five workflows ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) and
    the rest), of the template's three, Termina's two and Mirada's five sets one; the template's `full-tests` job
    in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml), which calls `full-tests.yml`, carries none, as the rule says, and nor does the `winget` job of
    Mirada's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/release.yml), which calls `winget.yml`. Torrenta, Modula and nux don't
    yet: the two jobs of Torrenta's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and the one of its [`engine-soak.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/engine-soak.yml) set none (its `release.yml`
    does); no job in Modula's three workflows ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml), [`notify-catalog.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/notify-catalog.yml)) or in
    nux's two ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml)) sets one: each app has it on one step only, the one that notarizes.

- **REL-31 · MUST.** Every workflow that runs on pull requests has a `concurrency` group that cancels a superseded
  pull-request run, and never a run on the default branch.
  - *Check (code):* every workflow with a `pull_request` trigger has a `concurrency` block whose `group` is shared
    by the runs of one pull request and by no run on the default branch (keyed by `github.ref`, or by the pull
    request's number), and whose `cancel-in-progress` is true for a pull-request run: true, or an expression that
    is true there. And in that workflow `cancel-in-progress` is never true for a run on the default branch,
    whatever starts it (a push, a schedule, or a run started by hand, which `workflow_dispatch` allows on any
    branch): it is an expression that is false there, and it may be plain true only in a workflow that nothing
    can start on the default branch. A workflow with no `pull_request` trigger is not judged.
  - *Reference:* Editora [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) (`cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`,
    in a group keyed by the pull request's number). The template's
    ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml)), Termina's ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) and Mirada's ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) pull-request workflows
    use the same expression, Termina's and Mirada's in a group keyed by `github.ref`. Editora's third pull-request
    workflow, [`terminal-image.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/terminal-image.yml), doesn't yet: its `cancel-in-progress` is plain true, and beside pull requests and
    pushes to `probe/**` it can be started by hand, so a second run started on `master` cancels the first.
    Torrenta, Modula and nux don't either: Modula's [`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml) and nux's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml) run on
    pull requests with no `concurrency` block, so they cancel nothing, and Torrenta's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml) sets
    `cancel-in-progress: true` for its pushes to `master` as well.

- **REL-27 · MUST.** A CI run leaves its results where they can be read without running it again: it uploads the
  surefire reports even when tests fail, uploads the JaCoCo report, and writes the coverage totals to the job
  summary.
  - *Check (code):* the step that uploads the surefire reports runs under `if: always()`, a step uploads the
    JaCoCo report, and a step appends the coverage totals to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Upload test reports and coverage data" and "Summarise coverage" steps in [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

- **REL-28 · MUST.** Signing skips cleanly when the secrets are absent (forks, dry runs), so they still build; a tag
  without them fails.
  - *Check (code):* each signing step checks its secrets first, skips without them, and fails on a tag push.
  - *Reference:* Editora's "Import signing certificate (macOS)" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) checks `MACOS_CERT_P12`
    first.

- **REL-29 · MUST.** The packaged app is launched once on each OS before a release (a smoke test).
  - *Check (code):* the release workflow runs the packaged launcher on each OS (a Linux, a macOS and a Windows leg)
    before the step that publishes.
  - *Reference:* Torrenta's "Smoke-test the packaged app" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs the launcher in the image of each
    of its three targets, one per OS. Editora runs only the notarized macOS app (`--version`, `--check-terminal`).
